docs.title: Research log — July 2026 carry round
docs.text: Method: strategy-research-methodology.md. Data: binance/ (17 spot large-caps, 30-min Go metrics, 2024-12-01..2026-05-29). Split: TRAIN 2024-12..2025-10, VALIDATION 2025-11..2026-05 (7 months, held out). Costs: fee 1.6 bps + half quoted spread + 1 bps slippage, next-bar VWAP fills.

docs.title: What was searched
docs.text: ~2,500 candidates: 41 base signals x spans (2-40d) x bands (0/0.3/0.6) x weighting (proportional / inverse-vol) x universe (all / 10 tightest-spread), plus ensembles, time-scale splits, seasonality, cluster relative value. Multiple-testing note: at this count the best pure-noise candidate on 11 months of daily PnL sits near Sharpe ~1.6-1.8; the train gate stayed at 2.0 and family grid-stability (median across the whole grid) was required on top, precisely because of this.

docs.title: What survived, what died
docs.text:
• Liquidity/carry complex — survived. Amihud, depth, spread, vol, beta rank-carries and their blends: train Sharpe 1.9-3.1 across the whole parameter grid (not a lucky cell), both train halves positive, validation positive (family medians +0.5..+1.3). Everything that passed the gates belongs to this one complex (pairwise daily-PnL corr 0.4-0.98).
  • Book pressure — only inside the blend. Standalone book-imbalance signals peaked at train ~1.9 and validated at ~0; blended with carry they add on both windows.
  • Died OOS: distance-from-high (val -0.9), levels-below/above-5% (val -1.4), book-state time-splits, flow imbalances, seasonality — grid-unstable or sign-flipped on validation. Not shipped.
  • Momentum regime-flipped: weak on train (median 0.5), strong on validation (median 2.2-2.3). Fails the train gate, so not shipped — flagged as the first candidate for the next round precisely because it diversifies carry.

docs.title: Round 3 — the <=10-day lookback constraint
docs.text: After round 2 a hard product constraint landed: no strategy may look back more than 10 days (every rolling window / EMA span parameter <= 10d). The full search was re-run under the cap (2,460 candidates): same verdict — only the carry/book complex passes the gates with grid-stable families. The 90d distance-from-high died; its 10d analog (proximity to the 10-day high) turned out to be the best out-of-sample sleeve of all.

docs.title: Shipped strategies (alpha_engine/strategies/carry.py)
docs.text:
All windows and spans <= 10 days.

name recipe train Sharpe val Sharpe turnover carry_liquidity amihud+depth+spread carry, liq-10, 10d 2.06 0.90 0.22 carry_core 5-way carry (vol/beta/spread/depth/amihud), 10d, band .6 2.64 0.02 0.18 carry_quality 10d-high proximity+vol+amihud, inv-vol, 3d, band .6 2.05 2.44 0.31 carry_book_blend 5-carry + 5-book blend, inv-vol, liq-10, 5d, band .6 2.51 0.52 0.33

Weight classes reproduce the research weights bit-for-bit (verified by direct frame diff before shipping). All four clear the individual train-Sharpe >= 2 gate; pairwise train correlations are 0.5-0.85 — they are components of ONE complex, decomposed so the Markowitz layer can weight them, not four independent alphas.

docs.title: Portfolio (production run: strategies + Markowitz)
docs.text:
python tools/backtest.py --metrics-roots binance/data-historical-vision binance/datametrics-1m --since 2024-12-01 --until 2026-05-29 --alphas carry_liquidity carry_core carry_quality carry_book_blend --execution vwap --max-w 0.125 --slippage-bps 1.0

Full period (18 months, includes the held-out window), net of costs, at gross exposure 1.0: Sharpe 1.92, PnL +56% (~37%/yr), max DD -11.3%, turnover 0.29/day. Research split of the equal-weight blend: train Sharpe 2.76 (+37%/yr), validation Sharpe 0.87 (+13%/yr). The constrained (<=10d) set beats the unconstrained round-2 set out-of-sample — shorter memory adapts faster to the regime change in the validation window.

docs.title: Honest read & the 100%/yr target
docs.text:
The train numbers meet the brief; the validation window does not. The carry complex is real (it survives every robustness cut), but its edge in Nov-2025..May-2026 was roughly a third of the train-period edge — regime dependence, not noise. Realistic forward expectation is Sharpe ~1-1.5 at ~15-25%/yr on gross 1.0.

Leverage math at the full-period numbers: 100%/yr needs ~2.7x leverage -> levered max DD ~-30% and a Sharpe still ~1.9. That is survivable but brutal; at the validation-period edge it would be ~10x and ruinous. The honest lever for 100%/yr is not leverage on this portfolio — it is breadth: 17 names is tiny for a cross-sectional book (Sharpe scales ~sqrt(breadth) at fixed signal quality), and the parser already collects the top-100 universe going forward. Second lever: a momentum sleeve (validated-regime diversifier) once it can clear the gate on a longer train window.

docs.title: Validation-integrity disclosure
docs.text: The holdout was scored once per sweep round and family-level medians were inspected while deciding what families to ship (2 looks total before the final scoring). The shipped set was still ranked and parameterised on train only, but the validation Sharpe reported here is mildly optimistic as an unbiased estimate. Next data extension shifts the split forward and re-tests untouched months.

docs.title: Round 4 — brother's good_alphas ideas + the val>=1.5 rule
docs.text:
The origin/good_alphas branch carries a 9-strategy book (accepted_alphas.py). Five of them (smart_money_flow, oi_shock_rev, crowd_contra, oi_churn_regime, smart_dumb_acct) need USD-M futures panels (open interest, long/short ratios) that the local binance/ spot metrics do NOT contain — untestable and untradable here until that data lands. The four testable ones, on our split and costs:

idea (his params) train val note pressure_flow_ens @20d 0.58 2.60 val-only; 20d span breaks the 10d rule small_large_flow_div @20d 0.98 -1.31 he marked it DECAYED himself book_pressure_mom @3d 1.13 0.74 below both gates us_session_mom @3d -1.03 -0.03 negative on train

Swept over our <=10d grid none of them clears val>=1.5 (best: small_large_flow_div@3d_b100, train 2.35 / val 1.15). None shipped.

New selection rule (user-set): train Sharpe >= 1.5 AND validation Sharpe >= 1.5. The previous carry_core / carry_liquidity / carry_book_blend@5d sleeves fail it and were dropped. Survivors + newly-admitted (the relaxed train bar finally lets momentum in):

name recipe train val turnover carry_quality 10d-high+vol+amihud, inv-vol, 7d 1.62 2.85 0.37 carry_book_blend carry+book, inv-vol, liq-10, 7d, band .3 2.47 1.90 0.38 carry_book_wide carry+book, full universe, 3d, band .3 2.45 1.70 0.58 book_curvature bid-vs-ask curvature imbalance, 3d, band .6 1.56 1.89 0.58 mom_9d 9d-1d momentum, inv-vol, 10d, band .6 1.55 1.58 0.33

mom_9d's train-PnL correlation to every carry sleeve is ~0.0 — the book finally has a second family. Equal-weight blend: train Sharpe 3.00 (+48%/yr), validation 3.38 (+38%/yr) at gross 1.0.

Holdout is now burned. With validation inside the selection gate these val numbers are selection criteria, not out-of-sample estimates. The next honest test is the next unseen months of data.

Production run (Markowitz, full period): net Sharpe 1.64, +37% total, maxDD -10.9%, turnover 0.51/day — notably WORSE than the equal-weight blend of the same sleeves (~3 Sharpe). The rolling-30d Markowitz allocator chases recent sleeve returns; the pre-cleanup research reached the same conclusion (EW / risk parity beat Markowitz walk-forward). Next step: expose an equal-weight / risk-parity combine mode in the pipeline.

docs.title: Round 5 — protocol v2 (pre-registered 3-way split), the clean run
docs.text:
Protocol fixed BEFORE the sweep (see methodology): TRAIN 2024-12..2025-08 (search), TEST 2025-09..2025-12 (admission gate only), VAL 2026-01..2026-05 (opened once, at the very end; never computed during the sweep). 38 simple one-formula bases x 5 spans x 2 bands x 2 weightings x 2 universes = 1,520 candidates; all windows <= 10d; liquidity mask is a fraction (60%) of the universe and the beta proxy is the cross-sectional mean, so every sleeve transfers unchanged to the ~100-name production universe.

Band answer (measured on TRAIN): the no-trade band lifts the mean candidate Sharpe from -0.62 to +0.08 by cutting turnover ~3x. It is a cost filter, and it stays.

Shipped book (6 sleeves; variant chosen by TRAIN, admitted by TEST):

name train test turnover carry_book_blend (carry+book, liq, 3d, b60) 3.52 1.07 0.44 carry_book_fast (carry+book, inv-vol, liq, 2d) 2.54 1.21 1.10 carry_core (5-way carry, 3d, b60) 2.50 1.97 0.19 carry_quality (10d-high+vol+amihud, inv-vol, 3d, b60) 2.43 1.63 0.31 book_curvature (curvature imbalance, inv-vol, liq, 2d, b60) 2.28 1.40 0.61 range_carry (10d range carry, liq, 2d) 1.70 1.66 0.35

Max pairwise TRAIN |corr| 0.69. EW blend: train 3.55, test 1.96.

Allocator (chosen on TRAIN+TEST walk-forward, pre-registered "highest, simpler wins ties"): EW 2.40 > RP-30d 2.37 ~ MK-30d 2.37. The pipeline now supports --combine ew|risk_parity|markowitz + --alloc-lookback-days / --max-strategy-weight.

FINAL VAL (opened once):

combine VAL Sharpe VAL ann PnL VAL maxDD full-period Sharpe ew (pre-registered pick) 1.12 +14.6%/yr -4.5% 2.68 risk_parity (reference) 1.32 +16.4%/yr -4.6% 2.18 markowitz (reference) 0.46 +6.0%/yr -12.0% 1.58

The honest number for this book on 17 names is VAL Sharpe ~1.1 (EW). Consistent with round 3's clean estimate (0.87) and with the train->test decay (3.55 -> 1.96): roughly a 2-3x haircut from train to reality. Caveat: the 18-month history was touched by earlier rounds at the family level, so even this number is mildly optimistic; and 5 months of VAL has a Sharpe standard error of ~1.5.

Route to Sharpe >= 4 (measured, not promised): breadth first — at fixed signal quality cross-sectional Sharpe scales ~sqrt(N); 17 -> 100 names is ~x2.4, putting the same book at ~2.5-3. The remaining gap needs new signal families on data we don't have locally yet (um futures panels: OI, LSR, funding — the brother's best sleeves lived there) and longer history. Markowitz allocation is NOT the route: on real sleeves it loses to EW/RP.

docs.title: Round 6 — cost-model audit, Markowitz fix, |corr| < 0.4
docs.text:
Cost audit (user: "numbers too depressive"). The quoted-spread metric (ob__minor__spread_bps__mean) is broken on this dataset: BTCUSDT has a NEGATIVE mean (-94.7 bps; 17% of bars negative, median 0) and thin alts are ~2x inflated vs. what takers actually paid (WIF quoted 18.2 vs effective 6.1 bps median; NEAR 6.3 vs 2.6; APT 5.0 vs 1.9; OP 7.8 vs 3.8). The cost model now uses the EFFECTIVE spread from the tape: (buy_vwap - sell_vwap)/vwap, 7d rolling median, clipped [0.2, 50] bps (alpha_engine/backtest/pnl.py::effective_spread_bps, wired into the pipeline with quoted-metric fallback). Fee 1.6 bps + 1 bps slippage and the decide-at-t / fill-at-VWAP(t+1) delay are unchanged — deliberately conservative. No double-counting found. Impact: EW book test Sharpe 1.96 -> 2.80 on comparable sleeves.

Markowitz fix (user: "reducing Sharpe looks wrong"). Two real defects in the combine layer: (a) mu/cov were estimated on raw 30-min bars — far too noisy for a tangency mean estimate, so the allocator chased the last day's hot sleeve; (b) the warm-up rows were NaN, silently flattening the whole portfolio for the first lookback days. Fixed: estimation now runs on daily-aggregated sleeve PnL and the warm-up trades equal weight. On train+test the markowitz combine went from portfolio-destroying to competitive (test-window Sharpe 3.61, the best of the three modes). It still loses out-of-sample to EW/RP — that is tangency fragility with few sleeves, not a bug.

Portfolio re-selected under pairwise TRAIN |corr| < 0.4 (user rule), same pre-registered gates, corrected costs:

name train test turnover carry_book_blend (carry+book, liq, 3d, b60) 3.53 1.13 0.44 carry_core (5-way carry, 3d, b60) 2.54 2.01 0.19 book_curvature (inv-vol, liq, 2d, b60) 2.30 1.47 0.61 dist_high10 (10d-high proximity, inv-vol, liq, 5d, b60) 1.69 1.09 0.38

Max pairwise |corr| = 0.40. EW: train 4.43, test 2.80.

Final numbers (pipeline, honest costs, val sliced):

combine train+test VAL Sharpe VAL maxDD full period ew 4.03 0.82 -4.7% 3.23 risk_parity 4.07 0.94 -4.2% 3.32 markowitz (fixed) 3.66 -0.19 -5.4% 2.64

VAL is no longer clean (this is its third opening across rounds) and 5 months of daily PnL has a Sharpe s.e. of ~1.5: the 0.8-1.3 spread between recent books is statistically indistinguishable. The stable conclusions: costs are now honest and slightly LOWER than before (the depressive numbers were not a cost bug — the val regime is genuinely hard for the carry complex); EW/RP remain the production allocators; Markowitz is fixed but should not be the default. Next real measurement: the 100-name universe / new months.

docs.title: Rounds 7-8 — the walk-forward machine and the 14-sleeve book
docs.text:
Goal (user): 20+ sleeves, pairwise |corr| <= 0.4, Sharpe >= 4 on data nothing was fitted to. Approach: a sleeve LIBRARY with canonical fixed parameters (~40 one-formula bases x {full / liquid-half / illiquid-half} + session-refresh and time-scale-split variants; no grids at all), and a monthly WALK-FORWARD: each month the portfolio is re-selected using only prior data (window Sharpe gate + greedy corr<=0.4 + risk-parity weights) and trades the next month. The concatenated 12 months are genuinely out-of-sample and hyperopt-free.

Measured: - Walk-forward OOS, 12 months: Sharpe 1.41 (halves 0.71 / 2.23), ann +10.8%, maxDD -4.1%, ~14 sleeves/month. - Selection avg pairwise corr 0.06 -> diversification ceiling ~4x; the implied honest per-sleeve OOS Sharpe is ~0.4-0.6, capping any portfolio of these sleeves at OOS ~1.5-2.5 on 17 names regardless of N. - Negative results, disclosed: 6-name tercile universes and a nested-tuned selector on a 272-sleeve library made walk-forward WORSE (0.17-0.33) — selection noise dominates; bigger pools need bigger universes, not more variants. - Corr saturation: under |corr|<=0.4 this universe supports ~14 genuinely distinct sleeves, not 20+. The cap binds on mechanisms, not effort.

Shipped: alpha_engine/strategies/book2026.py — spec-driven, 14 sleeves (book pressure x sessions, donchian/momentum by liquidity half, curvature, depth carry, OBV corr, slope, top-1 notional, whale prints, reversal-US, ts-split). Bit-for-bit parity with research (max daily-PnL diff 5e-7). Production run (--combine risk_parity): full-period net Sharpe 3.49, +38%, maxDD -3.0%, turnover 0.27/day — an IN-SAMPLE-SELECTED number (canonical params soften but do not remove selection bias); the honest forward expectation for this machine on 17 names is the walk-forward 1.41.

Route to OOS >= 4 stays breadth: on ~100 names each sleeve gains ~sqrt-breadth (x2.0-2.4) AND the universe supports 5-6 disjoint liquidity groups (more sleeves, lower avg corr). The identical walk-forward machine re-run on the 100-name metrics is the next measurement.

docs.title: Round 9 — new mechanism families, the 20-sleeve book
docs.text:
Response to "the formulas were lazy": 18 genuinely new mechanism families were designed and tested (canonical params, honest costs, 3 universes): BTC/liquid-half lead-lag, order-flow-vs-depth (OFI), book consumption and replenishment (d_size x flow sign), 8h funding-cycle echo, microprice drift, institutional footprint (q99/q50 trade sizes), impact asymmetry, book-mass location (weighted_distance), depth_ratio imbalance, flow persistence, tail-vs-mean pressure, absorption, flow-volatility carry, resilience trend, trade-mix shift.

Survivors (stable in both halves): flow_vol_carry (1.78), mass_dist (1.59 / 1.21), ofi on illiquids (0.98), resil_trend (0.88). Dead, for the record: lead-lag at 30-min bars (sub-bar phenomenon), flow persistence, impact asymmetry, consumption/replenishment, funding echo (half-unstable).

The new mechanisms unlocked the correlation saturation: the full-window book under pairwise |corr| <= 0.4 grew from 14 to 20 sleeves (avg corr 0.055, max 0.39). book2026.py updated; bit-for-bit parity for all 20. Full-period risk-parity: research 3.67 (ann +23.5%, maxDD -2.1%).

Honest read stands: full-window sleeve Sharpes (0.5-2.0) are fixed-parameter but window-selected; the walk-forward machine remains the honest expectation (~0.7-1.4 on 17 names). Individual sleeve Sharpe 2.5+ with honest evaluation does not exist in this dataset — 60+ formula families tried across 9 rounds. Breadth remains the lever.

docs.title: Round 10 — the clean book (full universe only) + creative round 2
docs.text:
User call: on 17 names sub-universe slicing is pseudo-diversification — dropped. 15 more new mechanisms tried (full universe, canonical params): anchored-VWAP gap, liquidity momentum (deepening book / compressing spread / improving amihud), churn carry, skew carry, BTC decoupling, regional (Asia-vs-US) footprint, crowd-vs-whale divergence, book-lean persistence, vol term structure, session variants, candle-body pressure, net-flow trend. Survivors: skew_carry (0.75, stable, corr 0.14 to the book) and lean_persist (1.17, stable — replaced book_ens_us which it dominates at corr 0.49). Dead: 13 of 15, including all "liquidity momentum" variants (-1.3..-1.5) and anchored-VWAP gap (-2.6).

FINAL PRODUCTION BOOK (book2026.py): 6 full-universe strategies — mass_dist 1.59, depth_carry 1.35, mom_9d 1.28, lean_persist 1.17, notional_top1 0.83, skew_carry 0.75. Avg pairwise corr -0.02, max 0.28. Pipeline run (risk-parity): net Sharpe 3.52, +39.6% total, maxDD -3.8%, turnover 0.37/day. Same disclaimers as ever: full-window selection; walk-forward expectation ~1-1.5; next honest measurement = the 100-name universe, where sub-universes and the 20+ book become legitimate again.

docs.title: Research protocol: strategy book v2 (2026-07)
docs.text: Pre-registered BEFORE any candidate evaluation on the rebuilt data. Data: fixed data-historical-vision (per-bar klines after the k-way replay fix) + datametrics-1m (order book), spot, 17 names, 2024-12-01..2026-05-29.

docs.title: Targets (owner-set, hard; REVISED by owner 2026-07-08 mid-round, before
selection was frozen)
docs.text:
• Per-strategy net Sharpe >= 1.5 (train), positive on holdout.
  • Pairwise |corr(PnL)| <= 0.4 across the final book.
  • Per-strategy turnover <= 1.0 gross/day (sanitary cap, not an objective).
  • Sign-flips admitted only for bases negative in BOTH train halves (stable inverse hypothesis, not sign mining).
  • Signal windows: research grid up to 45d (owner clarified 2026-07-08 that the old "<=10d" cap was really "fit within accumulated live parser history"). Shipping gate: a strategy goes live only when its longest window <= usable live usdm history (accumulated-since-2026-06-16 minus ~20% margin; ~17d usable at protocol time, grows ~1d/day). Longer-window survivors ship flagged "deploy when history suffices".
  • Simple: one readable formula per strategy + a one-sentence economic story.

docs.title: Anti-overfit discipline
docs.text:
1. Split: TRAIN = 2024-12-01..2025-11-30, HOLDOUT = 2025-12-01..2026-05-29. Holdout is opened ONCE, after the book is frozen on train. No re-selection after seeing holdout. Report both numbers whatever they are.
  2. All evaluation through the ONE pipeline (vwap execution, fee 1.6bps + half effective spread, smoothing ON) -- никаких самопальных eval.
  3. Candidate grid fixed in advance (families below); every evaluated candidate is logged, including failures -- the research log reports the count so the multiple-testing burden is visible.
  4. Parameter stability: a candidate passes only if neighbours in its own param grid (span x0.5 / x2) keep >= 70% of its train Sharpe.
  5. Selection: greedy by train Sharpe under the corr/turnover constraints; ties break toward the simpler formula.

docs.title: Candidate families (fixed vocabulary)
docs.text:
All from existing 791 Go keys; no OI (not captured by our parser -- the competitor OI example is not portable until the parser learns OI).

  • F1 price: momentum / reversal on per-bar closes (NEW: first honest run, old data was daily-stepped), windows 1-10d.
  • F2 OB shape: mass distance, depth cost asymmetry, imbalance persistence, book slope (ob__{5,25}pct__{bid,ask}* and ob__minor*).
  • F3 basis: OB-weighted mid vs close ratio (competitor #1 style).
  • F4 flow: buy/sell vwap gap, volume-quantile entropy (competitor #2 style, set_entropy analog over buy_volume_q{50,95,99} vs sell_*).
  • F5 tape distribution: skewness / tail asymmetry of returns and trade sizes.
  • F6 cross: norm_ratio combinations of F2 x F4.
  • Old book sleeves re-enter the same funnel as candidates (mass_dist, depth_carry, mom_9d, lean_persist, notional_top1, skew_carry).

docs.title: Parallel check (required)
docs.text: Smoothing A/B (delta 0.005 vs off) re-run on the FIXED data for the final book and per sleeve: confirm |delta Sharpe| < 0.1. If smoothing hurts more than that, escalate to owner before shipping.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• strategies/book2026v2.py + registry + tests.
  • Research log: candidates tried (count per family), survivors, train/holdout table, corr matrix, turnover, smoothing A/B.
  • Updated headline numbers on fixed data (old book vs new book).

docs.title: ADDENDUM 2026-07-08: null calibration (stage-3 of the systematic search)
docs.text: The full funnel (EMA -> neutral -> cap, honest costs) run on per-symbol circularly-shifted returns (3 seeds x 1035 candidates) yields |Sharpe| from NOTHING: median 1.31, p95 2.32, p99 2.98 on the 17-name train year. Consequences, binding for future rounds on this universe: - per-strategy train gate raised to >= 2.3 (null p95) AND positive holdout; - a train Sharpe of 1.5-2.5 alone is NOT evidence on 17 names; - pair-combinatorics mining on 17 names found nothing above the bar -- breadth (top-100 / expansion panels) is the statistical-regime lever, not more candidates.

docs.title: Strategy research methodology
docs.text: How new strategies are developed for this repo, and the rules that keep the reported numbers honest. The engine mechanics (PnL kernel, cost model) are in methodology.md; this document is about the search.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Maximise net annualised Sharpe of a dollar-neutral cross-sectional portfolio. PnL level is secondary: with Sharpe S, target volatility (and therefore PnL) is set by leverage; 100%/year is reachable at moderate leverage only if S is high enough that the levered max drawdown stays survivable. Rule of thumb used here: a portfolio with net Sharpe >= 3 and max drawdown <= 15% of one-year PnL can be levered to 100%/year without a realistic risk of ruin; Sharpe 2 cannot.

Hard gates for any individual strategy:

  • net Sharpe >= 2.0 on the TRAIN window (anything below 2 is discarded);
  • net Sharpe >= 1.0 on the untouched VALIDATION window, same sign in both halves of train;
  • daily turnover <= 2.0 (fees eat everything faster than that);
  • active (non-zero weights) >= 60% of bars.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
binance/ (git-ignored, ~5.2 GB): Backend-go precomputed 30-min metrics, spot market, 17 symbols, 2024-12-01 .. 2026-05-29 (26,113 bars):

  • data-historical-vision — trades/klines metrics (OHLCV, vwap, taker buy/sell flow, per-trade size quantiles, kyle_lambda, herfindahl, ...);
  • datametrics-1m — order-book metrics (ob__*, 721 keys: depth cost / size / slope / curvature / imbalance / microprice / resilience / spread at 5%/25%/minor bands).

Loaded once into RAM as wide (bars x tickers) frames via GoMetricsStore (parallel shard scan + on-disk parquet cache in .metrics_cache/, so the second run of anything is seconds). Liquidation and funding keys are not populated on spot and are excluded.

docs.title: Three-way split (protocol v2, pre-registered 2026-07-02)
docs.text:
TRAIN  2024-12-01 .. 2025-08-31  (9 months)  — signal search, parameter grids
TEST   2025-09-01 .. 2025-12-31  (4 months)  — selection gate ONLY
VAL    2026-01-01 .. 2026-05-29  (5 months)  — touched ONCE, at the very end

Roles: strategies are developed on TRAIN, admitted or rejected on TEST, and the finished portfolio (with its allocator) is scored once on VAL. Nothing is selected, re-tuned, or dropped based on VAL — its number is the deliverable, good or bad. During the sweep VAL PnL is not even computed: the research scorer only sees data through 2025-12-31.

Pre-registered gates (fixed before the sweep, not adjusted after):

  • per-candidate: TRAIN Sharpe >= 1.5, both TRAIN halves > 0, TEST Sharpe >= 1.0, turnover <= 2.0/day, active >= 60% of bars;
  • per-family: grid-median TRAIN Sharpe >= 1.0 (a family must work across its whole parameter grid, not in one lucky cell);
  • one variant per family, chosen by the highest TRAIN Sharpe among gate-passers (never by TEST rank — TEST only admits or rejects);
  • near-duplicates (TRAIN daily-PnL corr >= 0.9) collapse to the higher TRAIN Sharpe; portfolio built greedily by TRAIN Sharpe under pairwise TRAIN |corr| < 0.7 (the allocator handles moderate correlation).

Allocator settings (combine mode, lookback, rebalance cadence, per-strategy cap) are engineering choices fixed on TRAIN+TEST sleeve PnL before VAL is opened.

Known impurity, disclosed: earlier rounds (research log rounds 1-4) used 2025-11+ data for selection, so this history is not virgin for signal families. The protocol above still removes per-candidate test/val mining; the only fully clean check remains genuinely new data / paper trading.

docs.title: Execution & cost model (fixed, not searched)
docs.text: Everything is scored through the one kernel (alpha_engine/backtest/pnl.py), vwap execution mode: decide at bar t, fill at VWAP(t+1), earn VWAP(t+1)->VWAP(t+2). Costs per unit traded notional: fee 1.6 bps + half quoted spread (per ticker per bar, capped at 50 bps, fallback 2 bps) + 1 bps flat slippage. These are deliberately conservative for a maker-capable USD-M setup and are never tuned during the search.

docs.title: Candidate construction
docs.text:
Signals are cross-sectional (long/short across the 17 names), built only from economically motivated families — no exhaustive mining of all 791 keys:

  1. Book pressure — bid-vs-ask depth cost / cumulative size imbalance.
  2. Book shape — slope, curvature, level counts, top-of-book notional.
  3. Taker flow — buy/sell quote-volume imbalance, trade-count imbalance, large-trade (q95) imbalance.
  4. Microstructure state — kyle lambda, herfindahl, spread level/change, book resilience.
  5. Price action — multi-day momentum, short-term reversal, BTC-residual momentum, range position, close-vs-vwap gap.
  6. Carry / quality — inverse-vol, spread, depth and beta rank-carries.

Each family yields one base signal (z-scored or ranked). The searched hyper-parameters are deliberately few: EMA smoothing span, no-trade band (0 / 0.3 / 0.6 x cap), and weighting mode (proportional / inverse-vol). Weights = trunc_normalize(ema(signal), max_w=0.125), dollar-neutral, per-name cap 12.5% (17 names -> gross stays at 1).

Lookback budget (hard constraint): every rolling window and EMA span parameter in a shipped strategy is capped at 10 days. Signal families that need longer memory (90d distance-from-high, multi-week seasonality) are excluded from the search.

Simplicity budget: a base signal is one readable formula — at most a ratio/difference of 2-3 metrics plus one z-score/rank and one smoothing step. No stacked residualisations, no per-strategy token lists; everything must transfer unchanged to a wider universe (the production parser covers ~100 names; liquidity masks are defined as a fraction of the universe, not a fixed count). The no-trade band stays in the grid as {0, 0.6}; its usefulness is measured on TRAIN and reported, not assumed.

Multiple-testing budget: the total candidate count is kept in the low hundreds (dozens of bases x a small grid), and the expected best-of-N Sharpe under the null is checked against it: with ~300 candidates on ~11 months of daily PnL, a pure-noise best sits around Sharpe ~1.3-1.5 — one more reason the individual gate is 2.0, not 1.5.

docs.title: Portfolio construction
docs.text:
1. Gate candidates (train Sharpe >= 2, turnover <= 2, activity >= 60%).
  2. Drop near-duplicates (daily-PnL corr >= 0.9 within the same family — keep the higher-Sharpe one).
  3. Greedy max-Sharpe selection under pairwise daily-PnL |corr| < 0.35.
  4. Score the selected set on validation; drop failures; report both windows.
  5. The survivors are implemented as AlphaStrategy classes, registered in ALPHA_REGISTRY, and combined by the existing Markowitz layer (AlphaPipeline, rolling 30d window, per-strategy cap) — the production system is strategies + Markowitz on top, and the final reported numbers come from python tools/backtest.py --metrics-roots ..., not from the research scripts.

docs.title: Leverage & the 100%/year target
docs.text: All research PnL is at gross exposure 1.0. If the final portfolio makes p per year at Sharpe S with max drawdown d, leverage L = 1.0 / p delivers ~100%/year with max drawdown L*d and unchanged Sharpe. The decision to lever is made on S and L*d, never by picking higher-PnL / lower-Sharpe candidates.

docs.title: What is committed vs. throwaway
docs.text: Committed: this document, the final AlphaStrategy classes + tests, and the result tables in the research log. The sweep scripts themselves are throwaway (run from a scratch directory); anything worth keeping is the strategy definition, which lives as reviewable strategy code — not as a parallel research framework inside the repo.

docs.title: Backtesting & PnL
docs.text: How AlphaPipeline.run() turns target weights into a PnL series, and what the cost model captures (and doesn't).

docs.title: PnL definition
docs.text:
Implemented in compute_pnl (alpha_engine/backtest/pnl.py), re-exported from alpha_engine.pipeline for backwards compatibility. The per-bar math is pnl_core in the same module — the one kernel; do not implement PnL math anywhere else.

For each bar \(t\) (close-fill mode; vwap mode shifts weights by 2 and earns VWAP returns instead):

\[ \begin{aligned} r_{i,t} &= \frac{p_{i,t} - p_{i,t-1}}{p_{i,t-1}} \\ \text{gross}_t &= \sum_i w_{i, t-1} \cdot r_{i, t} \\ \text{fees}_t &= \sum_i \big| w_{i,t} - w^{\text{acc}}_{i,t} \big| \cdot \text{fee\_rate} \\ \text{funding}_t &= -\sum_i \text{funding}_{i,t} \cdot w_{i,t-1} \\ \text{net}_t &= \text{gross}_t \;-\; \text{fees}_t \;+\; \text{funding}_t \end{aligned} \]

where the accounting weight \(w^{\text{acc}}\) is the previous weight passively carried by the price move:

\[ w^{\text{acc}}_{i,t} \;=\; w_{i,t-1} \cdot \frac{p_{i,t}}{p_{i,t-1}} \]

So \(|w_t - w^{\text{acc}}_t|\) is the traded notional between bars — the part that incurs a fee. Pure price drift on a held position costs nothing.

The shift-by-1 on weights matters: at time \(t\) you're using the position you took at \(t-1\), so you don't see your own decision affect the price.

docs.title: Why subtract funding?
docs.text:
Sign convention on USD-M perpetuals: positive funding ⇒ longs pay shorts. If you're long (\(w > 0\)) and funding is positive, you pay, and your PnL goes down. The formula encodes that as pnl -= funding · w.

If funding is None (e.g. spot-only backtest) the funding leg is zero.

docs.title: Cost model — what's in, what's out
docs.text:
alpha_engine/backtest/pnl.py::pnl_core:

gross  = (w.shift(k) * ret).sum(axis=1)          # k=1 close, k=2 vwap
traded = (w - w.shift(1) * price_change).abs()   # net of passive drift
costs  = (traded * cost_rate).sum(axis=1)        # fee + spread/2 + slip
Captured Not captured Round-trip exchange fee at 0.00016 (= 1.6 bps maker on Binance USD-M) Market impact (size-dependent) Half quoted spread per trade (ob__minor__spread_bps__mean, fallback spread_default_bps) Borrow cost on shorts Flat slippage via slippage_bps Currency / FX (n/a — USD-quoted) Per-bar rebalance cost via change in target Funding settlement effect

Knobs: compute_pnl(fee_rate=…, slippage_bps=…, spread_default_bps=…), exposed on the CLI as --fee-bps / --slippage-bps / --spread-default-bps.

docs.title: Daily turnover
docs.text:
backtest/turnover.py::daily_turnover integrates |Δw| per ticker per day, then sums across tickers. It's reported in summary() as mean_daily_turnover and median_daily_turnover.

A daily turnover of 1.0 means you completely re-trade your gross exposure each day. Turnover × fee_rate is a useful sanity check on the PnL gross-vs-net gap.

docs.title: Sharpe annualisation
docs.text:
daily   = pnl_series.resample("1D").sum()
sharpe  = (daily.mean() / daily.std()) * sqrt(365)

We resample bar-level PnL to daily before computing mean / std. This is the right choice when the bar cadence differs (e.g. comparing 30-min strategies to a hypothetical 1-hour strategy). Use \(\sqrt{365}\) — crypto trades 24/7.

If you want bar-level Sharpe, compute it directly from the pnl_gross / pnl_net series: sharpe_bar = pnl.mean() / pnl.std() * sqrt(48 * 365).

docs.title: Drawdown
docs.text:
\[ \text{dd}_t \;=\; \text{cum}_t \;-\; \max_{s \le t}\, \text{cum}_s \]

Reported as max_drawdown (the most negative value) per leg in the summary. It's an additive PnL drawdown, not a percentage — the unit is "fraction of notional", same as pnl_gross.

docs.title: Plots
docs.text:
fig = pipeline.plot("dashboard")     # 6-panel grid
pipeline.plot("pnl")                  # cumulative gross + net
pipeline.plot("drawdown")             # cum_max − cum
pipeline.plot("weights")              # heatmap (timestamps × tickers)
pipeline.plot("turnover")             # daily turnover bars
pipeline.plot("allocations")          # per-strategy weight over time

Implementations in alpha_engine/backtest/plots.py. Each returns a matplotlib Figure; pipeline.plot() doesn't call plt.show() itself — that's the caller's job (the CLI does it for you when not --no-plot).

docs.title: Summary dict
docs.text:
After pipeline.run():

pipeline.summary()
# {
#   "n_strategies":          int,
#   "strategy_names":        [str, …],
#   "n_tickers":             int,
#   "n_timestamps":          int,
#   "date_range":            "...",
#   "mean_daily_turnover":   float,
#   "median_daily_turnover": float,
#   "gross": {"total_pnl": ..., "annualized_sharpe": ..., "max_drawdown": ...},
#   "net":   {"total_pnl": ..., "annualized_sharpe": ..., "max_drawdown": ...},
# }

The gross / net split is the single most important diagnostic. If gross.annualized_sharpe > 0 and net.annualized_sharpe < 0, the strategy is producing alpha but burning it on fees — reduce turnover (longer EMA, larger rebalance cadence) before searching for a better signal.

docs.title: Common results to watch
docs.text:
• Net Sharpe negative, gross positive → fees / funding eat the alpha. Lower turnover or trade larger names with tighter spreads.
  • Net Sharpe positive, max drawdown larger than realistic risk budget → tail risk. Check the drawdown plot, look at concentration (hh_buy, hh_sell metrics).
  • Allocations fully pinned at max_strategy_weight → at least one strategy is dominating. Either constraints are too lax, or the others contribute nothing — drop them.
  • Allocations bounce wildly between bars → lookback is too short or the strategies are too correlated. See Markowitz.

docs.title: Data layer
docs.text: Layer 1 of the pipeline: read raw ticks, aggregate to 30-minute bars, expose via a lazy dict.

docs.title: The four shapes
docs.text:
graph LR
  R["RawDataReader"]
  AGG[Aggregators]
  AMD["AggregatedMetricsDict<br/>per-exchange dict"]
  ED["ExchangeData<br/>dict[exchange] → AMD"]
  R --> AGG --> AMD
  AMD --> ED
  • RawDataReader — abstract interface over storage. Three concrete impls.
  • Aggregators — pure functions: raw ticks for one ticker → metric dict.
  • AggregatedMetricsDict — lazy dict[metric_name → DataFrame(t × tickers)].
  • ExchangeData — dict of exchange tag → AggregatedMetricsDict.

Strategies see ExchangeData. They write data["binance-f"]["mark_price"] and stay agnostic to whether the backing reader is parquet, mock, or live deque.

docs.title: Readers — pick the right one
docs.text:
Reader Backed by When to use MultiFileParquetReader parser's Hive layout data/market=…/type=…/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol=…/part-* Default for production. Reads what binance_parser writes. Partition-prunes by dt=. ParquetFileReader flat data_root/{exchange}/{kind}/{TICKER}.{parquet,csv,zip} Single-file-per-ticker archives consolidated by some other process. MockRawDataReader synthetic random walks Tests and the --mock flag on the CLI. LiveRawDataReader rolling deques fed by LiveTickBus Live runtime — see Live trading. 
from alpha_engine.metrics.raw_data_reader import (
    MultiFileParquetReader, ParquetFileReader, MockRawDataReader,
)

reader = MultiFileParquetReader("data")          # parser output
reader = ParquetFileReader("legacy_archive")      # flat layout
reader = MockRawDataReader(tickers=["BTC-USDT"])  # tests

The reader interface is intentionally tiny:

class RawDataReader(ABC):
    def read(self, exchange, kind, ticker, since, until) -> pd.DataFrame | None: ...
    def available_tickers(self, exchange, kind) -> list[str]: ...

kind ∈ {"trades", "orderbook", "klines", "funding"}.

docs.title: Aggregators — what they produce
docs.text:
Aggregators take raw ticks for one ticker over [since, until] and return a dict[metric_name → pd.Series] indexed at 30-min bars.

from alpha_engine.metrics.trades_aggregator    import aggregate_trades_30min
from alpha_engine.metrics.orderbook_aggregator import aggregate_orderbook_30min
from alpha_engine.metrics.market_data_aggregator import aggregate_klines_30min, aggregate_funding_30min

AggregatedMetricsDict lazily aggregates all metrics in a group the first time any metric in that group is requested, then caches. Groups: trades, orderbook, klines, funding. The mapping metric_name → group lives in metrics_dict.py::_METRIC_SOURCE.

docs.title: Empty-group behaviour
docs.text: If no ticker has data for a given group, _aggregate_group records the group as "computed" without populating any metrics. Subsequent data["binance-f"]["bid_25_cost"] raises a clear KeyError rather than silently returning a NaN frame — see metrics_dict.py:99.

docs.title: Exchange tags
docs.text:
Two exchange tags ship by default:

Tag Parser market= What it covers binance spot Binance spot streams binance-f usdm Binance USD-M perpetual futures

MultiFileParquetReader knows the mapping via _EXCHANGE_TO_MARKET in raw_data_reader.py. To add a venue (e.g. COIN-M):

  1. Add the entry to _EXCHANGE_TO_MARKET.
  2. Make sure the parser writes under the corresponding market=…/.
  3. Pass exchanges=["…", …] to AlphaPipeline / LiveEngineConfig.

docs.title: Lazy access semantics
docs.text:
data = ExchangeData(reader, since, until, exchanges=["binance-f"])

# These two lines are FREE — no I/O yet.
md = data["binance-f"]
print(type(md))                        # AggregatedMetricsDict

# This triggers ALL kline metrics to be aggregated for ALL tickers and cached.
close = md["close_price"]              # DataFrame(t × tickers)
high  = md["high_price"]               # cached — instant

# Mark price lives in its own kind (USD-M only, NSC-9), so the next line
# pulls in ALL markprice metrics for ALL tickers in one pass.
mark  = md["mark_price"]
pred  = md["predicted_funding"]        # cached — instant

# This triggers ALL trade metrics for ALL tickers.
buys  = md["buy_cost_quantile_0.95"]
hh    = md["hh_buy"]                   # cached

The "all metrics in a group at once" choice is deliberate: a strategy that uses 5 trade metrics pays the per-ticker iteration once instead of 5 times.

docs.title: Metric catalogue (short list)
docs.text:
Full table in Metrics catalogue. Highlights:

Group Examples klines close_price, volume_usd, high_price markprice mark_price, index_price, predicted_funding, next_funding_time_ms (USD-M) funding realized_funding trades buy_cost, buy_cost_quantile_0.95, buy_volume_quantile_0.95_usd, vwap, kyle_lambda, hh_buy, volatility orderbook bid_25_cost_avg, ask_25_vwap_avg, cost_imbalance_10_ratio_avg, bid_ask_spread_rel_avg, last_best_bid_price

The orderbook depth percentages are percent-of-mid (e.g. bid_0_5_cost_avg = bar-mean of bid notional within 0.5% of mid; bid_25_cost_avg = within 25% of mid). Each per-snapshot base is expanded into a 9-aggregate suffix pack (_avg, five quantiles, _skew, _min, _max). Underscores in the name come from str.replace(".", "_").

docs.title: Adding a new metric
docs.text:
1. Compute it inside the right aggregator (e.g. aggregate_trades_for_bar in trades_aggregator.py).
  2. Add its name to the matching *_METRICS registry list.
  3. The lazy dict picks it up automatically.

If the name doesn't match a registered prefix in _resolve_source (bid_*, ask_*, buy_*, sell_*, cost_imbalance_*, the kline allow-list, or *funding*), add a branch — the dict refuses to guess.

docs.text: How much history each component actually needs, and why the live --lookback-days default is 30.

docs.title: Minimum required lookback
docs.text:
The real ceiling is 20 days (book2026v2 momentum spread). Everything else fits in 14 days or less.

The 30-day default covers: - volume-based universe selection (min_periods=1, so it works on shorter history but stabilises around 30 days) - Markowitz default lookback (overridden to 14 in live via --alloc-lookback-days)

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text: --lookback-days 21 is sufficient for all current strategies and cuts live I/O by ~30 % versus the default.

docs.title: Live trading
docs.text: The same strategy code that the backtest uses, run on a real-time bar clock fed by the parser's WebSocket bus. Phase 1 only logs target weights — no orders are placed.

docs.title: The four-phase roadmap
docs.text:
Phase Status What it does Where it lives 1 shipped Signal-only loop end-to-end on Spot. Logs target weights at each bar boundary. alpha_engine/live/ 2 planned Binance USD-M futures venue + funding (funding_reversion works live). — 3 planned PaperExecutor + LiveBlotter — simulated fills + PnL accounting. — 4 planned BinanceFuturesExecutor — real REST orders, userDataStream reconciliation, testnet-by-default safety. —

Phases 2–4 are tracked in ~/.claude/plans/add-real-time-trading-shimmying-raven.md and the README. Phase 1 is what's runnable today.

docs.title: The wiring
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  WS[Binance WebSocket\nspot or usdm] --> WSC[ws_client.listen]
  REST[REST funding poller] --> FW
  WSC --> BUS[LiveTickBus]
  BUS --> FW[FileWriter\nparquet sink]
  BUS --> SUB[reader subscription\nevent-type filtered]
  SUB --> LR[LiveRawDataReader\nrolling deques]
  PARQ[(./data/parquet)] -.warm-start.-> LR
  LR --> ENG[LiveEngine.step]
  CLK[BarClock\nUTC-aligned] --> ENG
  ENG --> LOG[INFO log lines]

  OBM[OrderBookManager\noptional] --> SNAP[snapshot_loop]
  WSC -. depth diffs .-> OBM
  SNAP --> BUS

What the components do:

Component Lives in Job BarClock alpha_engine/live/bar_clock.py Async iterator, yields pd.Timestamp at each UTC-aligned boundary plus a settlement delay. LiveTickBus alpha_engine/live/tick_bus.py In-process pub/sub. Drop-in for FileWriter.write(market, record). Lossy backpressure with per-subscriber queues. LiveRawDataReader alpha_engine/live/live_reader.py RawDataReader interface backed by per-(exchange, ticker, kind) deques. Warm-startable from MultiFileParquetReader. LiveEngine alpha_engine/live/engine.py On every bar, builds ExchangeData, calls run_strategies, blends into one weight vector, logs. service.run_live alpha_engine/live/service.py Wiring of all of the above. Entry point of python main.py live-trade.

docs.title: What happens at each bar boundary
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Clock as BarClock
  participant Eng as LiveEngine.step
  participant Read as LiveRawDataReader
  participant Run as run_strategies
  participant Log

  Clock->>Eng: bar_ts (UTC, +settlement_seconds)
  Eng->>Read: read(exchange, kind, ticker, since, until)
  Read-->>Eng: DataFrame view (in-memory deque slice)
  Eng->>Run: data, alpha_names, max_w, end_range
  Run-->>Eng: dict[name, weights DataFrame]
  Note over Eng: Take the latest row at or before bar_ts<br/>per strategy.
  alt 1 strategy
    Eng->>Eng: combined = the row, copied
  else N strategies
    Eng->>Eng: combined = equal-weight blend of latest rows<br/>(Markowitz lands in Phase 3)
  end
  Eng->>Log: bar #N, gross=…, n_nonzero=…

A single bar uses exactly the same run_strategies call the backtest uses. There is no live-only strategy code.

docs.title: Why equal-weight in Phase 1?
docs.text: Markowitz needs a per-strategy realised-PnL series (the _strategy_returns step). That only exists once a blotter is wired in (Phase 3). Until then we blend by equal weight — coherent, conservative, and obvious in the logs.

docs.title: Warm-start
docs.text:
When you launch with parquet already on disk under ./data/, the live reader hydrates its deques from MultiFileParquetReader. This means your first bar already has the full lookback_days of history — no "wait 30 days" cold-start.

Logged at startup:

Warm-start complete: 12 (exchange,kind,ticker) buffers seeded, 387 654 rows total

If total_rows == 0 the warning suggests you check the parser's Hive layout. The most common cause is pointing --data-root at a directory that exists but doesn't contain market=…/type=…/dt=…/symbol=…/.

docs.title: Subscribing to specific event types
docs.text:
The bus subscriber is created with an event_types filter:

_READER_EVENT_TYPES = (
    "aggtrades", "trades", "klines", "booksnapshot", "funding",
)
sub = bus.subscribe("live-reader", event_types=_READER_EVENT_TYPES)

This drops raw orderbook diffs at the publishing edge — they're the hottest stream (hundreds/sec across symbols) and the live reader only cares about periodic booksnapshot events anyway. Without the filter, the per-subscriber queue fills with diffs and the reader starts dropping trade/kline events.

docs.title: Local order book in live mode
docs.text:
If --no-order-book is not passed (the default), the live runtime spins up OrderBookManager and a snapshot_loop. The snapshot loop calls book_manager.snapshot_top(...) every snapshot_interval_ms (default 1 s since NSC-10, configurable in config/settings.py::LIVE_ORDERBOOK_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS) and emits BookSnapshotEvent records to the bus. Those snapshots are what the orderbook aggregator consumes.

If you disable snapshots (either --no-order-book or --snapshot-interval-ms 0), strategies whose required_kinds include "orderbook" will be skipped at each bar boundary with a WARNING Skipping strategy '<name>' — missing data kinds: ['orderbook'] log line. This is the explicit failure mode that replaces the silent-NaN behaviour of the pre-NSC-10 engine.

docs.title: required_kinds contract
docs.text:
Each strategy declares the set of raw-data kinds it needs:

class BookDepthImbalance(AlphaStrategy):
    required_kinds = frozenset({"klines", "orderbook"})

Before instantiating a strategy, run_strategies queries reader.available_tickers(exchange, kind) for every candidate kind and unions the result. Strategies whose required_kinds aren't covered are skipped with a WARNING. This applies to both the live engine and the batch backtest, so a backtest run on a parquet root that's missing e.g. the markprice partition surfaces the gap immediately rather than producing an inscrutable NaN PnL.

docs.title: Process lifecycle
docs.text:
service.run_live uses asyncio.TaskGroup to spawn:

  • file-writer.start() — flush loop
  • ws-listener — ws_client.listen(bus, market, symbols, book_manager)
  • orderbook-manager.start() — diff replay (if enabled)
  • orderbook-snapshotter — snapshot loop (if enabled)
  • reader-consume — drain the bus subscription
  • engine — the bar tick loop

If any of these crash, TaskGroup cancels the rest and re-raises. There is no built-in retry; restart the process.

Ctrl+C from python main.py live-trade propagates a KeyboardInterrupt, which main.main() swallows with a clean print.

docs.title: CLI — full reference
docs.text:
python main.py live-trade [-h]
    --alphas {ob_mispricing,vol_ob_entropy,funding_reversion,
              trade_imbalance,vol_mean_reversion,book_depth_imbalance} …
    [--symbols SYMBOLS …]            # default: parser SYMBOLS
    [--bar-minutes BAR_MINUTES]      # default 30
    [--lookback-days LOOKBACK_DAYS]  # default 30
    [--max-w MAX_W]                  # default 0.03
    [--end-range END_RANGE]          # default 50
    [--market {spot,usdm}]           # default spot
    [--no-order-book]                # disable local L2 book
    [--snapshot-interval-ms MS]      # override snapshot cadence
    [--data-root DATA_ROOT]          # warm-start root, default ./data
    [--log-level LEVEL]              # default INFO

Examples:

# USD-M, single strategy, no book (signal-only loop on funding)
python main.py live-trade --market usdm --alphas funding_reversion --no-order-book

# Spot, two strategies on a custom universe, debug logging
python main.py live-trade --alphas trade_imbalance ob_mispricing \
    --symbols BTCUSDT ETHUSDT SOLUSDT --log-level DEBUG

# Faster bar cadence (signal-only — keep an eye on noise)
python main.py live-trade --bar-minutes 5 --alphas trade_imbalance

docs.title: Operational notes
docs.text:
• Bar cadence ≠ trade cadence. Phase 1 doesn't trade. Phase 4 will introduce a cooldown_seconds knob and a MAX_ORDERS_PER_BAR limit.
  • Settlement delay. BarClock(settlement_seconds=5.0) (default since NSC-11) waits 5 s past the boundary before yielding so the WS has time to deliver the last few ticks of the just-closed bar. Binance has been observed to lag 5–10 s on reconnect or under load; bump it via --settlement-seconds if your link is even worse. The engine still aligns on the boundary minute.
  • Late-event accounting. After every successful step(bar_ts) the engine calls LiveRawDataReader.mark_bar_processed(bar_ts). Any event arriving after that whose event_ts < bar_ts is counted in LiveRawDataReader.late_events_dropped. The reader logs a WARNING every 100 (configurable) and the total is included in the per-bar LiveEngine.step INFO line so an operator can spot drift. Ticks that miss bar T go into bar T+1, never silently into the deque against a closed bar.
  • Subscriber drops. LiveTickBus.total_dropped and per-subscriber dropped counters are exposed for monitoring. The bus logs a warning on every power-of-two drop count.
  • Warm-start is best-effort. A bad shard doesn't poison the rest: the reader logs and continues.

docs.title: Markowitz combination
docs.text:
Layer 3 of the pipeline. Treat each alpha strategy as an "asset" whose return time-series is the PnL it would have produced if used alone. Solve the closed-form max-Sharpe portfolio over those strategies on a rolling window. Reweight each strategy's per-ticker weights by the solved allocation; sum to get the combined portfolio.

Source: alpha_engine/portfolio/markowitz.py. Theory tests: tests/test_markowitz_theory.py (35 tests covering the closed form, properties, optimality, frontier shape, box constraints).

docs.title: The closed form
docs.text:
For \(n\) strategies with mean-return vector \(\mu \in \mathbb{R}^n\) and covariance \(\Sigma \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}\), the tangency portfolio (max-Sharpe assuming \(r_f = 0\)) is:

\[ w^* \;=\; \frac{\Sigma^{-1}\mu}{\mathbf{1}^\top \Sigma^{-1}\mu} \]

By construction \(\mathbf{1}^\top w^* = 1\). This is the Tobin tangency formula on the efficient frontier — derived by maximising \(w^\top \mu / \sqrt{w^\top \Sigma w}\) subject to \(\mathbf{1}^\top w = 1\).

docs.title: Why closed-form (and not a numerical solver)?
docs.text:
1. Speed. Vectorised Markowitz over hundreds of rebalance points takes milliseconds with np.linalg.inv. A QP solver would dominate the pipeline runtime.
  2. Determinism. Same inputs → same outputs to bit-equality. No solver tolerances to tune.
  3. Box constraints handled by water-filling. The unconstrained tangency is the proportionality direction; constraints that bind are pinned and the rest is renormalised. See below.

docs.title: Box-constrained projection
docs.text:
When [min_strategy_weight, max_strategy_weight] constraints would be violated, we clip + renormalise along the unconstrained tangency direction. This is a simplex projection along the ones direction, implemented as active-set water-filling:

direction := Σ⁻¹μ                    # unconstrained direction (not yet normalised)
loop:
    free      := indices not yet pinned
    mass_free := 1 − Σ_{pinned}     # mass available to free entries
    w_free    := direction[free] · mass_free / Σ direction[free]
    if no entry of w_free violates [min, max]: done
    else: pin the worst violator and iterate

Convergence: at most \(n\) iterations (one pin per loop). Implementation in _solve_markowitz lines 116-161. The test test_water_filling_preserves_ordering_among_unpinned checks the "preserves proportionality on the free set" property.

docs.title: Failure modes (we raise, not silent)
docs.text:
_solve_markowitz raises ValueError rather than fall back to equal-weight in any of these cases:

Failure Why it happens mu empty No strategies to combine cov.shape != (n, n) Dimension bug upstream e^T Σ⁻¹ μ ≈ 0 ("undefined tangency") \(\mu\) has no component along \(\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1}\) — there is no unique max-Sharpe direction. Common case: all-zero \(\mu\). Box constraints infeasible (max·n < 1 or min·n > 1) Constraints can't sum to 1 Water-filling fails to converge in \(n+1\) iterations Numerical pathology (e.g. degenerate cov after ridge) Box-projection collapses sum to ≤ 0 Constraints incompatible with tangency direction

A 1e-12 ridge on Σ stabilises near-singular covariances (perfectly correlated strategies) without hiding genuinely degenerate inputs — np.linalg.inv still raises if the input is truly singular.

docs.title: Rolling rebalance
docs.text:
markowitz_combine:

for i in range(len(common_idx)):
    if i < lookback:
        continue                          # warmup → leave NaN
    if i % rebalance_every != 0:
        allocations.iloc[i] = last_alloc  # carry forward
        continue

    window = strat_returns.iloc[i - lookback : i]
    mu     = window.mean().values
    cov    = window.cov().values
    last_alloc = _solve_markowitz(mu, cov, max_strategy_weight, min_strategy_weight)
    allocations.iloc[i] = last_alloc

Defaults: lookback = 48 * 30 (30 days), rebalance_every = 48 (daily), max_strategy_weight = 0.5, min_strategy_weight = 0.0.

The combined per-ticker portfolio is then:

\[ w_t^{\text{combined}} \;=\; \sum_{k=1}^n \alpha_{k,t} \cdot w_{k,t} \]

where \(\alpha_{k,t}\) is the allocation to strategy \(k\) at time \(t\) from the Markowitz step, and \(w_{k,t}\) is strategy \(k\)'s per-ticker weight vector.

docs.title: Strategy returns
docs.text:
Strategy \(k\)'s per-bar PnL is a scalar:

\[ r_{k,t} \;=\; \sum_i w_{k,i,t-1} \cdot \frac{p_{i,t} - p_{i,t-1}}{p_{i,t-1}} \]

i.e. previous bar's weights × current bar's per-ticker returns, summed across tickers. Implemented in _strategy_returns (markowitz.py:21).

This is the same shift-by-1 convention compute_pnl uses for the combined portfolio — see Backtesting & PnL.

docs.title: Single-strategy short-circuit
docs.text: If only one strategy is supplied, markowitz_combine returns it verbatim. The pipeline-level short-circuit goes further and skips allocations entirely (pipeline.allocations is None). This is a deliberate optimisation: there's nothing to optimise across.

docs.title: When NOT to trust the result
docs.text:
• Lookback shorter than the rebalance cadence. μ is dominated by noise; tangency flips wildly. Rule of thumb: lookback ≥ 30 × rebalance_every.
  • Highly correlated strategies. The tangency direction blows up when \(\Sigma\) is near-singular along \(\mu\). The 1e-12 ridge stops numerical NaN, but the interpretation breaks down. Inspect the strategy correlation matrix.
  • Negative-Sharpe lookback window. If the rolling window has all- negative \(\mu\), \(\Sigma^{-1}\mu\) points "the wrong way" and you'll short the most-negative strategy. That's the math doing exactly what it should — but if your alphas are uncorrelated noise, you're betting on noise.

docs.title: Pipeline overview
docs.text:
alpha_engine/pipeline.py defines:

  • AlphaPipeline — the batch backtest container.
  • run_strategies(data, alpha_names, …) — instantiate + invoke alphas.
  • compute_pnl(weights, prices, funding, fee_rate) — gross / net PnL.

The first is for backtests. The second two are also called by the live runtime — that's what keeps backtest and live coherent.

docs.title: The three layers
docs.text:
class AlphaPipeline:
    """
    Three-layer pipeline:
      Layer 1 -- MetricsDict: 30-min aggregated data from Binance
      Layer 2 -- Alpha strategies: each produces dollar-neutral weights
      Layer 3 -- Markowitz: optimally combines strategies into final weights
    """

sequenceDiagram
  participant CLI
  participant Pipe as AlphaPipeline.run()
  participant L1 as Layer 1<br/>ExchangeData
  participant L2 as Layer 2<br/>run_strategies
  participant L3 as Layer 3<br/>markowitz_combine
  participant PnL as compute_pnl

  CLI->>Pipe: run()
  Pipe->>L1: ExchangeData(reader, since, until, …)
  L1-->>Pipe: lazy view (data["binance-f"]["mark_price"] etc)
  Pipe->>L2: run_strategies(data, alpha_names, max_w, end_range)
  L2-->>Pipe: dict[name, DataFrame(t × tickers)]
  alt single strategy
    Pipe->>Pipe: combined = strategy_weights[only].copy()
  else multiple strategies
    Pipe->>L3: markowitz_combine(strategy_weights, prices, lookback, …)
    L3-->>Pipe: combined_weights DataFrame
  end
  Pipe->>PnL: compute_pnl(combined, prices, funding)
  PnL-->>Pipe: pnl_gross / pnl_net / cumulative_*
  Pipe-->>CLI: combined_weights

docs.title: Single-strategy short-circuit
docs.text: When len(alpha_names) == 1, the pipeline skips Markowitz and uses the single strategy's weights as-is. allocations is None in that case — it's only meaningful with ≥2 strategies.

docs.title: Constructor parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Meaning data_reader required A RawDataReader — the pipeline raises if you forget. Use MultiFileParquetReader for parser output, ParquetFileReader for a flat layout, MockRawDataReader for tests. since / until 2023-01-01 / 2025-01-01 UTC-tz pd.Timestamp window. tickers None (= all on disk) Restrict the universe. alpha_names None (= entire registry) Which alphas to run. exchanges ["binance", "binance-f"] Which exchange tags to instantiate. max_w 0.03 Per-ticker cap inside each strategy. end_range 50 Top-N tickers by volume per strategy. lookback_days 30 Rolling window for the Markowitz step. Bars per day = 48. rebalance_hours 24 Markowitz re-solve cadence. max_strategy_weight 0.5 Box constraint on per-strategy allocation. seed 42 Reserved for stochastic ops; deterministic by default.

docs.title: Outputs after .run()
docs.text:
Attribute Shape Meaning combined_weights (timestamps × tickers) DataFrame Final portfolio weights. strategy_weights dict[name, DataFrame] Per-strategy weights (input to Markowitz). allocations (timestamps × strategy_names) or None Per-strategy weight in the combined portfolio. NaN for warmup rows. pnl DataFrame pnl_gross, cumulative_pnl_gross, pnl_net, cumulative_pnl_net. data ExchangeData The Layer 1 view, kept for replays / plots. 
from alpha_engine.pipeline import AlphaPipeline
from alpha_engine.metrics.raw_data_reader import MultiFileParquetReader
import pandas as pd

p = AlphaPipeline(
    data_reader=MultiFileParquetReader("data"),
    since=pd.Timestamp("2025-01-01", tz="UTC"),
    until=pd.Timestamp("2025-04-01", tz="UTC"),
    alpha_names=["funding_reversion", "trade_imbalance"],
)
p.run()
print(p.summary())
fig = p.plot("dashboard")

docs.title: Shared strategy runner
docs.text:
def run_strategies(
    data,
    alpha_names: Sequence[str],
    max_w: float = 0.03,
    end_range: int = 50,
) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:

Both AlphaPipeline._run_strategies and the live LiveEngine.step call this helper. data is duck-typed — anything that exposes data["binance-f"]["mark_price"] works.

The live runtime constructs an ExchangeData view over [bar_ts - lookback, bar_ts] from the rolling deques, then calls run_strategies exactly as the backtest does. Strategy code is reused 1:1 — no "production-friendly" rewrite step.

docs.title: PnL helper
docs.text:
def compute_pnl(
    weights: pd.DataFrame,
    prices: pd.DataFrame,
    funding: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    fee_rate: float = 0.00016,
) -> pd.DataFrame:

Used internally by AlphaPipeline._compute_pnl, but also exported for ad-hoc analysis (e.g. compute PnL on a manually constructed weight series). See Backtesting & PnL for the math.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
pipeline.summary() returns:

{
  "n_strategies":          int,
  "strategy_names":        list[str],
  "n_tickers":             int,
  "n_timestamps":          int,
  "date_range":            "YYYY-… -> YYYY-…",
  "mean_daily_turnover":   float,
  "median_daily_turnover": float,
  "gross": {
    "total_pnl":         float,
    "annualized_sharpe": float,
    "max_drawdown":      float,
  },
  "net": { ... same shape ... },
}

The split into gross / net lets you see how much fees and funding ate. A strategy with a positive gross Sharpe and negative net Sharpe is a turnover-control problem, not an alpha problem.

docs.title: Writing a strategy
docs.text: Adding a new alpha is three changes in one file plus a smoke test.

docs.title: 1. Subclass AlphaStrategy
docs.text:
Open alpha_engine/strategies/alphas.py and add a class:

from typing import ClassVar

from alpha_engine.operators import normalize, ts_zscore, ts_ema
from alpha_engine.strategies.base import AlphaStrategy, KnownKind


class MyAlpha(AlphaStrategy):
    """One-paragraph hypothesis. Why does this make money?"""

    name = "my_alpha"        # CLI key, must be unique
    required_kinds: ClassVar[frozenset[KnownKind]] = frozenset(
        {"klines", "orderbook"}        # raw kinds this strategy needs
    )

    def gen_weights_raw(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        ex = self.futures_exchange
        bid = self.data[ex]["bid_25_cost"]
        ask = self.data[ex]["ask_25_cost"]

        signal  = (bid - ask) / (bid + ask)
        signal  = ts_zscore(signal, window=48 * 7)   # 7d
        return ts_ema(signal, span=48 * 3)           # 3d

required_kinds is the contract the pipeline checks before instantiating your strategy. Pick from {"trades", "orderbook", "klines", "funding", "markprice"}. If any of those kinds has no data (e.g. orderbook snapshots disabled in live), the engine logs a WARNING and skips your strategy instead of letting it run on NaNs. Always include "klines" — the base class uses volume_usd from there to filter the universe.

You override gen_weights_raw, not gen_weights. The base class handles:

  • _cut_to_top_by_volume — keep the top end_range tickers by 30-day rolling USD volume; NaN the rest. Default end_range = 50.
  • trunc_normalize — demean per row, scale so |w|.sum() == 1, clip to [-max_w, max_w]. Default max_w = 0.03.

So your raw output can be any sign-meaningful score; the framework makes it dollar-neutral and capped.

docs.title: 2. Register it
docs.text:
Same file, append to the registry:

ALPHA_REGISTRY: dict[str, type[AlphaStrategy]] = {
    cls.name: cls
    for cls in [
        OrderbookMispricing,
        VolumeOrderbookEntropy,
        FundingMeanReversion,
        TradeImbalance,
        VolatilityMeanReversion,
        BookDepthImbalance,
        MyAlpha,                 # <-- here
    ]
}

The CLI's --alphas choices=list(ALPHA_REGISTRY.keys()) picks it up automatically. Same for the live runtime.

docs.title: 3. Smoke test
docs.text:
tests/test_pipeline.py::TestAlphaStrategies::test_all_registered_alphas_produce_weights already iterates the entire registry — your new strategy is covered. Run:

pytest tests/test_pipeline.py::TestAlphaStrategies -v

If you want a strategy-specific assertion, add a method:

def test_my_alpha_is_long_when_bid_dominates(mock_data):
    alpha = MyAlpha(data=mock_data, end_range=8)
    w = alpha.gen_weights()
    # … your assertion …

docs.title: Inputs you can use
docs.text:
Anything in Metrics catalogue. A short list:

data = self.data
ex   = self.futures_exchange      # "binance-f" by default
spot = self.spot_exchange         # "binance"

# Klines (always available)
data[ex]["mark_price"]            # USD-M
data[ex]["close_price"]           # spot or futures
data[ex]["volume_usd"]
data[ex]["volume"]                # base-asset volume

# Funding (USD-M only)
data[ex]["predicted_funding"]
data[ex]["realized_funding"]

# Trades
data[ex]["buy_cost_quantile_0.95"]        # USD bought aggressively above 95th-percentile size
data[ex]["sell_volume_quantile_0.95_usd"]
data[ex]["vwap"], data[ex]["volatility"], data[ex]["kyle_lambda"]

# Order book — depth pct in {0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100}
# Per-snapshot bases (cost / size / vwap / levels_size_*) get a 9-agg suffix
# pack (``_avg``, five quantiles, ``_skew``, ``_min``, ``_max``).
data[ex]["bid_25_cost_avg"]
data[ex]["ask_5_vwap_avg"]
data[ex]["cost_imbalance_10_ratio_avg"]

Each access returns a DataFrame (timestamps × tickers) aligned to the strategy's universe.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
alpha_engine/operators.py ships a small toolkit. Use these — they handle the NaN / divide-by-zero cases that bite on real data.

from alpha_engine.operators import (
    rank, normalize, trunc_normalize, norm_ratio,
    ts_return, ts_logreturn, ts_ema, ts_std, ts_zscore,
    set_entropy, set_mean,
)
Op Purpose Cross-sectional or time-series rank(df) Per-row percentile rank in [0, 1] XS normalize(df) Per-row demean + abs-sum-1 scale XS trunc_normalize normalize then clip to [-max_w, max_w] XS norm_ratio(a, b) (a-b)/(a+b), NaN on a+b == 0 XS set_entropy(*dfs) Shannon entropy across a set XS set_mean(*dfs) Element-wise NaN-mean across a set XS ts_return(df, n) pct_change(n) TS ts_logreturn log(x / x.shift(n)) TS ts_ema(df, span) ewm(span).mean() TS ts_std(df, win) rolling(win).std() TS ts_zscore(df, win) rolling z-score TS

Full reference: Operators.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Bar units everywhere. 48 bars = 1 day, 48*7 = 1 week. Never hardcode minutes or hours.
  • Sign convention. Positive weight = long, negative = short. Make sure your formula matches that — it's the most common bug. The signal-to-weight pipeline in the base class doesn't flip signs.
  • No look-ahead. Use ts_* operators (rolling windows). Don't index into the future. compute_pnl shifts weights by 1 bar, so even if you did, the PnL would punish you.
  • Cross-venue is fine. ob_mispricing mixes spot book with futures mark — see its source. Just declare both exchanges in the pipeline config.
  • Document the hypothesis. Class docstring + a one-page write-up under docs/strategies/<name>.md. The template is at Strategies index.

docs.title: Common pitfalls
docs.text: Pitfall Symptom Fix Forgot to register in ALPHA_REGISTRY CLI says "unknown alpha" Add the class to the list Used print debug in gen_weights_raw Unbearable output during pipeline runs Use logging.getLogger(__name__).debug(...) Hardcoded 48 (1 day) and called it a "lookback" Hard to read, easy to break Name a local constant or use 48*1 Forgot ts_zscore window Signal is dominated by absolute scale (e.g. funding values) Z-score before EMA, almost always Weights leak future info Suspiciously high in-sample Sharpe Replace df.shift(-1) with df.shift(1) or use a ts_* op

docs.title: Бэклог по метрикам
docs.text: Список задач, которые мы сознательно отложили при фиксации спеки. Добавляется по мере того, как при обсуждении метрик всплывает что-то, что требует отдельной проработки и не хотелось блокировать основной прогресс.

docs.title: B1. Dust filter (фильтр пыли)
docs.text:
Контекст. При фиксации L1.1 / L1.2 (best_{side}_price, best_{side}_size) обсуждали, как отбрасывать «пыльные» уровни (test-ордера, бот-зонды, мусор от нестандартных источников), чтобы они не становились best.

Что обсуждали. Перебрали: - % × Σ(side_size) — bias к стенкам. - IQR / log-IQR / MAD — нестабильно на скошенных и бимодальных распределениях, плюс шумит на малом числе уровней. - Per-bar pool + 5%-перцентиль — устойчиво, но lookahead на бар. - USD-floor через min_notional — экономически осмыслено, требует mid-price на снапшот. - Гибрид нескольких критериев.

Ни один одиночный критерий не идеален на всех патологичных кейсах.

Что сейчас. Фильтр выключен. best_*_price / best_*_size / производные считаются по всем уровням как есть, включая пыль.

Что сделать. Реализовать настраиваемый dust filter с одним из двух кандидатов (или комбинацией): 1. USD-floor — порог = min_notional / mid_price снапшота. Завязать на exchange_info-feed, который у нас уже пишется. 2. Per-bar pool + перцентиль — threshold = quantile(pool, q), pool из всех sizes бара, q конфигурируемый, дефолт 0.05.

Реализация должна быть глобально-выключаемой через конфиг. По умолчанию — выключено (соответствует текущему состоянию спеки).

Когда приоритетно. Когда пойдём проверять метрики на реальных non-Binance данных или на mock'е — там пыль реально мешает. На чистых Binance-данных биржа сама не пускает sub-min_notional ордера, поэтому в большинстве кейсов filter будет no-op.

docs.title: B2. Расширить exchange_info-поллер на spot
docs.text:
Контекст. Для всех L2-метрик с оффсетом top_x (а это много — {ask/bid}_top_x_{cost,size,vwap,levels_*,...} для всех восьми top-оффсетов в нашем наборе) нужен tick_size символа на момент снапшота. tick_size — минимальный шаг цены, который определяет дискретную сетку, на которую кладутся все ордера. Без него невозможно построить top_x грид (p_i = floor_tick(mid) ± (i−1) × τ).

Где должно быть. tick_size приходит с биржи через REST endpoint: - spot: GET /api/v3/exchangeInfo - usdm: GET /fapi/v1/exchangeInfo

В ответе для каждого символа есть массив filters. Из них берётся запись с filterType == "PRICE_FILTER", поле tickSize. Это и сохраняется в parquet type=exchange_info/. Для BTCUSDT spot тик = 0.01, для BTCUSDT usdm = 0.10, и т.д.

Что сейчас. Парсер запускает exchange_info_poller только если в markets есть usdm (см. binance_parser/services/live.py). Комментарий объясняет: «у спота нет leverage tiers, поэтому пока скоупом ограничились USD-M». Для spot exchange_info на диск не пишется, и tick_size для spot символов недоступен в alpha_engine.

Эффект на метрики. Без tick_size для spot: - ВСЕ top_x метрики на spot невозможны → выпадают из датасета по всем 50+ spot-тикерам. Это ~50% всех L2 top_x ключей (8 оффсетов × ~12 базовых метрик × 9 агрегаций × 2 стороны ≈ 1700 ключей, половина из которых на spot). - Процентные оффсеты не страдают — они не зависят от tick_size. - На usdm всё работает как должно.

Что сделать. 1. Снять условие if "usdm" in markets для запуска exchange_info_poller — пусть запускается также если в markets есть spot. 2. Адаптировать сам поллер под spot endpoint. Сейчас он жёстко завязан на EXCHANGE_INFO_REST_URL (futures URL) и LEVERAGE_BRACKET_REST_URL (только usdm). 3. На spot leverage_bracket не существует — поллер должен корректно эмитить запись с max_leverage = 1 и пустым leverage_brackets. tick/step/min_notional — есть и в spot exchange_info. 4. Storage path: parquet пишется в market=spot/type=exchange_info/dt=…/symbol=…/. Симметрично текущей usdm-партиции. 5. Reader (alpha-engine) уже умеет читать spot/usdm одинаково — изменений не требуется.

Когда приоритетно. Блокирует L2 top_x метрики на spot. Если в фазе тестирования стратегий мы хотим top_x только на usdm — можно отложить. Если нужно симметричное покрытие spot+usdm — это prerequisite.

docs.title: B3. Backtest-доступность L2.8 OB updates метрик
docs.text:
Контекст. L2.8 определяет 12 bar-level счётчиков ({bid/ask}_{place,remove}_{cost,size,count}) из потока WS @depth-диффов. На L2-уровне это лучшая доступная аппроксимация L3-активности. Для live-режима эти метрики собираются in-process diff-observer'ом на парсере. Но для backtest на исторических данных метрики пустые, потому что @depth-диффы на диск не пишутся — мы храним только 30-минутные booksnapshot'ы (полное состояние книги, без дельт).

Эффект. В backtest 12 ключей L2.8 (×50 тикеров на каждом баре) = NaN или 0. Стратегии, использующие их, не работают на истории, только на live.

Что можно сделать.

  1. Сохранять @depth diffs в parquet. Большой объём данных (~100мс кадры × 50 тикеров × 24ч ≈ десятки ГБ/день в несжатом виде, ~5-10 ГБ в zstd). Партиция type=depth_diff/, формат — массив дельт на снапшот. Плюс: точные метрики на истории. Минус: x10 объём parser'а; дополнительный reader/aggregator.

  2. Купить исторические depth-feeds у вендора.

  3. tardis.dev — записывает полный L2 поток Binance, ~$200/мес для одного символа, дороже для пакета.
  4. kaiko, cryptocompare — аналогично.

  5. Преимущество: backfill за прошлые годы (мы не сможем сами сгенерировать без машины времени). Недостаток: платно; формат вендора нужно нормализовать в наш schema.

  6. Аппроксимация из booksnapshot'ов. Вместо реальных 100мс-диффов сравнивать 30-минутные снапшоты подряд: delta_30min = booksnapshot[t] − booksnapshot[t−30min] уровень за уровнем. Получим псевдо-place/remove события на 30-минутном масштабе, а не реальные мс-события. Из этого считать те же counts/sums. Плюс: бесплатно, использует то что уже есть. Минус: грубая аппроксимация — пропускает быстрые place-cancel пары, объединяет несколько событий в одно. На 30-минутах информация о flow сильно усредняется.

  7. Ничего не делать, оставить L2.8 как live-only. Стратегии, использующие эти метрики, тестируются только в live.

Когда приоритетно. Если стратегии активно используют L2.8 в сигналах — сразу. Если только experimentально — можно отложить.

docs.title: B4. Расширить парсер на сбор market-stats endpoints
docs.text:
Контекст. Спека market-stats.md описывает 5 метрик, источник которых — отдельные REST-эндпойнты Binance:

Метрика Endpoint Каденс open_interest /fapi/v1/openInterest?symbol=… (usdm) real-time, поллим 5 мин global_long_accounts /futures/data/globalLongShortAccountRatio (usdm) 5 мин top_long_accounts /futures/data/topLongShortAccountRatio (usdm) 5 мин top_long_positions /futures/data/topLongShortPositionRatio (usdm) 5 мин daily_interest_rate Margin API (/sapi/v1/margin/…) ~раз в сутки

Что сейчас. Парсер этих endpoint'ов не поллит. Соответствующая парquet-партиция отсутствует. В backtest и live все 5 метрик = NaN.

Что сделать. 1. Создать новый поллер в binance_parser/live/market_stats_poller.py по аналогии с funding_poller.py и exchange_info_poller.py. 2. Поллер дёргает каждый из 5 endpoint'ов с подходящей частотой (4 ratio'а — 5 минут синхронно; OI — 1–5 мин; interest rate — раз в час). 3. Складывает в parquet data/market={spot|usdm}/type=market_stats/dt=…/symbol=…/part-*.parquet с колонкой timestamp и колонками-значениями (одна строка на цикл опроса на символ). 4. Расширить reader (raw_data_reader.py) с kind="market_stats", реализовать алгоритм агрегации last value at boundary (как у markprice). 5. Зарегистрировать метрики в _METRIC_SOURCE.

Когда приоритетно. Если стратегии используют sentiment-сигналы (top_long_*, global_long_*) или OI-flow → высокий приоритет. Если нет — можно отложить.

docs.title: Funding — реализованные ставки финансирования
docs.text:
Метрики, источником которых являются реализованные funding-ставки с perpetual-фьючерсов USD-M. Только usdm; для spot funding не существует.

Документ описывает целевую спецификацию.

docs.title: Источник данных
docs.text:
Парсер пишет parquet: 

data/market=usdm/type=funding/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol=SYM/part-*.parquet

Источников два:

  1. Live REST-поллер — GET /fapi/v1/fundingRate дёргается ~30s после каждого UTC-боундари settlement'а: 00:00:30, 08:00:30, 16:00:30. Одна строка в parquet на (symbol, settlement_event).
  2. Historical REST-backfill — пагинированный тот же endpoint, страничкой limit=1000 по startTime/endTime.

docs.title: Используемые поля
docs.text:
funding_time_ms : int64    # время settlement'а в мс UTC
symbol          : string
funding_rate    : float    # ставка за settlement (доля; например 0.0001 = 1bp)
mark_price      : float    # mark-price на момент settlement'а (опционально, иногда NaN)

mark_price из этой партиции — снимок на момент settlement'а, не путать с метрикой mark_price из markprice-блока (та live с 1Hz).

docs.title: Каденс
docs.text: Realized funding settl'ится 3 раза в сутки (3 точки на тикер на сутки). На 30-минутный бар обычно ничего не меняется — ставка та же, что на последнем settlement'е до конца этого бара.

docs.title: Алгоритм агрегации в 30 минут
docs.text:
realized_funding — это forward-fill от последнего settlement'а на 30-минутную сетку:

funding_at_settlement[t]  = funding_rate from row at funding_time_ms = t
realized_funding(B)        = funding_at_settlement[t*]
                              where t* = max{t : funding_time_ms ≤ B.start, t ≤ now}
                           = NaN  if нет ни одного settlement'а до B.start

То есть для бара 14:00:00–14:30:00 берём ставку с самого последнего settlement'а в [..., 14:00:00]. Если последний settlement был в 08:00:00 со ставкой 0.0001 — realized_funding = 0.0001 для всех баров с 08:00:00 до 16:00:00 (следующий settlement).

В терминах pandas: df.resample("30min").reindex(all_bars_idx, method="ffill").

docs.title: Edge cases
docs.text:
• Бары до первого известного settlement'а → NaN. На bootstrap'е парсера (свежее тикер) первые 8 часов могут быть NaN.
  • Тикер только что добавлен на биржу → нет истории funding → NaN.
  • Spot-тикер → NaN всегда (для spot нет funding).

docs.title: realized_funding
docs.text:
Реализованная ставка финансирования за последний settlement. Положительная → лонги платят шортам; отрицательная → шорты платят лонгам.

realized_funding(B) = funding_at_settlement[ last settlement ≤ B.start ]
                    = NaN  if no prior settlement OR ticker is spot

Что говорит. Прямой proxy для перекоса позиций между лонгами и шортами. Высокий положительный funding → лонгов сильно больше → ожидаемо корректировка вниз (mean reversion). Сигнал для funding_reversion альф.

1 ключ.

docs.title: Сводка финальных ключей
docs.text:
realized_funding

1 ключ. Только usdm. NaN для spot и для баров до первого settlement'а.

docs.title: Связь с markprice-блоком
docs.text:
В блоке markprice.md есть метрика predicted_funding — предсказанный funding на следующий settlement, обновляется в реальном времени с частотой 1Hz через WS-стрим @markPrice@1s.

Различие: - realized_funding — последний фактически выплаченный rate (медленно меняющийся, 3 точки в сутки) - predicted_funding — прогноз биржи на следующий settlement (быстро меняющийся, обновляется секундно)

Разница predicted - realized — индикатор «куда развернулся basis с последнего settlement'а».

docs.title: Метрики на основе свечей (klines)
docs.text:
OHLCV-метрики, источником которых являются 1-минутные свечи Binance — живой WS-стрим <symbol>@kline_<interval> или исторические ZIP-архивы с data.binance.vision.

Документ описывает целевую спецификацию — то, как метрики должны считаться. Текущая реализация в коде может отличаться.

docs.title: Источник данных
docs.text:
Парсер пишет parquet в Hive-разметке: 

data/market={spot|usdm}/type=klines/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol=SYM/part-*.parquet

Источников два:

  1. Live — WS стрим <symbol>@kline_1m. Парсер пишет только закрытые бары (x: true); пробегающие промежуточные обновления выбрасываются.
  2. Historical — ZIP с data.binance.vision, разжимаемые в parquet с той же CSV-шапкой.

docs.title: Используемые поля
docs.text:
open_time : int64    (мс UTC, открытие минутной свечи)
open      : float
high      : float
low       : float
close     : float
