sell_cost_sl(B) = Σ LT.total_cost  for LT ∈ SellLT_SL(B)            ≥ 0

Пустой бар → 0.0.

Инвариант с trades-v2: 

buy_cost(B) = buy_cost_ml(B) + buy_cost_sl(B)
sell_cost(B) = sell_cost_ml(B) + sell_cost_sl(B)

Что говорит. Доля cost_ml от общего cost показывает сколько USD-объёма пришло через крупные агрессии. Если 80% денег в ml — рынок двигают пара китов, а не толпа retail. Полезно как нормализатор перед сравнением баров между собой.

4 ключа.

docs.title: L_ML.3 — Mean cost (per trade)
docs.text:
Средний размер логического трейда по типу:

buy_mean_cost_ml(B)  = mean(LT.total_cost  for LT ∈ BuyLT_ML(B))
                     = NaN  if BuyLT_ML(B) is empty
buy_mean_cost_sl(B)  = mean(LT.total_cost  for LT ∈ BuyLT_SL(B))
                     = NaN  if BuyLT_SL(B) is empty
sell_mean_cost_ml(B) = аналогично
sell_mean_cost_sl(B) = аналогично

Пустой подмножество → NaN (не 0.0 — нет трейдов, чтобы усреднить).

Что говорит. Средний размер ml-трейда показывает «насколько крупными были крупные» в этом баре. Если средний ml одного бара $5k, а другого $500k — у второго совсем другой класс игроков.

4 ключа.

docs.title: L_ML.4 — VWAP
docs.text:
Средневзвешенная по объёму цена ml/sl-трейдов:

buy_vwap_ml(B)  = Σ(LT.total_cost) / Σ(LT.total_size)  for LT ∈ BuyLT_ML(B)
                = NaN  if Σ(LT.total_size) = 0  (включая случай BuyLT_ML(B) is empty)
buy_vwap_sl(B)  = аналогично
sell_vwap_ml(B) = аналогично
sell_vwap_sl(B) = аналогично

Что говорит. Разница vwap_ml − vwap_sl ≈ effective price impact крупных ордеров. На толстом стакане разница маленькая (ml едва уходит вглубь), на тонком — большая. Полезно как proxy для ликвидности.

4 ключа.

docs.title: L_ML.5 — Quantile-filtered cost (top q% по размеру)
docs.text:
Сумма USD-ноционала ml/sl-трейдов из топ-q% по total_cost:

threshold_buy_ml_q(B) = quantile([LT.total_cost  for LT ∈ BuyLT_ML(B)], q)

buy_cost_ml_quantile_q(B) = Σ LT.total_cost  for LT ∈ BuyLT_ML(B)
                                              with LT.total_cost ≥ threshold_buy_ml_q(B)
                          = NaN  if BuyLT_ML(B) is empty
buy_cost_sl_quantile_q(B) = аналогично через BuyLT_SL
sell_cost_ml_quantile_q(B) = ...
sell_cost_sl_quantile_q(B) = ...

Что говорит. Концентрируемся на хвосте распределения. q = 0.95 для ml = «сколько USD прошло через топ-5% самых жирных multilevel-агрессий». Изолирует сигнал «китов» от шума мелких ml.

Для каждого q ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95} — 4 базы × 5 = 20 ключей.

docs.title: L_ML.6 — Quantile boundary
docs.text:
Значение total_cost на границе квантиля q (не сумма, а сама граница):

buy_trade_cost_ml_quantile_q(B) = quantile([LT.total_cost for LT ∈ BuyLT_ML(B)], q)
                                = NaN  if BuyLT_ML(B) is empty
buy_trade_cost_sl_quantile_q(B) = quantile([... for LT ∈ BuyLT_SL(B)], q)
sell_trade_cost_ml_quantile_q(B) = ...
sell_trade_cost_sl_quantile_q(B) = ...

Что говорит. Сама граница топ-q% (USD-размер на этой границе). Если buy_trade_cost_ml_quantile_0.95 = $30k — значит топ-5% multilevel buy этого бара начинаются от $30k. Прямое сравнение «насколько крупно было то что считалось крупным» между барами / тикерами.

Для каждого q — 4 базы × 5 = 20 ключей.

docs.title: L_ML.7 — Mean price delta (только для ml)
docs.text:
Средний процент изменения цены, который вызывает multilevel-агрегация, среди топ-q% самых крупных multilevel трейдов по total_cost:

threshold_buy_ml_q(B) = quantile([LT.total_cost for LT ∈ BuyLT_ML(B)], q)
top_buy_ml_q(B)       = [LT ∈ BuyLT_ML(B) : LT.total_cost ≥ threshold_buy_ml_q(B)]

buy_mean_price_delta_ml_quantile_q(B) = mean(LT.price_delta_pct  for LT ∈ top_buy_ml_q(B))
                                      = NaN  if top_buy_ml_q(B) is empty
sell_mean_price_delta_ml_quantile_q(B) = аналогично через SellLT_ML

Sl-версия не определена — для single-level трейдов price_delta_pct = 0 по построению, метрика бы была тривиальной.

Что говорит. На сколько % цена двигалась во время самых крупных multilevel-агрессий. Большие значения = тонкий стакан, цена «уезжает» под крупным ордером. Прямой proxy для близости волатильности.

Для каждого q — 2 стороны × 5 = 10 ключей.

docs.title: L_ML.8 — No-side aggregates
docs.text: Метрики без разделения по сторонам — на всех multilevel/single-level трейдах бара.

docs.title: Mean cost (no side)
docs.text:
mean_cost_ml(B) = mean(LT.total_cost  for LT ∈ LT_ML(B))
                = NaN  if LT_ML(B) is empty
mean_cost_sl(B) = mean(LT.total_cost  for LT ∈ LT_SL(B))
                = NaN  if LT_SL(B) is empty

Что говорит. «Средний размер ml/sl-агрессии без учёта стороны». Полезно когда направление неважно, нужен общий уровень крупности.

2 ключа.

docs.title: Mean price delta (no side, quantile-filtered)
docs.text:
threshold_ml_q(B) = quantile([LT.total_cost for LT ∈ LT_ML(B)], q)
top_ml_q(B)       = [LT ∈ LT_ML(B) : LT.total_cost ≥ threshold_ml_q(B)]

mean_price_delta_ml_quantile_q(B) = mean(LT.price_delta_pct  for LT ∈ top_ml_q(B))
                                  = NaN  if top_ml_q(B) is empty

Что говорит. Аналог L_ML.7 без сторон — общая «волатильность под ml». Если значение растёт от бара к бару → стакан истончается, готовится крупное движение в любую сторону.

Для каждого q — 5 ключей.

docs.title: Сводка финальных ключей
docs.text:
Раздел Метрика Ключей L_ML.1 {buy/sell}_trade_count_{ml/sl} 4 L_ML.2 {buy/sell}_cost_{ml/sl} 4 L_ML.3 {buy/sell}_mean_cost_{ml/sl} 4 L_ML.4 {buy/sell}_vwap_{ml/sl} 4 L_ML.5 {buy/sell}_cost_{ml/sl}_quantile_q × 5 q 20 L_ML.6 {buy/sell}_trade_cost_{ml/sl}_quantile_q × 5 q 20 L_ML.7 {buy/sell}_mean_price_delta_ml_quantile_q × 5 q 10 L_ML.8 mean_cost_{ml/sl} 2 L_ML.8 mean_price_delta_ml_quantile_q × 5 q 5 Итого 73

Плюс к 50 ключам в trades-v2.md и 48 в trades-v1.md — итого trades-блок: 171 ключ.

docs.title: Ограничения и зависимости
docs.text:
• Реконструкция доступна на чистых Binance aggTrade-данных. Для других источников требуется наличие first_trade_id/last_trade_id.
  • Алгоритм — аппроксимация L3 (полной book-by-order информации). False positives крайне редки благодаря contiguous_ids; false negatives возможны при engine timestamp jitter (ε=0 строгое равенство).
  • Все метрики per-bar, без 9-агг разворачивания.
  • В live доступно сразу. В backtest — тоже (aggTrade parquet содержит все нужные поля).
  • Нарушения price-monotonic во входных данных закрывают цепочку (трейды не склеиваются), потенциально логируются на DEBUG.

docs.title: trades_v1 — минимальная sanity-reference
docs.text:
trades_v1 — legacy скрипт, сохранён только как sanity check для v2 (trades-v2.md). На реальных альфах не используется — его метрики дублируются и расширяются в v2.

Зачем нужен: - v2 проводит multilevel-агрегацию (склеивает несколько aggTrades одного агрессора в один логический трейд). Это сложнее и может содержать баги в эвристике склейки. - v1 без multilevel-логики — каждый aggTrade считается как отдельный трейд. Проще, стабильнее, но менее точно с экономической точки зрения. - Совпадение базовых метрик v1 vs v2 (после поправки на multilevel) служит индикатором корректности реконструкции в v2.

docs.title: Источник данных
docs.text:
Партиция type=aggtrades/ (live @aggTrade) или type=aggTrades/ (historical archive). Колонки после нормализации: timestamp, side, price, size.

size — объём сделки в монете (base coin). price × size = USD-ноционал сделки.

«Trade» в v1 = одна запись aggTrade (без многоуровневой склейки).

docs.title: Безпороговые
docs.text:
volume(B)        = Σ size  по всем трейдам бара
buy_volume(B)    = Σ size  по buy-трейдам   (агрессор покупал)
sell_volume(B)   = Σ size  по sell-трейдам  (агрессор продавал)

Для пустого бара = 0.0.

docs.title: Пороговые по USD (_* и _*_usd)
docs.text:
* — USD-порог (например 100, 1000, 10000). Считается только то, что больше порога:

buy_volume_T(B)     = Σ size  по buy-трейдам с (price × size) > T          (в монете)
buy_volume_T_usd(B) = Σ (price × size)  по buy-трейдам с (price × size) > T (в USD)

Симметрично для sell_*.

Зачем: фильтр «крупные сделки» — отделить retail-шум от больших ордеров.

docs.title: Квантильные пороги
docs.text:
«Квантиль выше q» по спеке означает диапазон [q, 1] от распределения размеров трейдов внутри бара. То есть q = 0.95 = топ-5% самых крупных трейдов этого бара.

threshold_q(B) = numpy.quantile([trade.size for trade in B], q)
                                              # для side-split — отдельные распределения

volume_quantile_q(B)      = Σ size  по трейдам со size ≥ threshold_q (всё)
volume_quantile_q_usd(B)  = Σ (price × size)  по тем же
buy_volume_quantile_q(B)  = Σ size  по buy-трейдам в квантиле q (отдельный distribution)
buy_volume_quantile_q_usd(B) = Σ USD по buy-трейдам в квантиле q
sell_volume_quantile_q(B)    = аналогично
sell_volume_quantile_q_usd(B) = аналогично

count_quantile_q(B)       = число трейдов с size ≥ threshold_q
buy_count_quantile_q(B)   = число buy-трейдов в квантиле
sell_count_quantile_q(B)  = число sell-трейдов в квантиле

docs.title: Параметры
docs.text:
Параметр Значения Источник Квантили q {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95} стандартный набор (см. orderbook-l1) USD-пороги T TBD при фиксации v2 пока не закрепляем — общий набор для v1 и v2

USD-пороги решаются при работе с v2 (там они тоже используются).

docs.title: Инварианты для sanity-check
docs.text:
Эти равенства/неравенства должны выполняться, иначе либо v1, либо v2 посчитан некорректно:

volume_v1(B) == volume_v2(B)                          # сумма size одна и та же
buy_volume_v1(B) == buy_volume_v2(B)                  # multilevel не меняет сумму
sell_volume_v1(B) == sell_volume_v2(B)
buy_count_v1(B)  ≥  buy_count_v2(B)                   # v2 склеивает несколько aggTrades в один → count меньше
sell_count_v1(B) ≥  sell_count_v2(B)

Равенство count_v1 == count_v2 означает: ни одного multilevel не обнаружено (либо данных мало, либо рынок очень тонкий).

docs.title: Сводка ключей
docs.text:
volume                                 (1)
buy_volume                             (1)
sell_volume                            (1)

volume_quantile_q       × 5 квантилей  (5)
volume_quantile_q_usd   × 5            (5)
buy_volume_quantile_q   × 5            (5)
buy_volume_quantile_q_usd × 5          (5)
sell_volume_quantile_q  × 5            (5)
sell_volume_quantile_q_usd × 5         (5)

count_quantile_q        × 5            (5)
buy_count_quantile_q    × 5            (5)
sell_count_quantile_q   × 5            (5)

buy_volume_T            × N порогов    (N)
buy_volume_T_usd        × N            (N)
sell_volume_T           × N            (N)
sell_volume_T_usd       × N            (N)

Без USD-порогов: 48 ключей. С USD-порогами: 48 + 4N, где N — выбранный набор порогов (закрепится при v2).

docs.title: Ограничения
docs.text:
• Не различает single-level и multilevel сделки. Все aggTrades = единичные трейды.
  • Не выводит OHLC, vwap, kyle, asr, hh — это всё v2.
  • Не используется в продакшн-альфах. Только sanity.

Полная семантика трейд-метрик — в trades-v2.md.

docs.title: trades_v2 — основные метрики на трейдах
docs.text:
trades_v2 — основной trade-aggregator. Метрики из этого файла используются в продакшн-альфах. Содержит общие метрики (cost, count, vwap, OHLC, volatility, HH, kyle, ASR), но исключает ml/sl-разделение — это в trades-multilevel.md.

Документ описывает целевую спецификацию.

docs.title: Источник данных
docs.text:
Парсер пишет parquet: 

data/market={spot|usdm}/type=aggtrades/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol=SYM/part-*.parquet  (live)
data/market={spot|usdm}/type=aggTrades/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol=SYM/part-*.parquet  (historical)

Reader через kind="trades" объединяет обе партиции (_KIND_TO_TYPES["trades"] = ("aggtrades", "aggTrades")).

Колонки после нормализации: timestamp, side, price, size. - side ∈ {"buy", "sell"} — сторона агрессора - size — объём трейда в base coin - price × size — notional в quote coin (USD-эквивалент)

docs.title: Что такое «трейд» в v2
docs.text:
В v2 «трейд» = результат multilevel-реконструкции: одна логическая агрессия может быть склеена из нескольких aggTrades, если она исполнилась об несколько ценовых уровней. Алгоритм реконструкции — в trades-multilevel.md.

Это значит buy_count_v2 ≤ buy_count_v1 (см. trades-v1.md): v2 склеивает несколько aggTrades в один логический трейд.

Все формулы ниже применимы к итоговому списку «логических трейдов» после реконструкции. Если реконструкция выключена (опция парсера) — формулы применимы напрямую к aggTrades, и v2 ≡ v1 в этих метриках.

docs.title: Per-bar нативно
docs.text: В отличие от orderbook-метрик, trades — это поток событий, не снапшоты. Все метрики bar-level: одно число на бар на тикер. Никаких 9-агг шаблонов сверху не накладывается.

docs.title: Конвенция имён
docs.text:
Суффикс Значение Пример _quantile_q порог по q-й перцентили распределения внутри бара buy_cost_quantile_0.95 _above_T фиксированный USD-порог buy_count_above_1000

Параметры: - q ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95} (стандартный набор) - T ∈ {100, 1000, 10_000, 100_000, 1_000_000} (USD)

docs.title: Нотация
docs.text:
Trades(B) = [(t_1, side_1, price_1, size_1), ...]   # все трейды в баре B, t_1 < t_2 < ...
BuyTrades(B)  = [trade ∈ Trades(B) : trade.side == "buy"]
SellTrades(B) = [trade ∈ Trades(B) : trade.side == "sell"]

notional(trade) = trade.price × trade.size

docs.title: Per-side (buy/sell) и overall
docs.text:
Большинство метрик существуют в двух формах: - per-side: buy_*, sell_* — считается отдельно по BuyTrades / SellTrades - overall: метрика без префикса (vwap, volatility) — на всех Trades(B)

Если в баре нет трейдов нужной стороны → метрика этой стороны NaN (или 0.0 для аддитивных, см. конкретную метрику).

docs.title: L_T2.1 — Counts
docs.text:
Смысл. Количество трейдов за бар.

buy_count(B)  = |BuyTrades(B)|              ≥ 0  (0 для пустого бара)
sell_count(B) = |SellTrades(B)|             ≥ 0

docs.title: Per-USD-threshold:
docs.text:
buy_count_above_T(B)  = |{ trade ∈ BuyTrades(B)  : notional(trade) > T }|
sell_count_above_T(B) = |{ trade ∈ SellTrades(B) : notional(trade) > T }|

Для каждого T ∈ {100, 1000, 10_000, 100_000, 1_000_000} — 5 ключей × 2 стороны = 10.

Итого Counts: 2 + 10 = 12 ключей.

docs.title: L_T2.2 — Costs (notional sums)
docs.text:
Смысл. Суммарный USD-ноционал прошедших через бар трейдов.

buy_cost(B)  = Σ notional(trade)  for trade ∈ BuyTrades(B)             ≥ 0  (0 если нет buy)
sell_cost(B) = Σ notional(trade)  for trade ∈ SellTrades(B)            ≥ 0

docs.title: Per-quantile (топ q% по размеру):
docs.text:
sorted_buy = sorted(BuyTrades(B), key=notional, descending)
threshold_buy_q = quantile([notional(t) for t in BuyTrades(B)], q)

buy_cost_quantile_q(B)  = Σ notional(trade)  for trade ∈ BuyTrades(B)
                                              with notional(trade) ≥ threshold_buy_q
                        = NaN  if BuyTrades(B) is empty
                                              # nothing to compute quantile from
sell_cost_quantile_q(B) = аналогично

Семантически: «сумма USD-ноционала из топ-q% самых крупных buy-трейдов». Например, q = 0.95 → сумма ноционала топ-5% buy-трейдов.

Для каждого q ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95} — 5 × 2 = 10.

Итого Costs: 2 + 10 = 12 ключей.

docs.title: L_T2.3 — Trade-cost quantile boundaries
docs.text:
Смысл. Значение notional на границе квантиля (не сумма, а сама граница).

buy_trade_cost_quantile_q(B)  = quantile([notional(t) for t in BuyTrades(B)], q)
                              = NaN  if BuyTrades(B) is empty
sell_trade_cost_quantile_q(B) = аналогично

Различие с предыдущим разделом: buy_cost_quantile_0.95 это сумма, buy_trade_cost_quantile_0.95 это значение границы (USD).

Для каждого q ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95} — 5 × 2 = 10 ключей.

docs.title: L_T2.4 — Maximum trade cost
docs.text:
Смысл. Размер крупнейшей сделки за бар.

max_buy_trade_cost(B)  = max(notional(trade) for trade in BuyTrades(B))
                       = 0.0  if BuyTrades(B) is empty
max_sell_trade_cost(B) = аналогично

Согласовано с _sum-конвенцией пустых баров: 0.0, не NaN.

2 ключа.

docs.title: L_T2.5 — VWAP (volume-weighted average price)
docs.text:
Смысл. Средневзвешенная по объёму цена сделок. Эффективная цена исполнения для агрегата трейдов.

buy_vwap(B)  = buy_cost(B)  / buy_volume(B)            # buy_volume = Σ size for buy
             = NaN  if buy_volume(B) = 0

sell_vwap(B) = sell_cost(B) / sell_volume(B)
             = NaN  if sell_volume(B) = 0

vwap(B)      = (buy_cost(B) + sell_cost(B)) / (buy_volume(B) + sell_volume(B))
             = NaN  if total volume = 0

Формула эквивалентна Σ (price × size) / Σ size за один проход.

3 ключа.

docs.title: L_T2.6 — OHLC из трейдов
docs.text:
Смысл. Open, High, Low, Close цены бара, усреднённые между buy- и sell-агрегаторами, чтобы нивелировать bid-ask bounce trade-tape'а.

first_buy_price(B)  = price первого buy-трейда в B (по времени)
last_buy_price(B)   = price последнего buy-трейда
high_buy_price(B)   = max price среди buy-трейдов
low_buy_price(B)    = min price среди buy-трейдов

(аналогично для sell)

open(B)  = (first_buy_price(B) + first_sell_price(B)) / 2
close(B) = (last_buy_price(B)  + last_sell_price(B))  / 2
high(B)  = (high_buy_price(B)  + high_sell_price(B))  / 2
low(B)   = (low_buy_price(B)   + low_sell_price(B))   / 2

docs.title: Edge cases
docs.text:
Любая из четырёх метрик = NaN, если в баре нет хотя бы одной buy- или одной sell-сделки. То есть OHLC требует наличия обеих сторон.

Для пустого бара или однонаправленного бара — все четыре NaN.

4 ключа.

docs.title: L_T2.7 — Volatility
docs.text: Смысл. Стандартное отклонение минутных log-доходностей цены внутри бара.

docs.title: Алгоритм
docs.text:
1. Сгруппировать Trades(B) по минутам (внутри 30-минутного бара получается ≤ 30 групп).
  2. Для каждой минуты m с трейдами вычислить vwap_m = VWAP трейдов этой минуты.
  3. Построить последовательность log-доходностей: 
    r_m = log(vwap_m / vwap_{m_prev})    # m_prev — предыдущая непустая минута
    Минуты без трейдов пропускаются — нет точки в последовательности.
  4. volatility(B) = std(r_m, ddof=1) = NaN if меньше 2 непустых минут

Используем sample std (ddof=1), не population. На практике различие ничтожно при ≥10 наблюдениях.

1 ключ.

docs.title: L_T2.8 — Herfindahl-Hirschman index (HH)
docs.text:
Смысл. Концентрация объёма по трейдам. HH = 1 — весь бар это один трейд; HH = 1/n — равномерное распределение.

hh(B) = Σ (size_i / total_volume)²    for trade_i ∈ Trades(B)
        where total_volume = Σ size_j for j ∈ Trades(B)
      = NaN  if Trades(B) is empty (total_volume = 0)
      = 1.0  if there's only one trade

hh_buy(B)  = Σ (size_i / buy_volume)²    for trade_i ∈ BuyTrades(B)
           = NaN if BuyTrades(B) empty
           = 1.0 if only one buy trade

hh_sell(B) = аналогично для sell

Диапазон: [1/n, 1]. Чем выше — тем более концентрирован объём в нескольких крупных сделках. Можно использовать как proxy для «активности китов».

3 ключа.

docs.title: L_T2.9 — Kyle's lambda (price impact)
docs.text: Смысл. Регрессионный коэффициент price impact: насколько цена двигается на единицу нетто order flow.

docs.title: Алгоритм (по решению T2.E — вариант (а), классика Kyle 1985)
docs.text:
1. Сгруппировать Trades(B) по минутам (≤ 30 групп).
  2. Для каждой минуты m с трейдами: 
    signed_volume_m = Σ (size  if side == "buy"  else  -size)
                  for trade in минуте m
vwap_m          = VWAP трейдов минуты m
  3. Построить последовательность log-returns: 
    r_m = log(vwap_m / vwap_{m_prev})    # m_prev — предыдущая непустая минута
    (Эквивалентно volatility.)
  4. OLS-регрессия: 
    r_m = λ × signed_volume_m + ε
  5. kyle_lambda(B) = slope λ.

docs.title: Edge cases
docs.text:
kyle_lambda(B) = OLS slope                        if ≥ 3 непустых минут
                                                  AND non-zero signed_volume variance
               = NaN                              otherwise

При ≤ 2 минутах OLS вырождается; при signed_volume = const — denominator = 0.

1 ключ.

docs.title: L_T2.10 — Adverse Selection Ratio (ASR)
docs.text: Смысл. Доля «убыточных» taker-сделок. Сделка считается убыточной, если через 60 секунд после неё цена пошла против агрессора.

docs.title: Алгоритм (по решению T2.F — вариант (а), lookahead-window)
docs.text:
Окно фиксировано 60 секунд.

side_sign(side) = +1  if side == "buy"
                = −1  if side == "sell"

# Для каждого trade ∈ Trades(B) с timestamp t:
window_trades(trade) = [tr ∈ AllTrades : t < tr.timestamp ≤ t + 60s]
                       (берётся из ВСЕХ доступных трейдов, не только бара B —
                        поэтому возможен lookahead в следующий бар)

if window_trades(trade) is empty:
    trade исключается из ASR-расчёта (нет 60s-горизонта)

else:
    after_price = window_trades(trade)[-1].price       # цена последнего трейда в окне
    is_loss(trade) = (after_price - trade.price) × side_sign(trade.side) < 0
                     # buy убыточна, если цена упала; sell — если выросла

# Считаем по непустым trade'ам:
included = [trade ∈ Trades(B) : window_trades(trade) ≠ ∅]

asr_count(B)  = |{ trade ∈ included : is_loss(trade) }| / |included|
              = NaN  if included is empty

asr_volume(B) = Σ size  for trade ∈ included with is_loss(trade)
                / Σ size  for trade ∈ included
              = NaN  if included is empty  OR  total size = 0

docs.title: Семантика «убыточной»
docs.text:
trade.side = "buy", trade.price = 95000:
   after_price = 95005  →  Δ = +5,  side_sign = +1,  Δ × sign = +5  →  ✓ выигрыш (не loss)
   after_price = 94990  →  Δ = -10, side_sign = +1,  Δ × sign = -10 →  ✗ убыток (loss)

trade.side = "sell", trade.price = 95000:
   after_price = 95005  →  Δ = +5,  side_sign = -1,  Δ × sign = -5  →  ✗ убыток (loss)
   after_price = 94990  →  Δ = -10, side_sign = -1,  Δ × sign = +10 →  ✓ выигрыш

Покупатель «прав», если цена выросла; продавец — если упала.

docs.title: Cross-bar lookahead
docs.text:
ASR использует трейды из следующих баров, чтобы найти after_price для трейдов конца текущего бара. В backtest это работает (доступ ко всему датасету). В live режиме ASR доступен с задержкой ≥ 60s.

2 ключа: asr_count, asr_volume.

docs.title: Сводка финальных ключей trades-v2
docs.text:
Раздел Метрика Ключей Counts (L_T2.1) buy_count, sell_count 2 Counts (L_T2.1) {buy/sell}_count_above_T × 5 порогов 10 Costs (L_T2.2) buy_cost, sell_cost 2 Costs (L_T2.2) {buy/sell}_cost_quantile_q × 5 квантилей 10 Quantile boundaries (L_T2.3) {buy/sell}_trade_cost_quantile_q × 5 10 Max (L_T2.4) max_{buy/sell}_trade_cost 2 VWAP (L_T2.5) buy_vwap, sell_vwap, vwap 3 OHLC (L_T2.6) open, high, low, close 4 Volatility (L_T2.7) volatility 1 HH (L_T2.8) hh, hh_buy, hh_sell 3 Kyle (L_T2.9) kyle_lambda 1 ASR (L_T2.10) asr_count, asr_volume 2 Итого 50

Плюс ml/sl-метрики из trades-multilevel.md и production-эквивалентов из v1 (см. trades-v1.md).

docs.title: Ограничения и зависимости
docs.text:
• Все метрики per-bar, без 9-агг разворачивания.
  • volatility и kyle_lambda требуют минутной группировки трейдов внутри бара. На малых барах (< 5 минут с трейдами) ненадёжны.
  • ASR требует lookahead на следующий бар для трейдов конца текущего бара. В live доступна с задержкой 60s.
  • Реконструкция multilevel влияет на buy_count, buy_cost (в меньшей степени — в основном на count). Алгоритм — в trades-multilevel.md.

docs.title: Binance parser
docs.text:
Binance market-data pipeline for spot and USD-M perpetual futures. Three runtime modes — live (WebSocket), historical (ZIP download from data.binance.vision), and funding (REST backfill of USD-M funding rates). A local L2 order book is opt-in for live mode.

Page What it covers Live WebSocket The streaming pipeline: ws_client → writer → parquet Historical download ZIP download + funding REST backfill Storage layout Hive partitioning, schemas, why the choices Local order book Bootstrap algorithm, gap detection, snapshot loop Extending the parser Adding a stream, a market, a metric

docs.title: File-level layout
docs.text:
binance_parser/
├── main.py                  # CLI: `live`, `history download`, `history funding`
│
├── config/
│   ├── settings.py          # Per-market URL / endpoint dicts + writer settings
│   └── pairs.py             # PAIRS (601) + MAJOR (20)
│
├── models/
│   ├── events.py            # Live WS DTOs + Arrow schemas
│   ├── history.py           # Historical row DTOs + HISTORY_SCHEMAS
│   ├── rest.py              # ExchangeInfoSymbol
│   └── market.py            # MarketType = "spot" | "usdm"
│
├── live/
│   ├── ws_client.py         # WS connect / reconnect → writer + book
│   ├── writer.py            # Async buffered parquet writer (Hive, zstd)
│   ├── orderbook.py         # L2 book + manager + snapshot loop
│   └── funding_poller.py    # 8h REST poll of funding rates (USD-M)
│
├── history/downloader/
│   ├── urls.py              # FileSpec builder
│   ├── fetch.py             # Download + verify + extract one ZIP
│   ├── batch.py             # Parallel batch + checkpoint resume
│   └── funding_fetch.py     # Paginated funding-rate backfill
│
├── services/
│   ├── live.py              # Wires writer + listeners + book + funding
│   └── download.py          # Wires batch downloader + funding backfill
│
└── tests/                   # DTO parsing + local order-book tests

docs.title: Why this design
docs.text:
A handful of opinionated choices, mostly around storage and the data contract with alpha_engine. Full rationale in the per-page docs; quick summary:

  • Hive parquet for everything. data/market=…/type=…/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol=…/part-*.parquet. Compatible with pa.dataset.dataset(..., partitioning="hive"), DuckDB, Spark partition pruning. The strategy engine prunes by dt= before opening files.
  • Float32 prices, int64 ms timestamps. Halves memory vs. float64/datetime64; precision is plenty for crypto. Compresses well with zstd-3.
  • Array-per-snapshot order book. Each WS diff stored as one row with bids_price / bids_size / asks_price / asks_size as parallel list<float32> columns. The previous "one row per price level" layout had ~40× more rows and worse compression.
  • One flush, many days. At flush time, buffered records are grouped by event UTC date, so a flush that straddles midnight lands in the correct dt= partitions.
  • Market abstraction by dict, not class hierarchy. Every endpoint that differs between spot and usdm is a single dict keyed by MarketType in config/settings.py. Add a market = add an entry.
  • Realised funding via REST poller. Official settlement rates are sparse (3/day); live/funding_poller.py fires ~30 s past each UTC settlement boundary (00 / 08 / 16) and writes one row per symbol into type=funding.
  • Predicted funding + real mark price via WS. USD-M sessions also subscribe to <symbol>@markPrice@1s. Each tick lands in type=markprice with mark price, index price, the predicted next- settlement rate and that settlement's timestamp.
  • Async everywhere. asyncio.TaskGroup runs the writer + per-market listeners + optional book manager + optional funding poller concurrently. WebSocket reconnect is automatic with exponential backoff.

docs.title: CLI quick reference
docs.text:
# Live
python main.py live                              # spot, default symbols
python main.py live --market usdm --symbols BTCUSDT
python main.py live --market both --order-book   # spot + usdm + L2 book
python main.py live --market usdm --with-funding # usdm + 8h funding poll

# Historical download (data.binance.vision ZIPs)
python main.py history download --market spot --group major --months 1 --dry-run
python main.py history download --market usdm --group major --months 12
python main.py history download --market both --group all

# Funding backfill (USD-M)
python main.py history funding --months 12 --dry-run
python main.py history funding --months 12 --symbols BTCUSDT ETHUSDT

Always run from inside binance_parser/ (the package uses bare imports — see Architecture).

docs.title: Extending the parser
docs.text: Three common extensions: adding a stream type, adding a market, and adding a new metric the strategy engine can consume.

docs.title: Adding a new WebSocket stream
docs.text:
Say you want to capture @miniTicker.

  1. Add a DTO in models/events.py:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import ClassVar
import pyarrow as pa

@dataclass
class MiniTicker:
    symbol: str
    timestamp_ms: int
    open: float
    high: float
    low: float
    close: float
    volume: float

    event_type: ClassVar[str] = "miniticker"
    schema: ClassVar[pa.Schema] = pa.schema([
        pa.field("timestamp_ms", pa.int64()),
        pa.field("symbol",       pa.string()),
        pa.field("open",         pa.float32()),
        pa.field("high",         pa.float32()),
        pa.field("low",          pa.float32()),
        pa.field("close",        pa.float32()),
        pa.field("volume",       pa.float32()),
    ])

    @classmethod
    def from_ws(cls, data: dict) -> "MiniTicker":
        return cls(
            symbol       = data["s"],
            timestamp_ms = data["E"],
            open         = float(data["o"]),
            high         = float(data["h"]),
            low          = float(data["l"]),
            close        = float(data["c"]),
            volume       = float(data["v"]),
        )

    def to_rows(self) -> list[dict]:
        return [{
            "timestamp_ms": self.timestamp_ms,
            "symbol":       self.symbol,
            "open":         self.open,
            "high":         self.high,
            "low":          self.low,
            "close":        self.close,
            "volume":       self.volume,
        }]

  1. Wire dispatch in WsEnvelope.from_raw (same file): add a branch that maps the stream suffix to the new DTO.

  2. (Optional) auto-subscribe in live/ws_client.py::default_stream_names:

names.append(f"{s}@miniTicker")
  1. Add a test in binance_parser/tests/test_models.py mirroring the _KLINE_MSG / _TRADE_MSG fixtures.

The writer will pick up the new event type automatically (it routes by event_type ClassVar), and parquet files will land at data/market=…/type=miniticker/dt=…/symbol=…/.

docs.title: Adding a new market
docs.text:
Today the parser supports spot and usdm. To add coinm (COIN-M perpetuals):

  1. Extend the literal in models/market.py:
MarketType = Literal["spot", "usdm", "coinm"]
  1. Add per-market URL entries in config/settings.py:
WS_BASES = {
    "spot":  "wss://stream.binance.com:9443/stream?streams=",
    "usdm":  "wss://fstream.binance.com/stream?streams=",
    "coinm": "wss://dstream.binance.com/stream?streams=",
}
REST_BASES = {
    "spot":  "https://api.binance.com",
    "usdm":  "https://fapi.binance.com",
    "coinm": "https://dapi.binance.com",
}
EXCHANGE_INFO_PATH = {
    "spot":  "/api/v3/exchangeInfo",
    "usdm":  "/fapi/v1/exchangeInfo",
    "coinm": "/dapi/v1/exchangeInfo",
}
DEPTH_SNAPSHOT_PATH = {
    "spot":  "/api/v3/depth",
    "usdm":  "/fapi/v1/depth",
    "coinm": "/dapi/v1/depth",
}
HISTORY_BASES = {
    "spot":  "https://data.binance.vision/data/spot/monthly",
    "usdm":  "https://data.binance.vision/data/futures/um/monthly",
    "coinm": "https://data.binance.vision/data/futures/cm/monthly",
}

  1. Update the CLI — the --market choices in main.py (and in alpha_engine/main.py for live-trade) currently hard-code ["spot", "usdm"]. Add coinm.

  2. (Optional) extend _EXCHANGE_TO_MARKET in alpha_engine/metrics/raw_data_reader.py so the strategy reader knows how to map a new exchange tag to the new market partition.

That's it. No protocol classes, no factory pattern.

docs.title: Adding a new metric
docs.text:
This is on the alpha-engine side — the parser stores the raw ticks; the metric is computed by an aggregator. See Data layer — Adding a new metric.

Short version:

  1. Compute it inside the right aggregator (trades_aggregator.py, orderbook_aggregator.py, etc.).
  2. Add its name to the matching *_METRICS registry list.
  3. If the name doesn't match a registered prefix, add a branch in metrics_dict._resolve_source.
  4. Strategies access it as data["binance-f"]["my_new_metric"].

docs.title: Adding a new sink
docs.text:
LiveTickBus already has a sink interface (attach_sink(sink)). Any object that implements async write(market, record) and async flush() can plug in:

class StdoutSink:
    async def write(self, market, record):
        print(market, record.event_type, record)

    async def flush(self):
        pass

bus = LiveTickBus()
bus.attach_sink(FileWriter())     # parquet
bus.attach_sink(StdoutSink())     # also print

A common use: a metrics sink (Prometheus / StatsD) that counts events per type and reports drop counts.

docs.title: Anti-patterns to avoid
docs.text:
• Don't add a Protocol-based market hierarchy. The dict-of-URLs approach is deliberate — adding a market is one entry per dict.
  • Don't subclass the order book per market. The bootstrap algorithm is identical for spot and USD-M; the only delta is the REST URL, already abstracted.
  • Don't introduce per-event flush intervals. All event types share one flush cadence. If one type is way busier, raise the writer's buffer size, not its cadence.
  • Don't add WS subscriptions to "see what's there". Every subscribed stream costs bandwidth and disk. Subscribe only what a current or planned strategy needs, and document the consumer.

docs.title: Historical download
docs.text: Pull historical Binance market data from data.binance.vision (ZIP archives) and the REST /fundingRate endpoint, normalised into the same Hive-parquet layout the live writer produces.

docs.title: ZIP downloader
docs.text:
python main.py history download --market {spot,usdm,both} \
    [--group {all,major}] [--symbols SYM1 SYM2 …] \
    [--types DATA_TYPES …] [--months N] \
    [--intervals INTERVALS …] [--workers W] \
    [--dry-run] [--yes]
Flag What it does --market spot, usdm, or both. URLs differ — see HISTORY_BASES. --group all (601 pairs) or major (top 20). Override with --symbols. --symbols Manual symbol list — bypasses --group. --types Subset of HISTORY_DEFAULT_TYPES: klines, aggTrades, bookTicker. --months How far back to download. Default HISTORY_DEFAULT_MONTHS. --intervals For klines only. Default HISTORY_KLINE_INTERVALS (1m). --workers Parallel download workers. Default HISTORY_DOWNLOAD_WORKERS. --dry-run Print the URL plan and an estimated download size; don't fetch. --yes Skip the size-confirmation prompt.

Always --dry-run first on a wide selection — --group all --months 12 --types klines aggTrades bookTicker is multiple TB.

docs.title: What gets written
docs.text:
data/market={spot|usdm}/type={klines|aggTrades|bookTicker}/
    dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol=BTCUSDT/part-monthly[-{interval}].parquet

Note the historical files are monthly chunks (one parquet per symbol per month), partitioned by dt= of the first day of the month. The downloader fans them out into daily dt= partitions on disk to match the live layout — strategies don't see a difference.

The aggTrades history exposes a is_buyer_maker boolean instead of the live stream's pre-flipped side string. The reader's _normalise_columns (alpha_engine/metrics/raw_data_reader.py) maps is_buyer_maker → side (True ⇒ "sell", False ⇒ "buy") so the trades aggregator sees a uniform schema.

docs.title: Checkpoint resume
docs.text:
data/.download_checkpoint.json stores completed URLs. A second run skips them, so Ctrl+C / crash mid-batch is safe — re-run with the same arguments and it picks up where it stopped. Checkpoint keys are full URLs, so spot and usdm don't collide.

The checkpoint is per-data-root, so cleaning the data folder also "resets" the checkpoint.

docs.title: Common recipes
docs.text:
# Top-20 USD-M, last 6 months, 1m klines + aggTrades
python main.py history download --market usdm --group major \
    --types klines aggTrades --months 6

# All spot pairs, 1 month of bookTicker
python main.py history download --market spot --group all \
    --types bookTicker --months 1

# A specific list of symbols, default types, last 3 months
python main.py history download --market usdm \
    --symbols BTCUSDT ETHUSDT SOLUSDT --months 3

docs.title: Funding-rate backfill (USD-M only)
docs.text:
The official funding rate endpoint returns one row per settlement (3 per day). Use the history funding subcommand to backfill any window:

python main.py history funding [--group {all,major}] \
    [--symbols SYM1 SYM2 …] [--months N] [--dry-run]
Flag What it does --group major (default) or all. Override with --symbols. --symbols Manual list. --months How far back. Default HISTORY_DEFAULT_MONTHS. --dry-run Print the request count; don't hit the endpoint.

Pagination is handled by funding_fetch.py (1000 rows per page, startTime / endTime window). Output:

data/market=usdm/type=funding/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol=BTCUSDT/
    part-monthly.parquet

The schema is FundingRateRow: funding_time_ms, symbol, funding_rate (float32), mark_price (float32, optional).

Recipes:

# Backfill a year of funding for the major pairs
python main.py history funding --months 12

# Two specific symbols, 6 months
python main.py history funding --months 6 --symbols BTCUSDT ETHUSDT

docs.title: Storage cost estimates
docs.text:
Order of magnitude for a single major-pair, 1 month, USD-M:

Type Approx. size klines/1m ~1 MB aggTrades ~50–500 MB (volume-dependent; BTCUSDT is the upper end) bookTicker ~200 MB–2 GB funding <100 KB (3 rows/day)

--dry-run reports the exact upcoming bytes by HEAD-ing each ZIP, so trust the estimate over this table.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text:
• 403 / Not Found — usually a symbol that didn't exist for that month yet. The downloader logs and skips; the batch keeps going.
  • Verify failure — Binance ships per-ZIP .CHECKSUM files; the downloader verifies SHA256. A mismatch is rare and usually means a truncated download. Re-run; the checkpoint won't include it.
  • Pre-existing files — a dt=…/symbol=…/part-monthly.parquet already on disk is treated as complete and skipped (the checkpoint is the source of truth, but the file existence check is a fast fallback).

docs.title: Live WebSocket
docs.text: Real-time market data capture from Binance's WebSocket streams. Spot and USD-M futures share the same code; only the URL bases differ.

docs.title: Streams subscribed per symbol
docs.text:
{symbol_lc}@depth        ← order-book diffs (in-memory only — see below)
{symbol_lc}@trade        ← individual trades
{symbol_lc}@aggTrade     ← aggregated trades
{symbol_lc}@kline_<i>    ← OHLCV at KLINE_INTERVAL (default 30m)

KLINE_INTERVAL lives in config/settings.py.

Order-book diffs are not written to parquet. They feed the in-memory OrderBook only. The book state is sampled into type=booksnapshot/ every 30 min UTC by OrderBookManager.snapshot_to_parquet_loop — that's the only source of order-book data on disk. See order-book.md for the full snapshot pipeline.

The connection is one combined-stream socket per market — Binance multiplexes everything onto one URL of the form {WS_BASE}{a@depth/b@depth/...}. The listener loops async for raw in ws, parses, and forwards.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  WS[Binance WebSocket] --> LIST[ws_client.listen]
  LIST -->|raw json| ENV[WsEnvelope.from_raw]
  ENV -->|MarketEvent dataclass| WR[FileWriter.write]
  LIST -.@depth raw.-> OB[OrderBookManager]
  WR --> BUF[per-event-type buffers]
  BUF -->|interval or size| FLUSH[flush]
  FLUSH --> PARQ[(Hive parquet)]

WsEnvelope.from_raw dispatches by stream name:

Stream suffix DTO event_type persisted? @depth (in-memory book) — no — book sampled into booksnapshot every 30 min @trade Trade trades yes @aggTrade AggTrade aggtrades yes @kline_<interval> Kline klines yes (closed bars only)

Unknown streams raise UnknownStream (silently ignored — not every combined-stream payload is one we registered for). The book_manager side branch only fires on @depth and bypasses the DTO truncation because the book needs all levels.

docs.title: @trade vs @aggTrade
docs.text:
The default subscription includes only @aggTrade, controlled by LIVE_PREFER_AGGTRADES in config/settings.py (NSC-14). @aggTrade is the aggregated tick stream — Binance pre-rolls simultaneous fills into a single message, which matches the format of the data.binance.vision historical archive (type=aggTrades shards), so backtest and live read the same partition.

Subscribing to both @trade and @aggTrade would let the parser write to both type=trades/ and type=aggtrades/, but the alpha engine routes both event types into one in-memory kind="trades" deque — so the same fill ends up double-counted. To capture raw per-fill ticks (e.g. microstructure research) pass prefer_aggtrades=False to default_stream_names / listen; the alpha engine still reads only aggtrades.

docs.title: Reconnect policy
docs.text:
The loop in listen retries on every kind of failure (ConnectionClosed *, OSError, WebSocketException, Exception). Backoff is exponential, capped at 60 s:

backoff = 1
on disconnect:
    sleep(backoff)
    backoff = min(backoff * 2, 60)
on successful connect: backoff = 1

There's no global retry budget — the loop runs forever. If you want to fail fast in dev, kill with Ctrl+C; the parser exits cleanly via KeyboardInterrupt in main.

docs.title: Writer
docs.text:
live/writer.py::FileWriter is an async batched parquet writer. Records flow through await writer.write(market, record) → per-event-type in-memory buffers → flushed to parquet on either:

  • a buffer size threshold, or
  • a flush interval (FLUSH_EVERY_SEC in config/settings.py).

Flush goes to per-bucket files: at flush time, buffered records are grouped by event UTC date and the bucket lands in the matching dt=YYYY-MM-DD partition. A flush that straddles midnight produces two output files in two dt= directories — neither one bleeds across days.

data/market={market}/type={event_type}/dt={YYYY-MM-DD}/symbol={SYMBOL}/
    part-{HHMMSS}.parquet

HHMMSS is the flush-start UTC time, so multiple flushes within one date co-exist as separate part-*.parquet files.

docs.title: Compression
docs.text: zstd level 3 by default (a fair memory / ratio trade-off for float32 prices and int64 ms timestamps). All schemas are declared as pa.Schema ClassVars on the DTO classes so the writer doesn't infer them at flush time.

docs.title: Mark price stream (USD-M only)
docs.text:
When --market usdm is on, the WS listener also subscribes to <symbol>@markPrice@1s for every symbol. Each tick is persisted as a MarkPrice row with the real mark price, the spot index, the predicted next-settlement funding rate, and the timestamp of that settlement. The partition is data/market=usdm/type=markprice/.

The alpha engine treats markprice as a first-class RawDataKind: the 30-min aggregator carries forward the last-known value at each bar boundary, so strategies see mark_price, index_price, predicted_funding and next_funding_time_ms directly without round-tripping through klines.

docs.title: Funding poller (USD-M only)
docs.text:
live/funding_poller.py is a separate task. It hits https://fapi.binance.com/fapi/v1/fundingRate ~30 seconds past each UTC settlement boundary (00 / 08 / 16) and writes one FundingRateRow per symbol via the same FileWriter. This is the realised funding source of truth — it backfills the funding partition with the rate Binance actually settled at. The continuous mark-price WS stream above feeds the predicted funding (used by funding_reversion), so neither is a substitute for the other.

Enable with --with-funding on a python main.py live --market usdm run.

docs.title: Health watchdogs
docs.text:
Live-data-quality counters live in binance_parser/live/health.py and collect the four signals an operator needs (NSC-13):

Counter Source Log level trade_id_gaps ws_client.listen — non-contiguous trade_id per symbol WARNING ws_reconnects ws_client.listen — outer connect-loop iterations WARNING book_force_resyncs OrderBookManager.watchdog_loop — quiet live or stuck resyncing book ERROR last_event_ts_per_symbol All paths — most-recent timestamp_ms per symbol (probe)

The watchdog runs every 30 s and forces a re-bootstrap if a book has seen no diff in the last 30 s while live, or has been resyncing for more than 60 s. After a successful run on a stable network all three numeric counters should stay at zero; ticking up is the operator's cue that something upstream is wrong.

HealthCounters.snapshot() returns a copy ready for a Prometheus exporter or a one-shot grep-style probe.

docs.title: Exchange-info poller (USD-M only)
docs.text:
live/exchange_info_poller.py is a daily task started automatically whenever the live parser is launched with --market usdm. It polls /fapi/v1/exchangeInfo and /fapi/v1/leverageBracket once on startup and again at every 00:05 UTC, joins the two responses, and writes one row per symbol into

data/market=usdm/type=exchange_info/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol=…/part-*.parquet

The row carries everything the future executor needs to round/validate orders without an extra REST call: tick_size, step_size, min_notional, headline max_leverage and maintenance_margin_rate, default maker/taker fees (USD-M VIP-0 until the account-fee endpoint is wired in) and the full leverage curve as a list<struct> column with {bracket, notional_cap, mmr, max_leverage}.

Spot has its own filters but no leverage tiers, so the poller is USD-M-scoped for now.

docs.title: Local L2 order book
docs.text:
Opt-in via --order-book. When enabled, OrderBookManager:

  • Bootstraps each book with a REST snapshot.
  • Replays buffered diffs in order.
  • Detects gaps (U != prev.u + 1), flips state to resyncing, and re-bootstraps from a fresh snapshot.

Full algorithm in Local order book.

A snapshot loop emits a BookSnapshotEvent to the writer at a configurable cadence (default 5 s in LIVE_ORDERBOOK_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS). These are what the alpha engine's orderbook aggregator consumes.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
python main.py live [-h]
    [--market {spot,usdm,both}]    # default spot
    [--symbols SYMBOLS …]           # default config.settings.SYMBOLS
    [--order-book]                  # local L2 book + snapshot loop
    [--with-funding]                # 8h REST funding poll (usdm only)

Examples:

# Defaults: spot, all symbols, no book, no funding
python main.py live

# USD-M, two symbols, with funding
python main.py live --market usdm --symbols BTCUSDT ETHUSDT --with-funding

# Spot + USD-M concurrently with local L2 books
python main.py live --market both --order-book

docs.title: What you'll see in stdout
docs.text:
[WS spot] Connecting to 20 symbol(s): BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT, BNBUSDT, XRPUSDT...
[WS spot] Connection established ✓
[Writer] Flushed 12,450 records to data/market=spot/type=trades/dt=2026-04-26/...

Errors are printed to stdout too (no logging framework — keeps the parser stand-alone). Reconnects are noisy on purpose — silent re-connections are the worst kind of monitoring failure.

docs.title: Local L2 order book
docs.text: binance_parser/live/orderbook.py keeps a live in-memory L2 book per symbol per market by following Binance's official algorithm (spot and USD-M use the same algorithm; only the REST snapshot URL differs).

docs.title: Persistence and metric contract
docs.text:
Identical for spot and USD-M futures. Code that violates any of these three points is a bug.

# What Cadence Sink Purpose 1 Live state — single OrderBook per (market, symbol), updated by every WS @depth diff every WS event in-memory only live metric input + 30-min snapshot source 2 Full-depth BookSnapshotEvent to type=booksnapshot/ parquet LIVE_ORDERBOOK_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS (default 30 min, UTC-aligned) parquet durable record, 48 snapshots/day/symbol 3 Full-depth BookSnapshotEvent to in-process bus LIVE_ORDERBOOK_BUS_INTERVAL_MS (default 1 s, UTC-aligned) live bus live metric aggregators subscribe and recompute on the diff-applied state at this cadence

Diffs are never persisted to parquet. The bus stream is never written to disk (the file_writer sink excludes event_type="booksnapshot"). Both loops use _sleep_until_next_aligned_tick so ticks land on multiples of the interval irrespective of process start time. Books not in live state at a tick are skipped — half-bootstrapped data never reaches a sink.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> bootstrapping
  bootstrapping --> live: snapshot received and<br/>buffered diffs replayed
  live --> resyncing: gap detected (U != prev.u + 1)
  resyncing --> bootstrapping: re-fetch snapshot

States:

  • bootstrapping — buffering incoming @depth diffs, no book state yet. Triggers a REST snapshot fetch; the book is "live" once the snapshot lands and the first diff with U <= snapshot.lastUpdateId+1 <= u is applied.
  • live — every diff is applied; last_update_id is checked to be contiguous (U == last_update_id + 1).
  • resyncing — gap detected. Drop existing state and re-bootstrap. resync_count is incremented (good metric to watch).

docs.title: The bootstrap sequence
docs.text:
1. Subscribe to {symbol}@depth and start buffering events.
  2. Fetch GET /api/v3/depth?symbol=…&limit=1000 (spot) or GET /fapi/v1/depth?symbol=…&limit=1000 (USD-M). The response has a lastUpdateId.
  3. Drop all buffered events with u <= lastUpdateId.
  4. Find the first buffered event with U <= lastUpdateId + 1 <= u — this is the "matching" event that bridges snapshot and diff stream.
  5. Apply that event and every subsequent buffered event in order.
  6. State transitions to live. Future diffs apply directly.

If no buffered event "straddles" lastUpdateId (e.g. the buffer is entirely too old or too new), bootstrap fails — return False, sleep, retry from step 1. The test test_bootstrap_returns_false_when_buffer_does_not_straddle_snapshot exercises this path.

docs.title: Gap detection
docs.text:
In the live state, every incoming diff must satisfy U == last_update_id + 1. If not:

  • Flip state to resyncing.
  • Increment resync_count.
  • Drop the bid/ask books.
  • Restart bootstrap from step 1.

This happens on:

  • Lost WS messages (rare with Binance's pings, but possible).
  • Server-side state resets.
  • Network blip during reconnect (the writer reconnects automatically; the in-flight diffs may not align).

Tests test_gap_detection_flips_state_to_resyncing and test_resync_replays_buffered_events_after_gap cover the recovery sequence.

docs.title: qty == 0 means "remove"
docs.text:
Per Binance spec, a level with qty == 0 in a diff means delete that price level. OrderBook.apply_diff does:

for px, sz in updates:
    if sz == 0:
        book.pop(px, None)
    else:
        book[px] = sz

Test: test_zero_quantity_removes_level.

docs.title: Sorted by price
docs.text:
SortedDict from sortedcontainers keeps both sides ordered. Top-N queries (book.top(n)) are O(N) since N is small (Binance gives up to 5000 levels per side; we typically only inspect the top 25).

For bids, "best" means highest price; for asks, lowest. The top() helper handles the direction so consumers don't have to.

docs.title: Snapshot loops
docs.text:
Two cadences emit the same BookSnapshotEvent for two different consumers. WS @depth diffs are never persisted on their own — they only update the in-memory OrderBook. Periodic snapshots are the only thing on disk.

loop interval (default) sink purpose snapshot_to_parquet_loop LIVE_ORDERBOOK_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS = 1_800_000 (30 min) parquet (type=booksnapshot/) durable record, UTC-aligned to :00 / :30 snapshot_to_bus_loop LIVE_ORDERBOOK_BUS_INTERVAL_MS = 1_000 (1 Hz) in-process bus live metric aggregator (alpha_engine)

Both loops use _sleep_until_next_aligned_tick so ticks always land on a multiple of the interval — independent of process start time. Snapshots carry the full book; the previous top-N truncation is gone.

async def snapshot_to_parquet_loop(self, interval_ms, writer, writer_market):
    interval_s = interval_ms / 1000
    while True:
        await self._sleep_until_next_aligned_tick(interval_s)
        for book in self.books.values():
            if book.state != "live":
                continue
            evt = self._build_snapshot_event(book, int(time.time() * 1000))
            await writer.write(writer_market, evt)

The bus loop has the same shape but writes to a LiveTickBus which fans the snapshot to subscribed LiveRawDataReader instances without forwarding to the parquet sink — the bus's attach_sink(file_writer, exclude_types={"booksnapshot"}) opts out of that.

LiveRawDataReader keeps kind="orderbook" rows in its rolling deque with a per-kind lookback of 1 day (vs 60 days global default), so even 1 Hz × full depth fits in single-digit GB per symbol of memory.

docs.title: Manager
docs.text:
OrderBookManager is the multi-symbol container:

mgr = OrderBookManager(market="usdm", symbols=["BTCUSDT", "ETHUSDT"])
await mgr.start()                          # bootstrap all books
mgr.handle_raw_depth(stream, payload)      # called by ws_client
await mgr.snapshot_loop(interval_ms, top_levels, writer, market)

The handle_raw_depth entry point is the bridge to the WS listener — ws_client.listen pulls raw @depth payloads off the socket and tees them to both the DTO path (truncated, written to parquet) and the manager (full levels, kept in memory).

docs.title: Operational notes
docs.text:
• Memory: ~5000 levels × 2 sides × ~32 bytes/entry × N symbols. At 20 symbols, comfortably under 10 MB.
  • Initial REST fetch is slow — the first ~5 s after launch are spent bootstrapping every book. Subsequent restarts are similar (no on-disk persistence).
  • Resyncs are fine. A few per day per symbol is normal; dozens per hour suggests network problems or you're behind a flaky proxy.
  • Snapshots are point-in-time copies. They share no memory with the live book — safe to send across an asyncio.Queue without locks.

docs.title: Storage layout
docs.text:
Every parquet file the parser writes lives under one root, partitioned identically:

data/
└── market={spot|usdm}/
    └── type={orderbook|trades|aggtrades|klines|funding|booksnapshot|markprice|exchange_info}/
        └── dt=YYYY-MM-DD/
            └── symbol=BTCUSDT/
                └── part-{HHMMSS|monthly}[-{interval}].parquet

This is standard Hive partitioning. Tools that support it:

  • pa.dataset.dataset(path, partitioning="hive") (PyArrow)
  • DuckDB read_parquet('path/**/*.parquet', hive_partitioning=1)
  • Spark spark.read.parquet(path) (auto-detects hive)
  • The MultiFileParquetReader in alpha_engine

Partition pruning means a 30-day query on BTCUSDT klines opens 30 files, not the year on disk.

docs.title: Live vs. historical files
docs.text:
Both layouts share the directory tree, but the file names differ:

File pattern Source part-{HHMMSS}.parquet Live writer flushes (HHMMSS = flush start UTC) part-monthly.parquet Historical aggTrades, bookTicker, funding part-monthly-{interval}.parquet Historical klines (interval e.g. 1m) part-HHMMSS.parquet under booksnapshot/ Snapshot loop output

The strategy reader globs all *.parquet under the matching symbol= directory and concats — file naming doesn't matter for reads.

docs.title: Schemas — live streams
docs.text:
event_type Key fields Source orderbook timestamp_ms, symbol, first_update, last_update, bids_price list<f32>, bids_size, asks_price, asks_size @depth trades timestamp_ms, symbol, trade_id, price, qty, side @trade aggtrades timestamp_ms, symbol, agg_id, price, qty, side, first_trade_id, last_trade_id @aggTrade klines open_time, close_time, symbol, interval, o/h/l/c/volume, quote_volume, taker_buy_*, trades, closed @kline_<intv> funding funding_time_ms, symbol, funding_rate, mark_price REST poll (usdm) markprice timestamp_ms, symbol, mark_price, index_price, predicted_funding_rate, next_funding_time_ms @markPrice@1s (usdm) exchange_info timestamp_ms, symbol, status, contract_type, tick_size, step_size, min_notional, max_leverage, maintenance_margin_rate, maker_fee, taker_fee, leverage_brackets list<struct> daily REST poll (usdm) booksnapshot timestamp_ms, symbol, update_id, bids_price, bids_size, asks_price, asks_size local book loop

Defined as pa.Schema ClassVars on the corresponding DTO in models/events.py (or models/history.py for funding).

docs.title: Hive layout
docs.text:
• Partition pruning at the directory level — MultiFileParquetReader filters dt=YYYY-MM-DD directories by date before opening a single file.
  • Per-symbol directories let you tar / archive / move one symbol's history without touching others.
  • Plays well with object storage (S3 / GCS) when you eventually want to promote data/ to an S3 path.

docs.title: Float32 for prices and sizes
docs.text:
• Halves memory vs. float64; precision is plenty for crypto book cents.
  • Compresses better with zstd-3 (more value clustering at f32 resolution).
  • The aggregators promote to float64 at compute time, so loss of precision doesn't propagate.

docs.title: Int64 milliseconds for timestamps
docs.text:
• Matches Binance's wire format — no conversion at write time.
  • Sortable as plain integers for binary search.
  • The reader's _normalise_columns converts to pd.Timestamp on read.

docs.title: Array-per-snapshot order book
docs.text:
The naive layout is "one row per price level":

timestamp_ms, symbol, side, price, size
1700000000000, BTCUSDT, bid, 49998.5, 0.4
1700000000000, BTCUSDT, bid, 49997.0, 1.2
1700000000000, BTCUSDT, bid, 49996.5, 0.8
… 39 more rows for asks …

That's ~80 rows per snapshot, ~30 GB/day on a busy symbol with all the metadata duplicated. We use one row per snapshot, four parallel list columns: 

timestamp_ms, symbol, first_update, last_update,
bids_price=[49998.5, 49997.0, 49996.5, …],
bids_size =[0.4,     1.2,     0.8,    …],
asks_price=[…], asks_size=[…]

Same data, ~40× fewer rows, ~3× better zstd ratio. The aggregator unpacks the lists per row.

docs.title: One flush, many days
docs.text:
FileWriter buckets buffered records by event UTC date at flush time, then writes one file per (market, type, dt, symbol) group. A flush that straddles midnight UTC produces two files in two dt= directories, neither contaminated.

The alternative (one file per flush, all in "today's" partition) means a record from 23:59:59 UTC ends up under tomorrow's dt= partition. That breaks per-day queries.

docs.title: Dataset access from notebooks
docs.text:
import pyarrow.dataset as ds
import pandas as pd

# All BTC trades for one day, no copy step
d = ds.dataset(
    "data/market=usdm/type=trades",
    format="parquet",
    partitioning="hive",
)
df = d.to_table(
    filter=(ds.field("dt") == "2026-04-25") & (ds.field("symbol") == "BTCUSDT"),
).to_pandas()

# Or via the project's reader (handles column normalisation)
from alpha_engine.metrics.raw_data_reader import MultiFileParquetReader

r = MultiFileParquetReader("data")
df = r.read(
    "binance-f", "trades", "BTCUSDT",
    pd.Timestamp("2026-04-25", tz="UTC"),
    pd.Timestamp("2026-04-26", tz="UTC"),
)

docs.title: Removing data
docs.text:
There is no built-in retention policy. To clear:

# Remove one month of one symbol's USD-M trades
rm -rf data/market=usdm/type=trades/dt=2026-04-*/symbol=BTCUSDT/

# Reset the download checkpoint to re-pull a window
rm data/.download_checkpoint.json

Be aware that removing files without also removing the matching checkpoint entry will not cause a re-download — the checkpoint is the source of truth.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
For contributors and maintainers.

Page What it covers Setup Local dev environment, virtualenv, optional tools Testing How the test suite is laid out and run Contributing Conventions, PR checklist, commit style

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: A few conventions that make reviews fast and the codebase coherent.

docs.title: Before you open a PR
docs.text:
1. Tests pass: pytest from the repo root.
  2. CLI smoke test still works:

python tools/backtest.py --mock --since 2024-01-01 --until 2024-01-08 \
    --alphas funding_reversion --no-plot
3. If you touched the parser, the parser-only path also runs:

cd binance_parser && python main.py history download --dry-run --market spot
4. If you added a strategy: a one-page docs/strategies/<name>.md and a row in Strategies index.

docs.title: Commit style
docs.text:
The repo follows a loose conventional-commits format:

<scope>(<area>): <imperative summary>

<body — what / why, not how>

Examples from git log:

fix(live+storage): address PR review — make live stack runnable, cut disk waste
feat(parser): USD-M futures + funding + compact Hive storage; trim abstractions
docs: split research notes — methodology, per-strategy, research log

Keep the summary under ~70 chars. A multi-line body is fine for non-trivial changes; explain why, not what (the diff is what).

docs.title: What to include in a PR description
docs.text:
• Why the change is needed.
  • What's user-visible (CLI flags, output format, performance).
  • What you tested manually (real-data run, live mode smoke test).
  • What you didn't change that a reviewer might wonder about.

For strategy additions, include the back-test summary (gross / net Sharpe, drawdown, turnover) inline.

docs.title: Code conventions
docs.text:
• 30-min UTC bars everywhere. Lookbacks in bars (48*7), not hours. If you really need a non-30-min cadence, add a config knob rather than hardcoding 60 / 5 / etc.
  • Sign convention: positive weight = long, positive funding = longs pay. PnL math relies on it.
  • NumPy 2.x / pandas 2.2+ idioms. No pd.np, no pd.DataFrame.append, no import pandas.tseries.offsets as off.
  • Don't add a Pydantic / dataclass-validation dependency. The parser DTOs use plain @dataclass. The schema is enforced by pa.Schema ClassVars.
  • Don't introduce a logging framework into the parser. The parser prints. The alpha engine uses logging. Keep them separate so the parser stays a stand-alone runnable.
  • Don't catch Exception to "make tests pass". If something surprising fails, fix the root cause.

docs.title: Failure-mode philosophy
docs.text: _solve_markowitz raises rather than fall back to equal weights. AlphaPipeline raises if data_reader=None. The lazy metrics dict raises on unknown metric names rather than return a NaN frame. Adopt the same pattern in new code: fail loud on a misuse, degrade gracefully on a transient external problem.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Strategy README pattern. One file per alpha under docs/strategies/<name>.md. Code-derived sections (formula, params) must match alpha_engine/strategies/alphas.py — change them together.
  • Research-log entries. Numbers (Sharpe, drawdown) go in docs/research-log.md with date, commit, data range. Don't put numbers in the per-strategy file (they go stale).
  • MkDocs preview. mkdocs serve shows the rendered site; please check that any new page renders before opening the PR.

docs.title: What requires a discussion before coding
docs.text:
• New external dependency (a wheel that ships native code: ask first).
  • A change to the parquet schema (live or historical) — anything the alpha engine reads has a contract.
  • A new strategy that needs a new aggregator metric (vs. composing existing metrics).
  • Anything that changes the live engine's per-bar contract (timing, blocking I/O, exception handling).

For everything else: open the PR.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: Local development environment in five commands.

docs.title: Clone + venv
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/SNCapital/-Backend.git backend
cd backend

python3.13 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -U pip

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt -r binance_parser/requirements.txt

That gives you everything the engine and parser need — pandas, pyarrow, scipy, matplotlib for backtest; aiohttp, websockets, sortedcontainers for the parser.

For the docs site (this site) — install the doc tooling separately:

pip install 'mkdocs-material>=9.5' 'pymdown-extensions>=10'

docs.title: Smoke test
docs.text:
pytest                                 # 100 passing
python tools/backtest.py --mock --since 2024-01-01 --until 2024-01-08 \
    --alphas funding_reversion --no-plot

docs.title: Editor
docs.text:
Anything with Python LSP works. The repo uses:

  • from __future__ import annotations — forward refs everywhere.
  • Plain dataclasses — no Pydantic.
  • Stdlib pathlib and typing.Literal for paths and enums.

Recommended VS Code settings:

{
  "python.defaultInterpreterPath": ".venv/bin/python",
  "python.testing.pytestEnabled": true,
  "python.testing.pytestArgs": ["."],
  "editor.formatOnSave": false
}

docs.title: Optional tools
docs.text:
• Black for autoformat (pip install black; black .). Not enforced in CI yet, but the codebase is already roughly Black-shaped.
  • Ruff for linting (pip install ruff; ruff check .). The conftest's noqa: E402 for the parser sys.path hack is the only intentional lint suppression.
  • DuckDB for poking at parquet without loading the engine:
pip install duckdb
duckdb -c "
  SELECT symbol, count(*)
  FROM read_parquet('data/market=usdm/type=trades/**/*.parquet', hive_partitioning=1)
  WHERE dt = '2026-04-25'
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY 2 DESC
"

docs.title: A note about the parser's bare imports
docs.text:
binance_parser/ imports its own subpackages without the package prefix (from config.settings import …, not from binance_parser.config.settings import …). This is intentional — it means the parser is its own runnable application that doesn't care about being a sub-package.

To make pytest from the repo root work, the root conftest.py prepends binance_parser/ onto sys.path. The same trick lives in alpha_engine/live/service.py so python main.py live-trade works from anywhere.

If you write new code in the alpha engine that needs the parser, you have two equivalent options:

# Either: copy the sys.path trick (see alpha_engine/live/service.py)
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "binance_parser"))
from models.events import MarketEvent

# Or: use the namespaced form (also works because of conftest)
from binance_parser.models.events import MarketEvent

The first form matches the parser's internal style; the second is clearer in code review. Pick one and be consistent within a file.

docs.title: Common dev tasks
docs.text: Task Command Add a new strategy Edit alpha_engine/strategies/alphas.py — see Writing a strategy Add a new metric Edit one of alpha_engine/metrics/*_aggregator.py Add a new WS stream Edit binance_parser/models/events.py + live/ws_client.py — see Extending the parser Run the docs site locally mkdocs serve Run a single test class pytest tests/test_pipeline.py::TestMarkowitz -v Run with debug logging python main.py live-trade --log-level DEBUG …

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Unified test layout. One command from the repo root runs everything.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
pytest                                 # all 100 tests
pytest -v                              # with names
pytest tests/test_pipeline.py          # alpha engine pipeline only
pytest binance_parser/tests/test_orderbook.py -v   # parser order book only
pytest -k markowitz                    # by keyword

pyproject.toml declares:

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests", "binance_parser/tests"]
addopts  = "-ra --strict-markers"

conftest.py (repo root) injects binance_parser/ onto sys.path so the parser's bare imports resolve from any CWD — see Setup.

docs.title: tests/test_pipeline.py — pipeline plumbing
docs.text:
TestMockMetrics       — Layer 1 lazy access, shape consistency, caching
TestOperators         — normalize / trunc_normalize / rank / norm_ratio
TestAlphaStrategies   — every alpha in ALPHA_REGISTRY produces sane weights
TestMarkowitz         — _solve_markowitz failure modes + shape
TestPipeline          — end-to-end run, summary, allocations sum to 1
test_pipeline_requires_data_reader — pipeline raises if data_reader=None

The pipeline fixture is module-scoped — pipeline runs once per test session, all TestPipeline methods reuse it. Fast.

docs.title: tests/test_aggregators.py — Layer 1 / Layer 2 correctness
docs.text: Trade aggregator, orderbook aggregator, market data aggregator, the lazy AggregatedMetricsDict, multi-exchange access, and one end-to-end pipeline-with-reader sanity check.

docs.title: tests/test_markowitz_theory.py — the math
docs.text:
35 tests, the most interesting suite:

  • TestTangencyFormula — closed-form matches, identity / diagonal / full covariance.
  • TestTangencyProperties — sums to one, scale invariance, permutation equivariance, symmetric assets get equal weight.
  • TestMaxSharpeOptimality — tangency beats random portfolios, equal weight, minimum variance.
  • TestEfficientFrontier — minimum-variance point, parabola formula, tangency lies on the frontier.
  • TestStrictErrors — every documented failure mode raises with the expected message.
  • TestBoxConstraints — water-filling preserves ordering on the free set, max_weight respected, unbinding bounds match unconstrained.

If you change _solve_markowitz, this is the suite that will break first. Keep it green.

docs.title: binance_parser/tests/test_models.py — DTO parsing
docs.text:
Realistic Binance combined-stream payloads → DTOs:

  • Order book diffs (default + array format + @depth5@100ms etc.)
  • Trades (price / size / side parsing, side flip from is_buyer_maker)
  • AggTrades (routed to AggTrade, not Trade)
  • Klines (volume extensions: quote_volume, taker_buy_*)
  • Funding (REST shape, with and without mark_price)
  • ExchangeInfoSymbol (spot, perpetual, halted)
  • Unknown stream ⇒ UnknownStream raised

docs.title: binance_parser/tests/test_orderbook.py — local L2 book
docs.text: Bootstrap + replay, gap detection + resync, qty=0 removes a level, top() ordering, mid and spread_bps, empty-book API, snapshot event array shape.

docs.title: A new strategy
docs.text:
tests/test_pipeline.py::TestAlphaStrategies already iterates the entire ALPHA_REGISTRY. Your new strategy is covered by the existing "produces weights / approximately neutral / respects max_w" tests.

For a strategy-specific assertion, add a method:

def test_my_alpha_inverts_funding(mock_data):
    alpha = MyAlpha(data=mock_data)
    w = alpha.gen_weights()
    # check the per-strategy invariant

docs.title: A new aggregator metric
docs.text: Add a fixture in tests/test_aggregators.py covering the new metric. The existing TestMarketDataAggregator / TestTradesAggregator / TestOrderbookAggregator classes are good templates.

docs.title: A new parser DTO
docs.text: Add a fixture in binance_parser/tests/test_models.py with a representative wire payload, then a test_parse_<thing>_fields assertion checking field-by-field deserialisation.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Use the mock fixtures. MockExchangeData for strategy-level tests, MockRawDataReader for pipeline-level tests. Don't ship tests that hit Binance.
  • Module-scoped fixtures for expensive setups. The pipeline fixture saves ~15 s per session.
  • No time.sleep. Use FakeBarClock (alpha_engine/live/bar_clock.py) for deterministic time-driven tests.
  • Document test intent in the docstring. "What invariant does this test, and why is it sufficient?" — not "what does the code do".

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
There's currently a .gitlab-ci.yml from a previous host. The repo now lives at github.com/SNCapital/-Backend; the GitLab pipeline file is unused. If you set up GitHub Actions, the simplest workflow is:

# .github/workflows/test.yml
name: tests
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: { python-version: "3.13" }
      - run: pip install -r requirements.txt -r binance_parser/requirements.txt
      - run: pytest

Removing .gitlab-ci.yml is a separate cleanup task — left alone here because nothing depends on it being absent.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Three pages, in order:

  1. Installation — Python 3.13, a venv, dependencies.
  2. Quick start — run a synthetic backtest, then a real one.
  3. Architecture — how the pieces fit together.

If you only have five minutes, jump straight to Quick start.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: A bird's-eye view of how the two packages plug together and where data flows.

docs.title: Two packages, one parquet contract
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  classDef pkg fill:#eef,stroke:#88a
  classDef store fill:#fff8e1,stroke:#a98
  classDef proc fill:#f0fff0,stroke:#8a8

  subgraph BP[binance_parser]
    direction TB
    WS[WebSocket\nspot + usdm streams]:::proc
    REST[REST funding poller\n8h cadence]:::proc
    OB[Local L2 order book\noptional]:::proc
    HIST[history downloader\ndata.binance.vision ZIPs]:::proc
    WR[FileWriter\nasync, batched, zstd]:::proc

    WS --> WR
    REST --> WR
    OB --> WR
    HIST --> WR
  end

  STORE[(data/<br/>market=…/type=…/dt=…/symbol=…/part-*.parquet)]:::store
  WR --> STORE

  subgraph AE[alpha_engine — backtest]
    direction TB
    READ[RawDataReader\nMultiFileParquetReader]:::proc
    AGG[Aggregators\nklines • orderbook • trades • funding]:::proc
    METR[ExchangeData / MetricsDict\nlazy 30-min DataFrames]:::proc
    STR[ALPHA_REGISTRY\n6 strategies]:::proc
    MK[markowitz_combine\nrolling Tobin tangency]:::proc
    PNL[compute_pnl\nfees + funding]:::proc

    READ --> AGG --> METR --> STR --> MK --> PNL
  end

  STORE --> READ

  subgraph LV[alpha_engine — live runtime]
    direction TB
    BUS[LiveTickBus\nin-process pub/sub]:::proc
    LR[LiveRawDataReader\nrolling deques per ticker]:::proc
    BC[BarClock\nUTC-aligned]:::proc
    EN[LiveEngine\nstep at every bar]:::proc

    BUS --> LR
    LR --> EN
    BC --> EN
  end

  WS -. tee .-> BUS
  STORE -. warm-start .-> LR

  class BP,AE,LV pkg

The parquet directory is the contract between the two packages. Either side can be replaced (write a new exchange parser, or write a new strategy framework) as long as it speaks Hive-partitioned parquet with the schemas in Storage layout.

docs.title: Three runtime modes
docs.text:
Mode Entry point Reader Cadence Backtest python tools/backtest.py … MultiFileParquetReader over ./data/ Vectorised, all-at-once Live signal python main.py live-trade … LiveRawDataReader (warm + WS) Once per bar (default 30 min) Data capture cd binance_parser && python main.py live … (alone) n/a — writer only Real-time

The backtest and live modes share the same strategy code: both call alpha_engine.pipeline.run_strategies(data, alpha_names, …) where data is an ExchangeData view. In backtest mode that view is hydrated all at once; in live mode it's hydrated per bar from rolling deques.

docs.title: Three layers in the strategy engine
docs.text:
graph LR
  L1["Layer 1 — Data<br/>RawDataReader → Aggregators → MetricsDict"]
  L2["Layer 2 — Strategies<br/>each ALPHA_REGISTRY entry → DataFrame(t × tickers)"]
  L3["Layer 3 — Combination<br/>Markowitz Tobin tangency → final weights"]
  L4["PnL — fees + funding"]

  L1 --> L2 --> L3 --> L4
  • Layer 1 is lazy. data["binance-f"]["mark_price"] triggers all kline aggregation for all tickers and caches per metric group. See Data layer.
  • Layer 2 strategies only see DataFrames. They never know whether it's mock data, parquet, or live — see Writing a strategy.
  • Layer 3 treats each strategy as an "asset". Rolling 30-day window, μ and Σ of strategy returns, closed-form Tobin tangency. See Markowitz combination.

docs.title: What lives where
docs.text:
backend/
├── main.py                          # CLI: `backtest` (default) and `live-trade`
├── conftest.py                      # makes binance_parser importable for pytest
├── pyproject.toml                   # pytest config + lint settings
│
├── alpha_engine/
│   ├── pipeline.py                  # AlphaPipeline, run_strategies, compute_pnl
│   ├── operators.py                 # ts_*, normalize, rank, set_entropy …
│   ├── metrics/                     # raw_data_reader, aggregators, metrics_dict
│   ├── strategies/                  # base.py + alphas.py + ALPHA_REGISTRY
│   ├── portfolio/markowitz.py       # _solve_markowitz + markowitz_combine
│   ├── backtest/                    # costs, turnover, plots
│   └── live/                        # service, engine, bar_clock, tick_bus, live_reader
│
├── binance_parser/
│   ├── main.py                      # parser CLI: live / history download / history funding
│   ├── config/                      # settings + pairs (601 + MAJOR 20)
│   ├── models/                      # WS DTOs, history rows, REST schemas, MarketType
│   ├── live/                        # ws_client, writer, orderbook, funding_poller
│   ├── history/downloader/          # urls, fetch, batch, funding_fetch

│
