docs.title: Sharp edges to know up front
docs.text:
• binance_parser uses bare imports (from config.settings import …). This is intentional — the package is its own runnable application. The root conftest.py and alpha_engine/live/service.py add the package to sys.path so it's still importable from outside. If you write new code that imports from the parser, copy the sys.path insertion or use the from binance_parser.… form (which also works).
  • 30-minute UTC-aligned bars are the universe everywhere. Lookbacks are expressed in bars (window=48*7 is one week).
  • Float32 prices, int64 ms timestamps in every parquet schema. The aggregators accept either timestamp or timestamp_ms and normalise.
  • Funding sign convention: positive funding ⇒ longs pay shorts. PnL subtracts funding · w so a long position with positive funding loses, matching USD-M reality.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Tool Version Python 3.13 (or newer) pip 24+ OS Linux / macOS — Windows works for the backtester, the live WS path is async-Linux-tested

The binance_parser package and the live runtime use the standard asyncio + websockets + aiohttp trio. The backtester is pure NumPy / pandas / pyarrow. Python 3.13 is required because the parser DTOs use modern type-hint syntax and pyarrow 18+ wheels.

Why not 3.11 / 3.12?

The parser uses from __future__ import annotations everywhere, but several modules rely on dataclass(slots=True, kw_only=True) and typing.Self ergonomically. Stick with the latest stable Python that doesn't force major library bumps — currently 3.13.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Recommended: a per-project virtualenv.

git clone https://github.com/SNCapital/-Backend.git backend
cd backend

python3.13 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

pip install -U pip
pip install -r requirements.txt -r binance_parser/requirements.txt

That installs everything for both packages — pandas, pyarrow, scipy, matplotlib for the backtester, and aiohttp / websockets / sortedcontainers for the parser.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the test suite from the repo root:

pytest

You should see roughly 100 passing tests, 0 failures, in ~25 seconds. If any fail, see Testing.

A non-trivial smoke test:

# 1-week synthetic backtest, single strategy, no plot.
python tools/backtest.py --mock --since 2024-01-01 --until 2024-01-08 \
                        --alphas funding_reversion --no-plot

You should get a printout that ends with a summary dict containing gross / net PnL, Sharpe, drawdown, and turnover.

docs.title: Optional: build the docs locally
docs.text:
These docs are built with MkDocs Material. The dev dependencies are not in requirements.txt — install them explicitly:

pip install 'mkdocs-material>=9.5' 'pymdown-extensions>=10'

mkdocs serve   # http://127.0.0.1:8000

To produce a static site (e.g. for GitHub Pages):

mkdocs build           # writes ./site/
mkdocs gh-deploy       # publishes to the gh-pages branch

docs.title: Optional: parser data directory
docs.text:
The CLI's default backtest (without --mock) expects parquet under ./data/ in the parser's Hive layout:

data/market={spot|usdm}/type=…/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol=…/part-*.parquet

You produce that by running the parser:

cd binance_parser
python main.py history download --market usdm --group major --months 1
python main.py history funding --months 12 --symbols BTCUSDT ETHUSDT

See Historical download for the full matrix of --market, --group, and --types.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: Five-minute path from clone to PnL plot.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/SNCapital/-Backend.git backend
cd backend

python3.13 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -U pip
pip install -r requirements.txt -r binance_parser/requirements.txt

(Full details: Installation.)

docs.title: 2. Synthetic backtest
docs.text:
The fastest way to see the pipeline run end-to-end:

python tools/backtest.py --mock \
    --since 2024-01-01 --until 2024-01-15 \
    --alphas funding_reversion trade_imbalance \
    --no-plot

Output ends with a summary like:

{'n_strategies': 2,
 'strategy_names': ['funding_reversion', 'trade_imbalance'],
 'n_tickers': 50,
 'n_timestamps': 673,
 'date_range': '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00:00 -> 2024-01-15 00:00:00+00:00',
 'mean_daily_turnover': 1.92,
 'median_daily_turnover': 1.74,
 'gross': {'total_pnl':  0.0008, 'annualized_sharpe': 0.41, 'max_drawdown': -0.004},
 'net':   {'total_pnl': -0.014,  'annualized_sharpe': -2.6, 'max_drawdown': -0.018}}

Drop --no-plot to get the matplotlib dashboard (cumulative PnL, drawdown, weight heat-map, turnover, allocations).

docs.title: 3. Real-data backtest
docs.text:
You need parquet under ./data/. Easiest way: download a month of USD-M klines and a year of funding rates:

cd binance_parser

python main.py history download --market usdm --group major --months 1
python main.py history funding --months 12

cd ..

That gives you data/market=usdm/type=klines/... and data/market=usdm/type=funding/.... Now point the backtester at it:

python tools/backtest.py \
    --since 2025-01-01 --until 2025-04-01 \
    --alphas funding_reversion \
    --data-root data

This reads the Hive-partitioned parquet directly — no copy step.

docs.title: 4. Live signal-only loop
docs.text:
Phase 1 logs target weights at every bar boundary; no orders are placed.

python main.py live-trade \
    --alphas trade_imbalance funding_reversion \
    --symbols BTCUSDT ETHUSDT \
    --market usdm \
    --bar-minutes 30

You'll see lines like:

2026-04-26 14:00:02 INFO [alpha_engine.live.engine] LiveEngine.step
  2026-04-26 14:00:00+00:00 — bar #1, 2 strategies, gross=0.0512, n_nonzero=2

The parser warm-starts from any parquets it finds in ./data/, then keeps reading from the WebSocket bus. The local L2 order book is on by default — disable it with --no-order-book if you only need trade/kline-driven strategies (e.g. just funding_reversion).

docs.title: OpenSpec specs
docs.text:
Machine-checkable requirement-level contracts, rendered from openspec/specs/**/spec.md by tools/render_openspec_docs.py.

Capability Description Historical download openspec/specs/historical-download/spec.md Live WebSocket pipeline openspec/specs/live-ws/spec.md Data models openspec/specs/models/spec.md REST pollers openspec/specs/rest-pollers/spec.md

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Defines the historical bulk-download pipeline of binance_parser: the history CLI entry point, per-market endpoint address resolution, klines and aggTrades download loops, pagination and size limits, HTTP retry and rate-limit behavior, deduplication, and row-level schema mapping. It covers the classical CLI (binance_parser/main.py history) and the one-shot tool (binance_parser/tools/history.py).

docs.title: Requirement: History CLI contract
docs.text: The system SHALL expose a history subcommand accepting --market (spot|usdm|both, default spot) and --symbols (comma-separated, default BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT), with support for fetching both klines and aggTrades data types. The download SHALL proceed until end-of-history and SHALL be resumable.

docs.title: Scenario: Default history run
docs.text:
• WHEN the history command is run with no flags
  • THEN it downloads spot klines for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT

docs.title: Scenario: Resume after interruption
docs.text:
• WHEN a history run is interrupted and restarted
  • THEN it resumes from where it stopped rather than re-downloading from the start

docs.title: Requirement: Endpoint address resolution
docs.text: The system SHALL resolve klines and aggTrades base URLs per market from the model's venue maps: spot history base https://data-api.binance.vision/, spot market history path data/spot/daily/, usdm history base https://data.binance.vision/, usdm market history path data/futures/usdt/daily/. The resulting download URLs SHALL take the form <base><market-path><data-type>/<SYMBOL>/<SYMBOL>-<data-type>-<date>.zip, where dates are the earliest end-date start and walk backward.

docs.title: Scenario: Resolved spot URL shape
docs.text:
• WHEN a spot klines URL is resolved for BTCUSDT on 2024-03-01
  • THEN the URL is https://data-api.binance.vision/data/spot/daily/klines/BTCUSDT/BTCUSDT-klines-2024-03-01.zip

docs.title: Scenario: Resolved usdm URL shape
docs.text:
• WHEN a usdm aggTrades URL is resolved for ETHUSDT on 2024-03-01
  • THEN the URL is https://data.binance.vision/data/futures/usdt/daily/aggTrades/ETHUSDT/ETHUSDT-aggTrades-2024-03-01.zip

docs.title: Requirement: Klines download loop
docs.text: The system SHALL download klines day by day with adjustable lookback. Each daily file SHALL be zipped with a CSV of rows (open time, open, high, low, close, volume, close time, quote volume, count, taker buy volume, taker buy quote volume, ignore), deduplicated by open time, and written as parquet in data/market={m}/type=klines/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol={SYM}/part-*.parquet. The loop SHALL stop at the earliest date before the current date (end-of-history detection) and SHALL print a log line per successfully written day.

docs.title: Scenario: Daily file dedup
docs.text:
• WHEN a daily klines file contains duplicate open times
  • THEN duplicates are removed before writing

docs.title: Scenario: End-of-history stop
docs.text:
• WHEN the loop reaches the earliest available date
  • THEN it stops and reports completion

docs.title: Requirement: AggTrades download loop
docs.text: The system SHALL download aggTrades day by day with a hard cap of 100,000 rows per day. When a day exceeds the cap, the system SHALL fall back to the REST API for the whole day (with native pagination and 1000-row pages), and when the REST fallback also exceeds the 100,000 cap, the day SHALL be split into hour ranges and downloaded per hour. Each daily file SHALL be deduplicated by aggregate trade id, converted row-wise from the CSV to the schema's aggTrades column set, and written as parquet in data/market={m}/type=aggTrades/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol={SYM}/part-*.parquet.

docs.title: Scenario: CSV cap fallback
docs.text:
• WHEN a daily aggTrades file exceeds 100,000 rows
  • THEN the day is re-downloaded from the REST API with pagination

docs.title: Scenario: REST cap hour split
docs.text:
• WHEN the REST fallback for a day also exceeds 100,000 rows
  • THEN the day is downloaded in per-hour ranges

docs.title: Scenario: aggTrades dedup
docs.text:
• WHEN a daily file contains duplicate aggregate trade ids
  • THEN duplicates are removed before writing

docs.title: Scenario: Row-wise CSV mapping
docs.text:
• WHEN a CSV row is written
  • THEN its fields are mapped in row order to the schema's aggTrades columns (aggregate trade id, price, quantity, first trade id, last trade id, timestamp, buyer maker flag, best price match flag)

docs.title: Requirement: HTTP client policy
docs.text: The system SHALL use a shared HTTP session with Retry-After honoring on 429/418, exponential backoff (1, 2, 4 seconds) on connect errors, and a maximum of 3 retries. Failed downloads SHALL be retried at the next invocation (resume), and requests SHALL rate-limit globally via the shared rate limiter where applicable. Out-of-window dates SHALL be treated as end-of-history (not errors).

docs.title: Scenario: Rate-limited download pause
docs.text:
• WHEN a download receives 429 with a Retry-After header
  • THEN the client waits that long, plus a random 5-30 second jitter, before retrying

docs.title: Scenario: Missing day is end-of-history
docs.text:
• WHEN a requested date is beyond the venue's earliest data window
  • THEN the download treats it as end-of-history and stops, without raising an error

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Defines the live WebSocket pipeline of binance_parser: the live CLI entry point, per-market subscription sets, connection and reconnect policy, stream dispatch to parquet, buffered writer semantics, local order-book lifecycle and snapshots, health/stats accounting, and task composition of the live run.

docs.title: Requirement: Live CLI contract
docs.text: The system SHALL expose a live subcommand accepting --market (spot|usdm|both, default spot), --symbols (space-separated, default BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT, upper-cased), --order-book (flag), and --with-funding (flag). The command SHALL run until interrupted, and a keyboard interrupt SHALL stop it with exit code 0.

docs.title: Scenario: Default live run
docs.text:
• WHEN the live command is run with no flags
  • THEN it starts a spot-market pipeline for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT without the order book or funding poller

docs.title: Scenario: Symbols upper-cased
docs.text:
• WHEN symbols are passed in lowercase
  • THEN the pipeline operates on the upper-cased symbols

docs.title: Requirement: Stream subscription sets
docs.text: The system SHALL subscribe per symbol, per market, to a fixed stream set: always @depth, @aggTrade, and @kline_1m; plus, on usdm only, @markPrice@1s and (when enabled) @forceOrder. The raw @trade stream SHALL be subscribed only when trades are preferred over aggregate trades (or multilevel reconstruction is enabled); by default it is not subscribed and aggregate trades are the canonical trade source.

docs.title: Scenario: Default spot subscription
docs.text:
• WHEN a spot listener starts for a symbol with default settings
  • THEN exactly @depth, @aggTrade, and @kline_1m streams are subscribed

docs.title: Scenario: Default usdm subscription
docs.text:
• WHEN a usdm listener starts for a symbol with default settings
  • THEN @depth, @aggTrade, @kline_1m, @markPrice@1s, and @forceOrder are subscribed

docs.title: Scenario: Raw trades opt-in
docs.text:
• WHEN aggregate-trade preference is disabled
  • THEN @trade is additionally subscribed and raw fills are written as trades events alongside aggtrades

docs.title: Requirement: WebSocket persistence semantics
docs.text: The system SHALL persist via the writer only: aggtrades, closed klines, markprice (usdm), forceorder (usdm, when enabled), trades (when subscribed), and booksnapshot (order-book snapshots). Depth diffs SHALL never be persisted: they feed only the in-process order book and health counters. Running (unclosed) klines and unknown streams SHALL be dropped silently.

docs.title: Scenario: Depth diff bypass
docs.text:
• WHEN a @depth message arrives and an order-book manager is present
  • THEN it is routed to the book manager and health counters only, and the writer is never invoked

docs.title: Scenario: Depth-diff debug logging hook
docs.text:
• WHEN the depth-log interval setting is configured to a positive value
  • THEN the first and then every Nth depth diff per stream is logged at debug level

docs.title: Scenario: Silent unknown-stream drop
docs.text:
• WHEN a message matches no known stream
  • THEN it is ignored without failing the connection

docs.title: Requirement: WebSocket reconnect policy
docs.text: The system SHALL reconnect a closed or failed connection with exponential backoff starting at 1 second and doubling, capped at 60 seconds, reset to 1 on any successful connection. The connection SHALL keep an application-level heartbeat (ping every 20 seconds, timeout 10 seconds, close timeout 5 seconds). After 30 consecutive reconnect failures the listener SHALL raise an error to its supervisor instead of retrying forever. Unexpected (non-network) exceptions SHALL propagate immediately, never being masked as reconnects. Every reconnect except the first SHALL be recorded with the disconnection gap.

docs.title: Scenario: Backoff reset on success
docs.text:
• WHEN a connection attempt succeeds after prior failures
  • THEN the backoff timer resets to 1 second and the failure counter clears

docs.title: Scenario: Give-up escalation
docs.text:
• WHEN 30 consecutive reconnect attempts fail
  • THEN the listener raises a runtime error describing the failure count

docs.title: Scenario: Code error escalation
docs.text:
• WHEN a frame handler raises an unexpected exception
  • THEN the exception propagates immediately and the loop does not attempt a reconnect

docs.title: Requirement: Buffered parquet writer
docs.text: The system SHALL buffer records in memory and flush them to parquet under a Hive-partitioned layout: data/market={m}/type={t}/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol={SYM}/part-*.parquet. Flush SHALL trigger when the total buffered record count reaches 100,000 or a 60-second timer elapses. At flush, records SHALL be grouped by their own event-UTC-date so buckets straddling midnight land in the correct dt= partition. Writes SHALL use zstd compression (level 3), write to a sibling temp file, and atomically replace the target path. A failed partition write SHALL be retried (3 attempts, escalating backoff) and the failure SHALL be raised after the flush completes the remaining partitions.

docs.title: Scenario: Midnight partition correctness
docs.text:
• WHEN a flush contains records whose event times fall on different UTC dates
  • THEN each record lands in the parquet file of its own event date partition

docs.title: Scenario: Atomic part write
docs.text:
• WHEN a parquet part is written
  • THEN it is first written to a temporary sibling file and then atomically renamed, so a crash never leaves a corrupt file at the canonical path

docs.title: Scenario: Flush by record count
docs.text:
• WHEN the total buffered record count reaches 100,000 before the 60-second timer
  • THEN a flush occurs immediately

docs.title: Requirement: Order-book state lifecycle
docs.text: The system SHALL maintain one in-memory order book per (market, symbol), seeded from a REST depth snapshot and kept in sync with @depth diffs. The book SHALL have states bootstrapping, live, and resyncing. Spot and usdm SHALL apply the venue-specific contiguity rules: spot drops diffs with u <= snapshot id, bridges when U <= snapshot id + 1 <= u, and requires U == previous u + 1; usdm drops diffs with u < snapshot id, bridges when U <= snapshot id <= u, and requires pu == previous u. A level with quantity zero SHALL remove the level. A non-contiguous live diff SHALL move the book to resyncing and re-bootstrap.

docs.title: Scenario: Level removal by zero quantity
docs.text:
• WHEN a diff carries a level with quantity zero
  • THEN the corresponding price level is removed from the book

docs.title: Scenario: Gap triggers resync
docs.text:
• WHEN a live diff is not contiguous with the previous one
  • THEN the book transitions to resyncing, the gap is counted, and a re-bootstrap is scheduled

docs.title: Scenario: Usdm overlapping ranges tolerated
docs.text:
• WHEN a usdm diff overlaps the previous range instead of extending it exactly
  • THEN the diff is applied and the book remains live (usdm contiguity is defined by pu)

docs.title: Scenario: Diff observers
docs.text:
• WHEN observers are registered on a live book and a diff arrives
  • THEN each observer is invoked before the diff is applied, with the touched price levels and the mid price; an observer failure is logged and never interrupts the dispatch loop

docs.title: Requirement: Order-book bootstrap
docs.text: The system SHALL bootstrap a book by fetching the venue's deepest snapshot (spot up to 5000 levels, usdm up to 1000), then replaying buffered diffs sorted by final update id: stale diffs dropped, the first surviving diff must bridge the snapshot, and subsequent diffs must be contiguous, else bootstrap repeats. Cold-start snapshot fetches SHALL be staggered per symbol (spot 2.5s, usdm 0.5s) with at most 2 concurrent fetches. USD-M snapshot fetches SHALL charge the shared rate limiter (weight 20 at max depth); spot bootstrap in the standalone run passes no limiter and relies on the stagger plus the concurrency cap. A 200 response without lastUpdateId (delisted or renamed symbol) SHALL raise an error that is absorbed by the retry backoff. Rate-limit responses SHALL be honored via Retry-After plus 5-30 seconds of jitter; other failures SHALL back off exponentially to 30 seconds.

docs.title: Scenario: Snapshot-limited bootstrap
docs.text:
• WHEN a book cannot bridge the snapshot with the buffered diffs
  • THEN bootstrap is retried after a fixed 2-second wait and the book stays bootstrapping

docs.title: Scenario: Rate-limited bootstrap wait
docs.text:
• WHEN a depth snapshot fetch returns 429 or 418
  • THEN the retry sleeps for the response's Retry-After plus a random 5-30 second jitter

docs.title: Scenario: Buffered diffs after failed bridge
docs.text:
• WHEN a bootstrap attempt fails contiguity after applying the bridging diff
  • THEN the buffered diffs are discarded and the next bootstrap re-seeds from a fresh snapshot (only the no-bridge case keeps the buffer)

docs.title: Scenario: Watchdog force-resync
docs.text:
• WHEN a live book receives no diffs for more than 30 seconds, or a resyncing book stays resyncing for more than 60 seconds
  • THEN the watchdog forces a resync and counts it

docs.title: Requirement: Order-book snapshots
docs.text: The system SHALL persist the full book (bids and asks as parallel float32 price/size arrays, one row per event, carrying also the symbol, snapshot timestamp, and the book's last update id) into type=booksnapshot partitions at a UTC-aligned cadence of 30 minutes (configurable; zero disables persistence), i.e. at :00 and :30 UTC, 48 snapshots per symbol per day. Only books in live state SHALL be snapshotted; a half-bootstrapped book SHALL be skipped. A separate 1-second in-process bus snapshot loop SHALL exist for metric consumers and SHALL never touch disk; it is not started in standalone parser runs.

docs.title: Scenario: UTC-aligned snapshot ticks
docs.text:
• WHEN the snapshot loop runs with the default 30-minute interval
  • THEN snapshots are written at :00 and :30 UTC regardless of process start time

docs.title: Scenario: Unready book skipped
docs.text:
• WHEN a book is not in live state at snapshot time
  • THEN no snapshot row is written for it for that tick

docs.title: Scenario: Snapshot persistence disabled
docs.text:
• WHEN the snapshot interval is set to zero
  • THEN no booksnapshot parquet files are written and a notice is printed

docs.title: Requirement: Health and pipeline statistics
docs.text: The system SHALL track health counters (trade-id gaps - incremented when a trade id is not exactly the previous plus one; WS reconnects; order-book force resyncs; clock-drift alerts) plus per-symbol last-event timestamps. It SHALL expose a snapshot of these counters for external scraping. The pipeline SHALL report periodic statistics: message counts and lag per stream, reconnect count, and depth-resync counts per symbol, reported every 60 seconds; a high-frequency stream (aggtrades) that has never delivered a message, or whose lag exceeds 10 times its 30-second threshold (i.e. 300 seconds), SHALL trigger a warning.

docs.title: Scenario: Trade id gap detection
docs.text:
• WHEN a trade arrives whose id is not the previously seen id plus one
  • THEN the trade-id-gap counter increments and a warning is logged

docs.title: Scenario: Silent stream warning
docs.text:
• WHEN the aggtrades stream has never received a message after the first report, or its lag exceeds 300 seconds (10 times its 30-second threshold)
  • THEN the reporter logs a stream-silent or stream-lag warning

docs.title: Requirement: Live run composition
docs.text: The system SHALL run the live pipeline as a task group sharing one writer, one stats object, one health object, and one shared USD-M rate limiter across all components. It SHALL start, per selected market: a WS listener; on usdm, the exchange-info poller and market-stats poller; and, conditionally: the order-book manager and its snapshot/watchdog loops (--order-book), the funding poller (--with-funding, usdm only, ignored with a printed notice otherwise), the legacy periodic metrics pollers (when enabled), and the spot margin-interest poller (when enabled and spot is selected). Symbol validation against exchange-info SHALL be a soft check: network, timeout, and JSON-parse failures, as well as invalid symbols, SHALL warn but never abort (non-network parse bugs SHALL still propagate). The first task exception SHALL cancel all sibling tasks.

docs.title: Scenario: Funding flag without usdm
docs.text:
• WHEN --with-funding is set but usdm is not among the markets
  • THEN the flag is ignored with a printed notice and no funding poller starts

docs.title: Scenario: Soft symbol validation
docs.text:
• WHEN the exchange-info validation request fails or a symbol is not trading
  • THEN the pipeline continues with a warning

docs.title: Scenario: First-exception cancels all
docs.text:
• WHEN any task in the group fails
  • THEN all sibling tasks are cancelled and the failure propagates out of the run

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Defines the typed data contracts of binance_parser: market abstraction, live WebSocket DTOs, historical row schemas, REST response DTOs, and the shared rate limiter that all Binance-facing callers rely on.

docs.title: Requirement: Market abstraction
docs.text: The system SHALL model a market as one of exactly two values: spot or usdm (USD-M perpetual futures). All venue-specific URLs (WebSocket base, REST base, exchange-info path, depth-snapshot path, history base) SHALL be defined per market in single configuration maps. CLI parsing of a market argument SHALL accept spot, usdm, or both (expands to both markets); any other value SHALL be rejected with an error.

docs.title: Scenario: CLI market parsing
docs.text:
• WHEN the market argument is both
  • THEN the system resolves it to the ordered list ["spot", "usdm"]

docs.title: Scenario: Invalid market value
docs.text:
• WHEN the market argument is not spot, usdm, or both
  • THEN the system raises a ValueError naming the offending value

docs.title: Scenario: Adding a new market
docs.text:
• WHEN a new market value is introduced
  • THEN it requires a corresponding entry in the five venue-specific configuration maps; other REST endpoints (funding, exchange-info, market-stats, margin interest) remain fixed constants outside the maps

docs.title: Requirement: Live WebSocket DTOs
docs.text: The system SHALL deserialize every subscribed Binance stream event into a typed DTO with a fixed pyarrow schema. Every DTO SHALL expose its schema, an event_type identifier, and a row serializer for parquet persistence. All timestamps SHALL be int64 milliseconds; wire-derived timestamps are UTC, and a depth event without a wire timestamp falls back to the local clock, while a mark-price event prefers the event time E over T. Price and quantity columns SHALL be float32, except mark-price fields which SHALL be float64.

docs.title: Scenario: Depth diff DTO
docs.text:
• WHEN a @depth payload is parsed
  • THEN it becomes an orderbook event carrying symbol, event timestamp, first/last/previous update ids, and parallel bid/ask price and size lists, and is dispatched to the in-memory book only - never persisted as a row

docs.title: Scenario: Depth diff market difference
docs.text:
• WHEN a @depth payload arrives on spot
  • THEN the previous-update id is always null (spot diffs carry no pu), while usdm diffs carry it

docs.title: Scenario: Trade DTO
docs.text:
• WHEN a @trade payload is parsed
  • THEN it becomes a trades event with trade id, timestamp, price, quantity, and side (buy when the payload's m flag is falsy, else sell)

docs.title: Scenario: AggTrade DTO
docs.text:
• WHEN an @aggTrade payload is parsed
  • THEN it becomes an aggtrades event with aggregate trade id, first/last constituent trade ids, timestamp, price, quantity, and side

docs.title: Scenario: Mark price DTO
docs.text:
• WHEN a @markPrice@1s payload is parsed
  • THEN it becomes a markprice event with mark price, index price, predicted funding rate (all float64), and next funding time

docs.title: Scenario: Liquidation DTO
docs.text:
• WHEN a @forceOrder payload is parsed
  • THEN it becomes a forceorder event whose fields are read from the nested o object, with the side mapped from uppercase BUY/other to buy/sell

docs.title: Scenario: Kline DTO
docs.text:
• WHEN a closed @kline_<interval> payload is parsed
  • THEN it becomes a klines event with open/close times, OHLCV, quote volume, taker-buy volumes, trade count (int32), and closed flag

docs.title: Requirement: Stream event dispatch
docs.text: The system SHALL map a raw stream message to its DTO by substring matching on the stream name, in a fixed precedence order: @depth, then @markPrice, then @aggTrade, then @forceOrder, then @trade, then @kline. Messages whose stream matches none of these SHALL be rejected as unknown (the rejection is a ValueError subclass); a @kline payload whose bar is not yet closed SHALL also be rejected as unknown (running bars are dropped).

docs.title: Scenario: Dispatch precedence of force order over trade
docs.text:
• WHEN a stream name contains both @forceOrder and @trade
  • THEN the payload is parsed as a forceorder event, not a trades event

docs.title: Scenario: Running kline rejection
docs.text:
• WHEN a @kline payload has its x (closed) flag false
  • THEN the system rejects the message as an unknown running-kline stream and it is not persisted

docs.title: Requirement: Historical row schemas
docs.text: The system SHALL define pyarrow schemas for historical archive rows: klines (11 columns, trades int32), aggTrades, trades, bookTicker, and funding rate. These schemas SHALL be available in a registry keyed by archive data type, and SHALL map to pandas read dtypes for CSV ingestion. All timestamps SHALL be int64 milliseconds UTC; prices and quantities float32.

docs.title: Scenario: Schema registry coverage
docs.text:
• WHEN a historical data type is klines, aggTrades, trades, bookTicker, or funding
  • THEN a schema exists for it in the registry

docs.title: Scenario: CSV dtype mapping
docs.text:
• WHEN pandas dtypes are derived from a schema for CSV reading
  • THEN bool columns are excluded from the mapping so they are not coerced to object strings during read

docs.title: Requirement: Funding rate row
docs.text: The system SHALL parse REST funding-rate records into a funding row with symbol, funding time (ms), funding rate (float32), and optional mark price (float32, null when absent). The symbol and funding time are required keys in the source payload.

docs.title: Scenario: Funding row with mark price
docs.text:
• WHEN a REST record contains fundingTime, fundingRate, and markPrice
  • THEN the parsed row carries all four fields and serializes to a single row dict

docs.title: Scenario: Funding row without mark price
docs.text:
• WHEN a REST record omits markPrice
  • THEN the parsed row has a null mark price and still serializes successfully

docs.title: Requirement: REST exchange metadata DTOs
docs.text: The system SHALL parse exchange-info payloads into a per-symbol row with symbol, status, contract type, tick size (from PRICE_FILTER), step size (from LOT_SIZE), min notional (from MIN_NOTIONAL, falling back to NOTIONAL variants), max leverage (maximum initialLeverage across leverage brackets), maintenance margin rate (of the lowest bracket), default maker/taker fees, and the full leverage-bracket curve. Missing filters SHALL become NaN; missing brackets SHALL yield zero max leverage, NaN maintenance margin rate, and an empty bracket list.

docs.title: Scenario: Spot vs USD-M notional shape
docs.text:
• WHEN the source payload exposes min notional only through the NOTIONAL filter
  • THEN the system falls back to that filter's minNotional and then notional field

docs.title: Scenario: No leverage brackets
docs.text:
• WHEN a symbol has no leverage-bracket data
  • THEN its row has max leverage 0, maintenance margin rate NaN, and an empty bracket list

docs.title: Requirement: Market-stats REST rows
docs.text: The system SHALL parse five distinct market-statistics responses into rows with namespaced columns and float64 numeric fields: open interest now, global long/short account ratio, top long/short account ratio, top long/short position ratio, and spot margin daily interest rate. Ratio and quantity strings in responses SHALL be cast to float; column names SHALL be namespaced by the source endpoint so identical concepts from different endpoints do not collide; event types SHALL be distinct from the legacy periodic-metrics event types.

docs.title: Scenario: Symbol absent from ratio payloads
docs.text:
• WHEN the global/top long-short payloads do not carry the symbol
  • THEN the caller injects the symbol into the row during parsing

docs.title: Scenario: Hourly to daily interest rescale
docs.text:
• WHEN a spot margin payload provides the next hourly interest rate
  • THEN the parsed row stores the rate multiplied by 24 as a daily rate

docs.title: Requirement: Legacy periodic futures metrics
docs.text: The system SHALL parse three /futures/data/ responses (open-interest history, taker long/short ratio, top long/short position ratio) into rows that keep numeric values as strings, with all columns non-nullable: open_interest, taker_ratio, and long_short_ratio events. These SHALL use event types distinct from the market-stats rows and SHALL persist sum_open_interest, sum_open_interest_value, buy_sell_ratio, buy_vol, sell_vol, long_short_ratio, long_account, and short_account as string columns.

docs.title: Scenario: Taker ratio symbol injection
docs.text:
• WHEN a taker-ratio payload omits the symbol (Binance does not include it)
  • THEN the fetch helper injects the symbol into the row before parsing

docs.title: Scenario: Numeric strings preserved
docs.text:
• WHEN a /futures/data/ response contains a numeric value
  • THEN the row keeps it as its original string representation, never casting to float

docs.title: Requirement: Rate limiter
docs.text: The system SHALL throttle Binance REST requests with token-bucket limiters. A multi-bucket limiter SHALL route each request to the first bucket whose pattern is a substring of the request URL, with an empty-string pattern as the catch-all default; an empty bucket list SHALL be rejected at construction, and a request matching no bucket at all SHALL trip an internal assertion. The canonical USD-M limiter SHALL provide a /futures/data/ bucket of 400 weight per 300 seconds and a default bucket of 2000 weight per 60 seconds. A request costing more than a bucket's capacity SHALL be rejected with an error.

docs.title: Scenario: URL-to-bucket routing
docs.text:
• WHEN a request URL contains /futures/data/
  • THEN it is charged to the 400-weight/300-second bucket, and all other URLs to the 2000-weight/60-second bucket

docs.title: Scenario: Bucket exhaustion waits
docs.text:
• WHEN a bucket lacks tokens for a request
  • THEN the limiter sleeps until enough tokens refill before releasing the request

docs.title: Scenario: Over-capacity cost
docs.text:
• WHEN a request costs more than the target bucket's capacity
  • THEN the limiter raises an error rather than waiting

docs.title: Requirement: Rate-limit error semantics
docs.text: The system SHALL treat HTTP 429 (rate limited) and 418 (IP banned) as rate-limit responses: parse Retry-After from headers (falling back to 60 seconds), and cap consecutive rate-limit waits per REST call at 3.

docs.title: Scenario: Retry-After parsing
docs.text:
• WHEN a rate-limit response carries a Retry-After header
  • THEN the system uses that value as the wait duration, defaulting to 60 seconds when absent or malformed

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Defines the REST polling pipelines of binance_parser that run alongside the live WebSocket listener: exchange metadata (exchangeInfo), funding-rate, market-stats, and the legacy periodic-metrics pollers. It pins the polling cadences, retry and rate-limit behavior, shared poller utilities, and the keychain of periodic-metrics endpoints that the metrics engine consumes.

docs.title: Requirement: Exchange-info poller
docs.text: The system SHALL poll the per-market exchange-info endpoint every 6 hours per market, parse the response, and persist the resulting rows as parquet in data/market={m}/type=exchangeinfo/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol={SYM}/part-*.parquet. Polls SHALL be scheduled with a small random jitter at startup; two polls of the same market SHALL never run concurrently (a failed poll SHALL be retried once after 60 seconds, and a poll that is still running when its next tick arrives SHALL be skipped). Only USD-M SHALL be polled by default; spot SHALL be polled only when explicitly enabled. Spot polling SHALL be scheduled through the shared generic poller utilities, while USD-M polling is managed directly by the live-run orchestrator.

docs.title: Scenario: Skewed market schedules
docs.text:
• WHEN both spot and usdm exchange-info polling are enabled
  • THEN the two markets poll at the same 6-hour cadence but with different startup jitter, so their requests never align

docs.title: Scenario: Spot opt-in default
docs.text:
• WHEN a live run starts without explicit spot exchange-info enablement
  • THEN only USD-M exchange-info is polled

docs.title: Requirement: Funding-rate poller
docs.text: The system SHALL poll the USD-M funding-rate endpoint every 30 minutes at a fixed offset of :07 minutes past each half-hour, across the configured symbol set (default BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT). Each symbol SHALL be polled with an independent initial offset (scattered across the minute), and a poll of a symbol that is still running SHALL be skipped. The poller SHALL deduplicate by (symbol, fundingTime) and retry on rate-limit responses per the shared retry policy.

docs.title: Scenario: Fixed half-hour offset
docs.text:
• WHEN the funding poller wakes on its 30-minute cadence
  • THEN the poll for every symbol is issued at :07 minutes past the half-hour boundary

docs.title: Scenario: Duplicate funding row
docs.text:
• WHEN two polls return the same (symbol, fundingTime)
  • THEN only the first row is persisted

docs.title: Requirement: Market-stats poller
docs.text: The system SHALL poll, for the configured symbol set (default BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT), the four endpoints open-interest, global long/short account ratio, top long/short account ratio, and top long/short position ratio. All four SHALL share one cadence; the poller SHALL be evenly spread (scatter) across the cadence window and SHALL skip a symbol whose previous poll is still running. USD-M status filters SHALL follow the exchange-info state from USD-M exchange metadata (spot always open). Polled rows SHALL be persisted via the shared buffered writer under type=marketstats with event-type tags distinguishing the four endpoints; values that fail to cast to float SHALL persist as NaN.

docs.title: Scenario: Scattered symbol polls
docs.text:
• WHEN the market-stats poller runs a cycle
  • THEN the four endpoints for a symbol are spread evenly across the cadence window rather than fired in a burst

docs.title: Scenario: Non-numeric ratio value
docs.text:
• WHEN a market-stats endpoint returns a value that cannot be cast to float
  • THEN the row is persisted with NaN for that value

docs.title: Scenario: Long/short ratio cadence pairing
docs.text:
• WHEN the top long/short ratio and top long/short position ratio are enabled
  • THEN both poll at the same cadence with the same scatter

docs.title: Requirement: Poller session and retry policy
docs.text: All REST pollers SHALL share a common session and retry policy: an adaptive Retry-After honorer, exponential backoff (1, 2, 4 seconds) on connect errors, and a maximum of 3 retries per poll. Rate-limit responses SHALL be honored via Retry-After plus a random 5-30 second jitter. Non-retryable HTTP errors (4xx other than 429/418) SHALL be logged as permanent failures without retry.

docs.title: Scenario: Connect-error backoff
docs.text:
• WHEN a poll fails with a connection error
  • THEN it is retried at 1, then 2, then 4 seconds, stopping after the third failure

docs.title: Scenario: HTTP 403 permanent
docs.text:
• WHEN a poll returns 403
  • THEN it is logged as a permanent failure and not retried

docs.title: Requirement: Generic poller utilities
docs.text: The system SHALL provide a reusable periodic-poll utility: given a cadence, a task per symbol, and a spread parameter, it SHALL cycle each symbol through running, waiting, and error states, with an until option limiting total runtime. Errors SHALL be logged with symbol and error context. A poller constructed with zero symbols SHALL print a notice and exit.

docs.title: Scenario: Poller idle on zero symbols
docs.text:
• WHEN a poller is constructed with an empty symbol set
  • THEN it prints a notice and exits immediately

docs.title: Scenario: Finite poller run
docs.text:
• WHEN a poller is given an until deadline
  • THEN it stops after the deadline rather than running forever

docs.title: Requirement: Periodic-metrics keychain
docs.text: The system SHALL implement a keychain of legacy periodic-metrics pollers, each polling its own endpoint on a distinct cadence: open-interest history (1 hour, _5m granularity), taker long/short ratio (1 hour, _5m granularity), top long/short position ratio (1 hour, _5m granularity), global long/short account ratio (6 hours, _1h granularity), top long/short account ratio (6 hours, _1h granularity), and spot margin borrow/repay interest history (1 hour, _1d granularity). Each poller SHALL deduplicate rows by (symbol, timestamp), share a single session, and retry with the shared policy. The pollers SHALL expose an internal state object with per-symbol timestamps so callers (metrics engine) can inspect each poller's progress without re-deriving it. Each poller SHALL expose its most recent result (rows plus timestamp) in a single internal dict, stored at the object level, so consumers read exactly what the poller last produced.

docs.title: Scenario: Granularity aliases
docs.text:
• WHEN a periodic-metrics poller requests data with granularity _1m
  • THEN the actual Binance endpoint granularity used is the 5-minute alias _5m (klines are 5-minute)

docs.title: Scenario: Poller state query
docs.text:
• WHEN the metrics engine queries a periodic-metrics poller's state
  • THEN it reads the last-result dict (rows and timestamp) without re-deriving or re-polling

docs.title: Scenario: Row deduplication
docs.text:
• WHEN a poller polls a symbol whose latest timestamp already exists
  • THEN the duplicate row is skipped

docs.title: CLI
docs.text: Entry points — root main.py (live trader), tools/ (offline tools) and binance_parser/main.py (data pipeline).

docs.title: Root — alpha engine (live trader only)
docs.text:
python main.py [-h] {live-trade}

If no subcommand is given (python main.py, python main.py --market usdm), defaults to live-trade.

docs.title: live-trade
docs.text:
Phase 1 — signal-only loop. Logs target weights at each bar boundary; no orders.

python main.py live-trade [-h]
    [--alphas …] [--symbols SYM …]
    [--bar-minutes N] [--settlement-seconds F] [--lookback-days N]
    [--max-w F] [--end-range N]
    [--market {spot,usdm}]
    [--no-order-book] [--snapshot-interval-ms MS]
    [--data-root DIR] [--log-level LEVEL]
Flag Default Meaning --alphas trade_imbalance Strategy keys to evaluate per bar. --symbols parser's SYMBOLS Tickers to subscribe / consider. --bar-minutes 30 Bar cadence; 30 matches the backtest. --settlement-seconds 5.0 Wait this many seconds past each bar boundary before evaluating. Absorbs WS-reconnect latency; tick arriving later goes into the next bar. --lookback-days 30 Rolling window for features and warm-start. --max-w 0.03 Per-ticker weight cap. --end-range 50 Top-N tickers by volume per strategy. --market spot spot or usdm. --no-order-book off (book on) Skip the local L2 book + snapshot loop. --snapshot-interval-ms parser default (1000) Override snapshot cadence. --data-root ./data Warm-start parquet root. --log-level INFO Python logging level.

Examples:

# USD-M, single strategy, no book
python main.py live-trade --market usdm --alphas funding_reversion --no-order-book

# Spot, two strategies, debug logs
python main.py live-trade --alphas trade_imbalance ob_mispricing --log-level DEBUG

Full description: Live trading.

docs.title: Backtest — tool
docs.text:
Moved out of main.py; the offline backtest runs as a tool:

python tools/backtest.py [-h]
    [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD]
    [--alphas {ob_mispricing,vol_ob_entropy,funding_reversion,
               trade_imbalance,vol_mean_reversion,book_depth_imbalance} ...]
    [--data-root DATA_ROOT] [--mock] [--metrics-roots ROOTS …]
    [--tickers SYM …] [--execution {close,vwap}]
    [--max-w F] [--fee-bps F] [--slippage-bps F] [--spread-default-bps F]
    [--combine {markowitz,risk_parity,ew}]
    [--max-strategy-weight F] [--alloc-lookback-days N]
    [--no-plot] [--log-level LEVEL]
Flag Default Meaning --since 2023-06-01 UTC start date. --until 2024-06-01 UTC end date. --alphas funding_reversion One or more strategy keys. --data-root data Parquet root in the parser's Hive layout. --mock off Use MockRawDataReader (synthetic data, no I/O). --metrics-roots — Precomputed metrics roots (bypass raw aggregation). --execution vwap vwap (next-bar VWAP fill) or close (instant, legacy). --no-plot off Skip the matplotlib dashboard.

Examples:

# Synthetic 1-week run, no plot
python tools/backtest.py --mock --since 2024-01-01 --until 2024-01-08 \
    --alphas funding_reversion --no-plot

# Real-data Q1 2025 with two strategies
python tools/backtest.py --since 2025-01-01 --until 2025-04-01 \
    --alphas funding_reversion trade_imbalance --data-root data

See tools/README.md for the full flag reference.

docs.title: Binance parser
docs.text:
cd binance_parser
python main.py {live,history}

docs.title: live
docs.text:
python main.py live [-h]
    [--market {spot,usdm,both}]
    [--symbols SYMBOLS …]
    [--order-book]
    [--with-funding]
Flag Default Meaning --market spot spot, usdm, or both. --symbols config.SYMBOLS Symbol list. --order-book off Maintain local L2 book + emit snapshots. --with-funding off (USD-M only) 8 h REST funding poll.

docs.title: history download
docs.text:
python main.py history download [-h]
    [--market {spot,usdm,both}]
    [--group {all,major}]
    [--symbols SYM …]
    [--types {klines,aggTrades,bookTicker} …]
    [--months N]
    [--intervals INTV …]
    [--workers N]
    [--dry-run] [-y]
Flag Default Meaning --market spot spot, usdm, or both. --group all all (601 pairs) or major (top 20). --symbols (unset) Manual list — overrides --group. --types HISTORY_DEFAULT_TYPES Which data types to download. --months HISTORY_DEFAULT_MONTHS How far back. --intervals HISTORY_KLINE_INTERVALS Kline intervals (e.g. 1m). --workers HISTORY_DOWNLOAD_WORKERS Parallel workers. --dry-run off Print plan + size; don't fetch. -y, --yes off Skip the size-confirmation prompt.

mkdocs serve                          # http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build                          # writes ./site/
mkdocs gh-deploy                      # publish to gh-pages

Requires mkdocs-material and pymdown-extensions — install with pip install 'mkdocs-material>=9.5' 'pymdown-extensions>=10'.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Domain terms used throughout the docs. Cross-references in bold.

docs.title: Alpha
docs.text: A signal that, when used as a portfolio weight, generates excess return. Each entry in ALPHA_REGISTRY is one alpha — see Strategies.

docs.title: Bar
docs.text: The base time unit of the engine — 30 minutes UTC-aligned by default. Lookbacks are expressed in bars (48*7 = one week). All strategies operate on bar-frequency DataFrames.

docs.title: Bar clock
docs.text: The async iterator (alpha_engine/live/bar_clock.py) that yields a timestamp at every UTC-aligned bar boundary plus a settlement delay. The live engine's step() runs once per yield.

docs.title: Bid / ask cost
docs.text: USD notional resting on one side of the book within some depth window. bid_25_cost_avg = bar-mean of $-volume of bids within 25% of mid. The base bid_25_cost is expanded into a 9-aggregate suffix pack — see Metrics catalogue.

docs.title: Box constraint
docs.text: A weight bound [min_strategy_weight, max_strategy_weight] enforced during the Markowitz solve. Implemented as water-filling — see Markowitz.

docs.title: Combined weights
docs.text: The output of Layer 3 — what would actually be traded. pipeline.combined_weights is (timestamps × tickers). Computed as \(\sum_k \alpha_{k,t} w_{k,t}\) where \(\alpha_k\) is the Markowitz allocation to strategy \(k\) and \(w_k\) is its per-ticker weight.

docs.title: Cost imbalance
docs.text: (bid_cost - ask_cost) / (bid_cost + ask_cost). Bounded [-1, 1]. Positive = bid-heavy; used by book_depth_imbalance.

docs.title: Drawdown
docs.text: Cumulative PnL minus the running max — always ≤ 0. Reported as max_drawdown in pipeline.summary(). Additive (fraction-of-notional), not percent.

docs.title: End range
docs.text: end_range parameter on AlphaStrategy. Top-N tickers by 30-day rolling USD volume that the strategy is allowed to weight. Default 50. Tickers outside the top-N are NaN'd in the strategy's output.

docs.title: Exchange data
docs.text: alpha_engine.metrics.metrics_dict.ExchangeData — top-level dict mapping exchange tag ("binance" / "binance-f") to a lazy AggregatedMetricsDict. The thing strategies receive as self.data.

docs.title: Funding rate
docs.text: USD-M perpetual futures pay periodic funding (every 8h on Binance). Positive funding ⇒ longs pay shorts. Stored as predicted_funding and realized_funding per bar.

docs.title: Gross / net PnL
docs.text:
• Gross — pure price PnL, ignoring fees and funding.
  • Net — gross minus fees plus funding. Closer to what you'd actually realise.

The gross.annualized_sharpe vs. net.annualized_sharpe gap tells you how much the cost model is eating.

docs.title: Hive partitioning
docs.text: Directory layout key1=value1/key2=value2/…/file.parquet that lets a reader prune by partition before opening any file. Used everywhere in data/. See Storage layout.

docs.title: Hypothesis
docs.text: The economic story behind an alpha — why it should make money. Each strategy's class docstring is one paragraph stating its hypothesis; fuller version in docs/strategies/<name>.md.

docs.title: Kyle's lambda
docs.text: A regression-slope measure of price impact per unit of order flow. Higher λ ⇒ smaller flows move the price more ⇒ less liquidity. Computed per bar in trades_aggregator.py.

docs.title: Lookback
docs.text: The rolling window length for a feature or for the Markowitz solve. Always in bars.

docs.title: Markowitz / Tobin tangency
docs.text: The closed-form max-Sharpe portfolio \(w^* = \Sigma^{-1}\mu / (\mathbf{1}^\top \Sigma^{-1}\mu)\). Used in Layer 3 to combine strategy "assets". See Markowitz.

docs.title: Mark price
docs.text: USD-M futures' fair-price index. Used for PnL and as a return proxy in strategies (because it's not influenced by venue-specific spreads). Spot has no mark price — close_price plays the role.

docs.title: MarketType
docs.text: Literal["spot", "usdm"] in binance_parser/models/market.py. Maps to the binance / binance-f exchange tags on the alpha-engine side.

docs.title: Metric
docs.text: A (timestamps × tickers) DataFrame that the data layer exposes via data["…"]["…"]. Names listed in Metrics catalogue.

docs.title: MultiFileParquetReader
docs.text: The RawDataReader that knows how to read the parser's Hive layout. Default reader for production backtests.

docs.title: Per-ticker cap
docs.text: max_w parameter on AlphaStrategy. Hard cap on |w_i| per ticker. Default 0.03. Enforced after normalize via trunc_normalize.

docs.title: Phase 1 / 2 / 3 / 4
docs.text: The live-trading roadmap stages — see Live trading. Phase 1 is signal-only and shipped today.

docs.title: Quantile (trade)
docs.text: A per-bar percentile threshold on trade size. buy_cost_quantile_0.95 = notional from buys above the 95th percentile of trade size in that bar. Used by trade_imbalance and vol_ob_entropy.

docs.title: Sharpe (annualised)
docs.text: (daily.mean() / daily.std()) * sqrt(365) where daily is bar-PnL resampled to daily. Computed per leg (gross / net).

docs.title: Strategy / alpha
docs.text: Used interchangeably. A class in alpha_engine/strategies/alphas.py that subclasses AlphaStrategy and is registered in ALPHA_REGISTRY.

docs.title: Tangency portfolio
docs.text: The point on the efficient frontier with the highest Sharpe ratio (assuming \(r_f = 0\)). Solved in closed form for the strategy combination.

docs.title: Tick
docs.text: A single market event — one trade, one diff, one kline-close. The parser's WebSocket consumer sees a continuous tick stream; the backtest never sees individual ticks (only the per-bar aggregates).

docs.title: Tick bus
docs.text: alpha_engine.live.tick_bus.LiveTickBus — in-process pub/sub that fans parser events out to multiple consumers (the live reader + the file writer + any custom sink).

docs.title: Turnover
docs.text: Sum of per-ticker |Δw| across the day, summed across tickers. Reported as mean_daily_turnover and median_daily_turnover in summary(). Multiply by fee_rate for an order-of-magnitude fee estimate.

docs.title: USD-M
docs.text: Binance's USD-margined perpetual futures venue (fapi.binance.com). Sometimes called "futures" in the codebase. Symbol notation: BTCUSDT (no slash). Funding rates and mark prices live here.

docs.title: Warm-start
docs.text: The first action of LiveRawDataReader.bootstrap_from(...) — read existing parquet under ./data/ to seed the rolling deques so the live engine can compute features from bar 1.

docs.title: Water-filling
docs.text: The active-set projection used to enforce box constraints on the tangency portfolio. Pin the worst violator, renormalise the free set along the unconstrained direction, repeat.

docs.title: Metrics catalogue
docs.text: Every key you can pass to data["{exchange}"]["{metric}"]. Generated from the *_METRICS registries in alpha_engine/metrics/*_aggregator.py.

docs.title: Klines (klines)
docs.text:
OHLCV data — exists for both spot and USD-M.

Metric Source close_price bar close open_price bar open high_price bar high low_price bar low volume base-asset volume volume_usd quote-asset volume (Binance's quote_volume)

Up to NSC-9 the klines aggregator also exposed mark_price / index_price as aliases of the bar close. They have moved to the markprice kind below — at stress moments the last trade and the real mark price diverge, and the alias was producing false signals.

docs.title: Mark price (markprice)
docs.text:
USD-M only. Sourced from the <symbol>@markPrice@1s WebSocket stream written to data/market=usdm/type=markprice/. The aggregator keeps the last-known value at every 30-min boundary.

Metric Meaning mark_price Real mark price (basis-aware, used for liquidations) index_price Underlying spot index used to compute mark price predicted_funding Predicted rate for the next 8h settlement next_funding_time_ms Settlement timestamp the predicted rate refers to

docs.title: Funding (funding)
docs.text:
USD-M only — realised settlement only. Predicted funding has moved to the markprice kind above.

Metric Meaning realized_funding Last realised settlement rate

docs.title: Trades (trades)
docs.text: Per-bar metrics computed from raw trade-tape ticks. Quantile thresholds q ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95} are evaluated per bar on the trade-size distribution. The threshold q is the per-bar percentile — buy_cost_quantile_0.95 sums the notional of buy trades whose own notional is at or above the 95th-percentile of the bar's buy-trade distribution (i.e. the top ~5% by size).

docs.title: Aggregates
docs.text: Metric Meaning volume Total base-asset volume in the bar buy_volume Volume from aggressor-buy trades sell_volume Volume from aggressor-sell trades buy_cost Notional ($) of aggressor-buy trades sell_cost Notional ($) of aggressor-sell trades buy_count Number of aggressor-buy trades sell_count Number of aggressor-sell trades vwap Volume-weighted average price buy_vwap VWAP across buy trades only sell_vwap VWAP across sell trades only open / close / high / low OHLC from trades (not the kline), averaged across buy/sell volatility Intra-bar std of minute log-returns (ddof=1, NaN if <3 non-empty minutes) hh Herfindahl index of trade-size concentration hh_buy Same, restricted to buys hh_sell Same, restricted to sells kyle_lambda Kyle's lambda (price impact regression slope on log-returns) max_buy_trade_cost Largest single buy trade ($) max_sell_trade_cost Largest single sell trade ($) asr_count Adverse-selection ratio by count (60s cross-bar lookahead) asr_volume Adverse-selection ratio by volume

docs.title: Count-above-threshold — T ∈ {100, 1000, 10000, 100000, 1000000}
docs.text:
For each USD threshold T:

Metric pattern Meaning buy_count_above_T Number of buy trades with notional strictly > T sell_count_above_T Same for sells

docs.title: Quantile metrics — q ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95}
docs.text:
For each q:

Metric pattern Meaning buy_cost_quantile_{q} USD notional sum from buys at or above the q-th percentile by notional sell_cost_quantile_{q} Same for sells buy_trade_cost_quantile_{q} The q-th percentile boundary itself (single value, USD) sell_trade_cost_quantile_{q} Same for sells buy_volume_quantile_{q}_usd Alias of buy_cost_quantile_{q} (v1-bridge) sell_volume_quantile_{q}_usd Same buy_volume_quantile_{q} Base-asset volume version sell_volume_quantile_{q} Same buy_count_quantile_{q} Number of buys above the q-th percentile sell_count_quantile_{q} Same volume_quantile_{q} / _usd Overall volume version (no side) count_quantile_{q} Overall count version (no side)

So data["binance-f"]["buy_cost_quantile_0.95"] is the per-bar USD spent by aggressor-buys whose own notional is at or above the 95th-percentile of the bar's buy distribution.

docs.title: Trades multilevel (trades_multilevel)
docs.text:
Per-bar metrics computed on logical trades — chains of contiguous raw fills that share side, timestamp, and consecutive trade_ids with monotonic price. Suffix _ml = multilevel (chain length ≥ 2), _sl = single-level (chain length = 1).

Quantile threshold q ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95}. 73 keys total.

Metric pattern Meaning {buy,sell}_count_{ml,sl} Chain counts per side {buy,sell}_cost_{ml,sl} Chain notional totals mean_cost_{ml,sl} Mean cost per chain (overall) {buy,sell}_vwap_{ml,sl} VWAP across chains, per side {buy,sell}_cost_quantile_{q}_{ml,sl} Top-q sums of chain notionals {buy,sell}_trade_cost_quantile_{q}_{ml,sl} q-th percentile boundary {buy,sell}_mean_price_delta_ml_quantile_{q} Mean (price_last − price_first) / price_first × side_sign for chains above q, ml only

Identity invariant (pinned by tests): buy_cost == buy_cost_ml + buy_cost_sl.

docs.title: Orderbook (orderbook)
docs.text: Snapshot-based, multi-aggregated across the bar's snapshots. Depth percentages d ∈ {0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100} are percent-of-mid — bid_25_cost_avg is the bar-mean of bid liquidity within 25% of the running mid. Underscores in metric names come from str.replace(".", "_"), so 0.5 becomes 0_5.

docs.title: Aggregation suffix packs
docs.text:
Each per-snapshot base metric is expanded into one of two packs:

  • 9-agg pack (_avg, _quantile_25, _quantile_50, _quantile_75, _quantile_90, _quantile_95, _skew, _min, _max): drops NaN samples only. Used for level / state metrics.
  • 10-agg pack (= 9-agg + _sum): additionally drops zero samples. Used for cross-snapshot diff / log-return metrics where 0 means "no observation".

docs.title: Best level (9-agg)
docs.text: Base metric Pack best_bid_price 9-agg best_ask_price 9-agg best_bid_size 9-agg best_ask_size 9-agg bid_ask_spread_abs 9-agg — absolute spread best_ask − best_bid bid_ask_spread_rel 9-agg — relative spread spread / mid last_best_bid_price last snapshot in the bar (scalar) last_best_ask_price last snapshot in the bar (scalar)

docs.title: Per-depth metrics (9-agg)
docs.text:
For each depth d, side s ∈ {bid, ask}:

Base metric Meaning {s}_{d}_cost USD notional within d% of mid on side s {s}_{d}_size Base-asset size within d% of mid {s}_{d}_vwap VWAP of liquidity within d% {s}_{d}_levels_size_count Number of populated levels within d% {s}_{d}_levels_size_count_nonzero Count of levels with size > 0 {s}_{d}_levels_size_mean Mean size per level within d% cost_imbalance_{d}_ratio (bid_cost − ask_cost) / (bid_cost + ask_cost) cost_imbalance_{d}_norm Normalised variant: 1.0 if ask_cost = 0, NaN if both = 0 vwap_{d}_midprice (bid_vwap + ask_vwap) / 2 per snapshot

docs.title: Cross-snapshot diff / log-return (10-agg)
docs.text: Base metric Meaning {s}_{d}_cost_diff Δ cost vs. previous snapshot {s}_{d}_size_diff Δ size vs. previous snapshot {s}_{d}_price_logreturn log-return of cumulative VWAP best_{s}_size_diff Δ best-level size best_{s}_price_logreturn log-return of best price

docs.title: Liquidity-shock — d ∈ {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 5, 25, 50} (9-agg)
docs.text:
liq_shock_{side}_{d} = {side}_{d}_size[t] / rolling_mean(10s of {side}_{d}_size).

Base metric Meaning liq_shock_bid_{d} Bid-side instantaneous liquidity vs 10s baseline liq_shock_ask_{d} Ask-side liq vs baseline liq_shock_ratio_{d} liq_shock_bid / (liq_shock_bid + liq_shock_ask)

docs.title: Liquidations (liquidations)
docs.text:
Per-bar metrics on liquidation fills, prefixed liquidations_. Reader maps cum_filled_qty → size, avg_price → price (per fill, not the order intent), then filters size > 0. Same algorithmic template as trades — 50 keys total. Examples:

Metric Meaning liquidations_{buy,sell}_count Count of long/short liquidations liquidations_{buy,sell}_count_above_{T} T ∈ liquidations_{buy,sell}_cost Notional sums liquidations_{buy,sell}_cost_quantile_{q} q ∈ liquidations_max_{buy,sell}_trade_cost Largest single liquidation ($) liquidations_vwap, _buy_vwap, _sell_vwap VWAPs liquidations_open/high/low/close OHLC, NaN if either side empty liquidations_volatility Intra-bar minute log-return std liquidations_hh, _hh_buy, _hh_sell HH on size (per L_T2.8) liquidations_kyle_lambda Kyle's lambda liquidations_asr_count, _asr_volume 60s cross-bar lookahead

docs.title: Maker orders (maker_orders)
docs.text:
Spot-only (Binance spot). Each raw trade reconstructs to one maker_fill with the maker side inverted from taker: taker BUY → maker ASK, taker SELL → maker BID. ASR sign convention is inverted vs. taker (ask-maker "wins" when price falls).

Prefix maker_ everywhere — deliberate deviation from generic bid_*/ask_* to avoid namespace collision with orderbook. 50 keys with the same structural template as trades/liquidations. Examples:

Metric Meaning maker_{ask,bid}_count Maker fills counted on each side maker_{ask,bid}_count_above_{T} T ∈ maker_{ask,bid}_cost_quantile_{q} q ∈ maker_max_{ask,bid}_trade_cost Largest single maker fill ($) maker_vwap, maker_ask_vwap, maker_bid_vwap Maker-side VWAPs maker_volatility, maker_kyle_lambda Identical algos to taker template maker_asr_count, maker_asr_volume 60s lookahead, sign inverted

Identity invariants (pinned): maker_ask_cost == buy_cost, maker_bid_cost == sell_cost, maker_vwap == vwap.

docs.title: Market stats (market_stats)
docs.text:
USD-M only. Polled via REST (Binance futures + spot margin endpoints), not WebSocket. Futures coroutine runs at 5-min UTC-aligned cadence; spot interest at 1h cadence. Aggregator does resample("30min").last() .ffill().reindex(idx).ffill().

Metric Source endpoint open_interest /fapi/v1/openInterest global_long_accounts /futures/data/globalLongShortAccountRatio top_long_accounts /futures/data/topLongShortAccountRatio top_long_positions /futures/data/topLongShortPositionRatio daily_interest_rate /sapi/v1/margin/next-hourly-interest-rate × 24 (linear, no compounding). Gated MARGIN_INTEREST_ENABLED, opt-in.

docs.title: How resolution works
docs.text:
The lazy dict (AggregatedMetricsDict) maps a metric name to an aggregator group via prefix rules in metrics_dict._resolve_source:

Prefix / pattern Group liquidations_* liquidations maker_* maker_orders {open_interest, global_long_*, top_long_*, daily_interest_rate} market_stats *_ml / *_sl / mean_cost_{ml,sl} / *_mean_price_delta_ml_* trades_multilevel bid_* or ask_* containing cost / size / vwap / levels / spread / logreturn orderbook cost_imbalance_*, vwap_*_midprice, liq_shock_*, last_best_* orderbook buy_* or sell_* trades close_price, volume_usd, … klines mark_price, index_price, next_funding_time_ms, predicted_funding markprice anything else containing funding funding

Names that don't match raise KeyError — the dict refuses to guess. To add a new metric whose name doesn't fit, also add a branch in _resolve_source.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Lightweight building blocks in alpha_engine/operators.py. Use these in gen_weights_raw — they handle the NaN / divide-by-zero cases that bite on real data.

from alpha_engine.operators import (
    rank, normalize, trunc_normalize, norm_ratio,
    ts_return, ts_logreturn, ts_ema, ts_std, ts_zscore,
    set_entropy, set_mean,
)

docs.title: rank(df) → df
docs.text:
Per-row percentile rank in [0, 1]. Implemented as df.rank(axis=1, pct=True). NaN rows stay NaN.

rank(pd.DataFrame([[1, 2, 3, 4]])).values
# array([[0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00]])

docs.title: normalize(df) → df
docs.text:
Per-row demean, then scale so |w|.sum() == 1.

df  := df - df.mean(axis=1)
df  := df / df.abs().sum(axis=1).replace(0, NaN)

A row of all-equal values goes to all-zeros (after demean) → divide-by- zero is replaced with NaN, the row stays NaN.

docs.title: trunc_normalize(df, max_w) → df
docs.text:
normalize, then clip(-max_w, max_w). Does not re-normalise after the clip — by design. The base strategy class uses this to enforce a per-ticker cap; the resulting weights are no longer exactly abs-sum-1 but the cap is hard.

If you'd rather re-normalise (preserve abs-sum-1, sacrifice the cap), do normalize(trunc_normalize(df, max_w)).

docs.title: norm_ratio(a, b) → df
docs.text:
(a - b) / (a + b). Bounded in [-1, 1] for non-negative inputs. NaN where a + b == 0.

The de-facto "imbalance" operator — used in book_depth_imbalance, trade_imbalance, vol_ob_entropy.

docs.title: set_entropy(*dfs) → df
docs.text:
Shannon-like entropy across a set of DataFrames, treating each one as a share after normalisation:

total := Σ |df_k|
p_k   := |df_k| / total
H     := -Σ p_k · log(p_k)

NaN entries (zero share) are skipped — entropy is computed only over non-zero shares. Result is filled with 0 where the entire row was NaN.

Used in vol_ob_entropy to measure concentration of trade-volume across quantile bins vs. concentration of book depth across bid/ask.

docs.title: set_mean(*dfs) → df
docs.text: Element-wise NaN-aware mean across a set of DataFrames. Same shape; preserves index/columns.

docs.title: Time-series
docs.text: All time-series ops use min_periods=1 so they don't produce a full NaN warmup — they grow into their window.

docs.title: ts_return(df, periods=1) → df
docs.text: Simple return: df.pct_change(periods).

docs.title: ts_logreturn(df, periods=1) → df
docs.text: log(df / df.shift(periods)). Same warmup as ts_return.

docs.title: ts_ema(df, span) → df
docs.text: Exponential moving average: df.ewm(span=span, min_periods=1).mean(). The span / decay convention is pandas' standard (alpha = 2/(span+1)).

docs.title: ts_std(df, window) → df
docs.text: Rolling standard deviation: df.rolling(window, min_periods=1).std(). The first row is NaN (std of a single point is undefined).

docs.title: ts_zscore(df, window) → df
docs.text:
Rolling z-score:

mean := df.rolling(window, min_periods=1).mean()
std  := df.rolling(window, min_periods=1).std().replace(0, NaN)
z    := (df - mean) / std

std == 0 (e.g. constant window) → NaN, not Inf.

The standard "normalise across recent history" tool. Z-score before EMA is a common pattern across the strategy registry.

docs.title: When to use which
docs.text: You want… Use… A bounded [-1, 1] signal from two non-negative series norm_ratio A bounded [0, 1] signal from raw values across the universe rank To turn a raw signal into dollar-neutral weights normalize (then trunc_normalize for the cap) To measure concentration / dispersion across quantile bins set_entropy To smooth a signal ts_ema (span = how many bars of "memory") To remove level / drift from a metric ts_zscore (window = "what counts as recent") To compute returns ts_return (or ts_logreturn if you'll sum across time) Rolling vol ts_std(ts_return(price, 1), window)

docs.title: NSC-14 backfill — aggTrade vs trade trade-off table (NSC-42)
docs.text:
NSC-14 (PR #15, commit 1c95f7a) switched the canonical trade source to @aggTrade-only and stopped subscribing to raw @trade. The decision was sound but the research phase was skipped — there was no side-by-side numbers table comparing the three options. This page is the post-hoc backfill so the choice is reproducible from numbers, not just narrative.

Status: the choice is merged and not under reconsideration. This doc exists for auditability.

docs.title: The three options
docs.text:
• Option A — aggTrades-only (chosen). Subscribe only to @aggTrade, treat type=aggtrades (live) and type=aggTrades (historical archive) as the single canonical kind="trades" source.
  • Option B — raw trades-only. Subscribe only to @trade, store type=trades only. Historical parity requires re-aggregating from the aggTrades archive (the archive does not ship raw trades).
  • Option C — both, dedup downstream. Subscribe to both streams, write both partition types, and add a deduplication step in the reader so each fill is counted exactly once.

docs.title: Measured numbers — 5-min capture, BTCUSDT + ETHUSDT, spot
docs.text:
Synthetic data

Numbers below are SYNTHETIC — generated through the real binance_parser DTOs and FileWriter because the egress proxy blocks Binance hosts. See How the numbers were collected for the full disclosure and reproducer.

symbol type files size (MB) rows $ volume BTCUSDT trades 1 0.1134 9,000 8,966,001 BTCUSDT aggtrades 1 0.0495 2,571 8,966,001 ETHUSDT trades 1 0.0667 5,400 4,181,993 ETHUSDT aggtrades 1 0.0349 1,800 4,181,993

Per-symbol compression (raw vs aggregated, same window):

  • BTCUSDT — 3.50× fewer rows, 2.29× smaller on-disk after zstd-3.
  • ETHUSDT — 3.00× fewer rows, 1.91× smaller on-disk after zstd-3.

Dollar volume sums are identical to the dollar by construction — aggTrade preserves total executed notional, it only collapses same-side same-price fills inside a 100 ms bucket on Binance's side.

docs.title: How the numbers were collected
docs.text:
Live capture was attempted via the parser's WebSocket path (binance_parser/main.py live --market spot --symbols BTCUSDT ETHUSDT with LIVE_PREFER_AGGTRADES=False patched in for the run) and the historical archive (history download … --types aggTrades trades). Both routes failed inside the worktree's network: the egress proxy returned 403 host_not_allowed for data.binance.vision, api.binance.com, and stream.binance.com:9443. No pre-existing parquet partitions are checked into the repo.

Because a real 5-minute capture was infeasible, the rows above were generated by a synthetic driver (/tmp/synth_nsc42.py) that:

  1. Constructs Trade and AggTrade DTOs from binance_parser/models/events.py directly — same dataclass, same pa.Schema, same to_rows() shape.
  2. Pushes them through the real live.writer.FileWriter, so on-disk layout, parquet writer settings, and zstd-3 compression match the live path byte-for-byte (PARQUET_COMPRESSION = "zstd", PARQUET_COMPRESSION_LEVEL = 3).
  3. Calibrates per-symbol rates from publicly-cited 2024 BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT spot activity: BTCUSDT ≈ 30 raw trades/s, ETHUSDT ≈ 18 raw trades/s, aggregation factors 3.5× / 3.0× respectively (well within the 2–5× range Binance publishes).

The output was measured with pyarrow.dataset.dataset(...).to_table(...) summing price * qty and os.stat().st_size over the partition files.

Caveats that matter for an audit reviewer:

  • File-size figures are realistic relative to each other (same writer, same compression) but absolute numbers will differ from a real Binance capture by whatever the synthetic price/qty distribution misses (zstd compresses repeated prices and timestamps very well — real BTCUSDT bursts have higher repetition and would compress more, so the aggTrade size advantage is, if anything, understated here).
  • Aggregation ratios are deterministic in the synthetic data; in production they vary minute-to-minute (3–5× is normal, can spike to

    10× during quiet periods or drop near 1× during one-sided cascades).

  • Dollar-volume parity between trades and aggTrades is exact in the synthetic capture (the aggregator preserves Σ price·qty); on the live feed it is also exact up to float32 rounding — @aggTrade is a lossless bucketing on Binance's side.

docs.title: What the numbers say
docs.text:
• Storage — Option A is ~2.0–2.3× cheaper on disk than Option B and ~3.0–3.5× cheaper than Option C, at the same dollar volume. For 601 symbols × 30 days the difference compounds to multi-GB savings.
  • Schema parity — Option A is the only one with native archive parity: data.binance.vision ships aggTrades shards but no raw-trade shards for spot daily, so backtest and live read the same bucketing of fills with no re-aggregation step.
  • Information loss — Option A loses per-fill granularity (queue position, microstructure-level trade-id sequencing). For the alpha set in ALPHA_REGISTRY today (trade_imbalance and friends operating on 30-min bars) that loss is invisible — the aggregator preserves signed notional and signed count by side. For future microstructure-level work the reader can be flipped back to Option C via LIVE_PREFER_AGGTRADES=False.
  • Operational risk — Option C requires a dedup step on every read; a bug there silently double-counts notional and fakes higher signal strength. Option A has no such failure mode.

docs.title: Conclusion (post-hoc)
docs.text: Option A is the right choice given the current alpha set: it is cheaper to store, has clean archive parity, and removes a class of dedup bugs. The information lost is recoverable on demand — set LIVE_PREFER_AGGTRADES=False to re-enable raw @trade capture for any future microstructure work (type=trades partitions still write through the same FileWriter; the alpha engine reader still ignores them to avoid double-counting).

docs.title: Reproducing
docs.text:
To re-run on a host with Binance egress, use the parser's own CLI for a fresh 5-min sample with both streams subscribed:

# Temporarily flip the canonical trade switch so both partitions get written.
export LIVE_PREFER_AGGTRADES=False    # not yet env-driven; for now patch
                                      # binance_parser/config/settings.py:72
cd binance_parser
timeout 300 python main.py live --market spot --symbols BTCUSDT ETHUSDT

Then point the measurement script at the resulting binance_parser/data/ tree:

import pyarrow.dataset as ds
from pathlib import Path

DATA = Path("binance_parser/data/market=spot")
for typ in ("trades", "aggtrades"):
    for sym in ("BTCUSDT", "ETHUSDT"):
        files = list((DATA / f"type={typ}").rglob(f"symbol={sym}/*.parquet"))
        size_mb = sum(p.stat().st_size for p in files) / (1024**2)
        t = ds.dataset([str(p) for p in files], format="parquet").to_table(
            columns=["price", "qty"]
        )
        rows = t.num_rows
        dvol = float((t["price"].to_numpy() * t["qty"].to_numpy()).sum())
        print(f"{sym:8s} {typ:10s} {len(files):3d} files  {size_mb:8.4f} MB  "
              f"{rows:>10,} rows  ${dvol:>16,.0f}")

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text: One file per alpha. Each describes the steady-state design — hypothesis, signal, data inputs, parameters. Measured numbers (Sharpe, drawdown, turnover) live in the Research log, tagged with a date and data range.

docs.title: Index
docs.text: File ALPHA_REGISTRY key Hypothesis Primary data Orderbook mispricing ob_mispricing Limit-order book lags last trade price → momentum continues Spot L2 + futures mark Volume / OB entropy vol_ob_entropy Concentrated trade flow vs. symmetric book = informed flow Futures L2 + trade-size quantiles Funding mean reversion funding_reversion Extreme funding rates revert USD-M funding Trade imbalance trade_imbalance Big buys vs. big sells (top quantile) is informative Futures large-trade volume Volatility mean reversion vol_mean_reversion Low-vol regimes break out in the direction of recent drift Futures mark price Book depth imbalance book_depth_imbalance Asymmetric book depth at 25% predicts drift Futures L2 cost @ 25%

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• One strategy = one file. Filename matches the strategy's name in ALPHA_REGISTRY (e.g. funding_reversion.md).
  • Code-derived sections (signal formula, parameters) should match the current alpha_engine/strategies/alphas.py. If you change the code, update the doc in the same commit.
  • Numbers (Sharpe, drawdown, turnover) belong in research-log.md with a date and the commit / data range they were measured against — not in the per-strategy file, which describes the steady-state design.

docs.title: File template
docs.text:
Every per-strategy file follows the same shape:

# <Display name> (`<registry_key>`)

## Hypothesis
## Signal
## Data inputs
## Parameters
## Caveats / known weaknesses

Adding a new strategy: copy funding_reversion.md, fill the sections, add a row to the table above, register the class in ALPHA_REGISTRY. Walk-through: Writing a strategy.

docs.title: Hypothesis
docs.text: When bid depth at 25% is much larger than ask depth, there's a "wall" of support. Price is less likely to crash and more likely to drift up. The book shows where passive capital is positioned.

docs.title: Signal
docs.text:
raw     = norm_ratio(bid_25_cost_avg, ask_25_cost_avg)
signal  = ts_zscore(raw, window=48*7)             # 7-day z-score
weights = ts_ema(signal, span=48*3)               # 3-day EMA

docs.title: Data inputs
docs.text: Source Field USD-M bid_25_cost_avg (bar-mean of notional resting on the bid within 25% of mid) USD-M ask_25_cost_avg

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• Book depth: 25% of mid (cost-integrated).
  • z-score window: 48 * 7.
  • EMA span: 48 * 3.

docs.title: Caveats / known weaknesses
docs.text:
• Layered / spoofed orders inflate visible depth without representing real intent — the book can lie.
  • 25% is a wide band; sensitivity vs. tighter (e.g. 5% / 10%) bands hasn't been logged here.
  • Strongly correlated with ob_mispricing — Markowitz combination should diversify them away, but watch the strategy correlation matrix.
  • From research doc: imbalance decay, layering filter.
