docs.title: Hypothesis
docs.text: Extreme funding rates revert. When funding is very positive, longs are paying shorts heavily — the market is overleveraged long, and price tends to drop. Vice versa for very negative funding.

docs.title: Signal
docs.text:
signal  = -ts_zscore(predicted_funding, window=48*14)   # 14-day z-score
weights = ts_ema(signal, span=48*3)                     # 3-day EMA

The z-score normalises across the per-ticker funding distribution; the negative sign turns "expensive to be long" into a short.

docs.title: Data inputs
docs.text:
Source Field USD-M predicted_funding

Realised funding is also consumed by the PnL leg (compute_pnl(funding=...)) — see ../methodology.md.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• z-score window: 48 * 14 (two weeks of 30-min bars).
  • EMA span: 48 * 3 (three days).

docs.title: Caveats / known weaknesses
docs.text:
• Funding settles every 8h — at the bar level the predicted-funding series steps rather than evolves smoothly. The 3-day EMA is the main smoother.
  • "Extreme" is defined by the rolling 2-week distribution per ticker; regime shifts (BTC funding regime in bull vs. flat market) can mute the signal.
  • From research doc: regime sensitivity, funding-reversion vs. carry.

docs.title: Hypothesis
docs.text: Limit-order traders in the book are slower than the market. When the volume-weighted mid-price in the book lags behind the last trade price, the book hasn't caught up yet — price will continue in the same direction.

docs.title: Signal
docs.text:
ob_mid = (bid_25_vwap_avg + ask_25_vwap_avg) / 2  # spot, bar-mean of per-snapshot VWAPs
signal = -(ob_mid / mark_price)                   # futures mark
weights = ts_ema(signal, span=48*5)               # 5-day EMA

Negative sign: "book is behind, momentum will continue".

docs.title: Data inputs
docs.text:
Source Field Spot bid_25_vwap_avg, ask_25_vwap_avg (bar-mean of book VWAP at 25% depth) USD-M mark_price

Cross-venue: spot book vs. futures mark. Requires both feeds in MetricsDict.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• EMA span: 48 * 5 (5 days of 30-min bars).
  • Per-ticker cap max_w = 0.03, top-end_range = 50 by volume.

docs.title: Caveats / known weaknesses
docs.text:
• Spot book ≠ futures execution venue: basis moves (cash-and-carry, funding) bleed into the signal as noise.
  • 25% depth VWAP can be thin for small-cap pairs.
  • From research doc: validate on rolling windows.

docs.text: To be filled in from the Google Doc.

docs.title: Hypothesis
docs.text: Buy/sell imbalance in large trades (top quantile) is informative — big buyers know something. Small trades are noise.

docs.title: Signal
docs.text:
big_buy  = buy_cost_quantile_0.95
big_sell = sell_cost_quantile_0.95

raw     = norm_ratio(big_buy, big_sell)
signal  = ts_zscore(raw, window=48*5)             # 5-day z-score
weights = ts_ema(signal, span=48*3)               # 3-day EMA

Positive ⇒ more large buys than sells ⇒ go long.

docs.title: Data inputs
docs.text: Source Field USD-M buy_cost_quantile_0.95 (notional traded by aggressors above the 95th-percentile size) USD-M sell_cost_quantile_0.95

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• Quantile threshold: 0.95.
  • z-score window: 48 * 5.
  • EMA span: 48 * 3.

docs.title: Caveats / known weaknesses
docs.text:
• "Large" is per-ticker percentile, not absolute USD — small caps with low absolute volume still produce a signal.
  • The 95th-percentile cutoff is arbitrary; sensitivity vs. 0.99 / 0.90 has not been logged here.
  • Aggressor-side classification depends on the parser's trade-tape sign (buyer vs. seller maker flag).
  • From research doc: quantile sweep + decay analysis.

docs.title: From research doc
docs.text: To be filled in from the Google Doc.

docs.title: Hypothesis
docs.text: Coins that had unusually low realised volatility recently will revert to normal vol, and the direction of the breakout is predicted by the sign of recent returns (continuation, not reversion, on direction). Low vol + positive drift ⇒ go long.

docs.title: Signal
docs.text:
ret = ts_return(mark_price, 48)                       # 1-day return
vol = ts_std(ts_return(mark_price, 1), window=48*14)  # 14-day rolling vol

signal  = -(rank(vol) - 0.5) * sign(ret)
weights = ts_ema(signal, span=48*5)                   # 5-day EMA

rank(vol) - 0.5 is centred in [-0.5, 0.5]; the leading minus inverts it so low-rank vol (quiet coins) gets weight, and sign(ret) picks the direction.

docs.title: Data inputs
docs.text:
Source Field USD-M mark_price

Single-input strategy — no book / trade-tape dependency.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• Return horizon: 48 bars (1 day).
  • Vol window: 48 * 14 (14 days).
  • EMA span: 48 * 5.

docs.title: Caveats / known weaknesses
docs.text:
• "Vol rank" is cross-sectional at each bar — needs a meaningful universe size (end_range = 50 by default).
  • Continuation on direction during low-vol is the empirical claim; in ranging markets the sign of the recent return is noise and the alpha degenerates to a vol-bet only.
  • From research doc: separate the "low-vol selection" effect from the "direction" effect.

docs.title: Hypothesis
docs.text: When large trades are concentrated (low entropy in trade-size distribution) but the orderbook is symmetric (high entropy in bid/ask balance), informed traders are hiding in the flow. Divergence between trade entropy and book entropy predicts direction.

docs.title: Signal
docs.text:
volume_entropy    = mean over q ∈ {0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95}:
                       set_entropy(buy_volume_q, sell_volume_q)
orderbook_entropy = mean over depth ∈ {10%, 25%}:
                       set_entropy(bid_cost_avg, ask_cost_avg)

raw     = norm_ratio(volume_entropy, orderbook_entropy)
signal  = ts_zscore(raw, window=48*7)             # 7-day z-score
weights = ts_ema(signal, span=48*7)               # 7-day EMA

docs.title: Data inputs
docs.text: Source Field USD-M buy_volume_quantile_{0.5,0.75,0.9,0.95}_usd USD-M sell_volume_quantile_{0.5,0.75,0.9,0.95}_usd USD-M bid_{10,25}_cost_avg, ask_{10,25}_cost_avg

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• Trade-size quantiles: {0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95}.
  • Book depth percentages: {10%, 25%}.
  • z-score window: 48 * 7.
  • EMA span: 48 * 7.

docs.title: Caveats / known weaknesses
docs.text:
• Heavily parameterised — risk of overfitting the quantile / depth grid.
  • set_entropy on small samples is noisy; quantile bins must have non-trivial volume.
  • From research doc: stability of the entropy ratio under thin liquidity.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: • G1 (trades-v2): top quantile shifted from 0.99 → 0.95. The canonical trade-quantile grid in trades_aggregator.py no longer emits a 0.99 boundary (current set: {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95}). Effect on this signal: the largest-trade tail now covers top ~5% instead of top ~1%, so set_entropy weighs broader concentration. No live A/B has been logged yet — treat as semantic drift relative to historical backtests.
